3/10★ Must-learnYes Bank reconstruction (March 2020)

  • 5 Mar 2020 → Centre placed Yes Bank under moratorium (RBI request) until 3 Apr; withdrawals capped at ₹50,000 per depositor; RBI superseded the board and appointed Prashant Kumar (ex-SBI CFO) as administrator
  • 6 Mar 2020 → RBI released the draft Yes Bank Ltd. Reconstruction Scheme, 2020
  • 13 Mar 2020 → Cabinet approved; scheme came into force the same day
  • SBI as investor bank → up to 49%, invested ₹7,250 crore (725 crore shares at ₹10); lock-in of 3 years, cannot fall below 26% within that time; other lenders (ICICI, HDFC, Axis, Kotak, Bandhan) joined
  • Moratorium lifted at 6 pm on 18 Mar 2020; Prashant Kumar became MD and CEO
Mnemonic

"5-6-13-18 March": moratorium, draft, scheme, lifted. "49-26-3".

Exam angle

What was the withdrawal cap, SBI's stake and the lock-in?

8.3 Tax and disinvestment

4/10★ Must-learnCorporate tax cut of Sep 2019

In plain words

In 2019 the Government cut the corporate tax rate to revive growth; this card gives the new rate and the legal provision.

  • Taxation Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 20 Sep 2019 (later an Act) → announced by the Finance Minister to revive growth
  • Section 115BAA → option for domestic companies: 22% base (effective 25.17% with 10% surcharge and 4% cess); no exemptions; no MAT
  • Section 115BAB → 15% (effective 17.16%) for new manufacturing companies incorporated on or after 1 Oct 2019 and starting production before 31 Mar 2023
  • MAT for others cut from 18.5% to 15% | estimated revenue loss about ₹1.45 lakh crore
Memory tricks

"22 and 15; 25.17 and 17.16".

5/10★ Must-learnLIC IPO (May 2022)

In plain words

LIC's IPO in May 2022 was India's largest at that time; this card gives the dates, the price and the stake sold.

  • Subscription 4–9 May 2022 | listed on BSE and NSE 17 May 2022 | price band ₹902–949 (issue price ₹949)
  • Offer for sale of about 3.5% stake (22.13 crore shares), cut from the planned 5% | raised ₹20,557 crore (issue size ₹21,008 crore before discounts) → largest IPO in India at the time, ahead of Paytm (₹18,300 crore, Nov 2021)
  • Run by DIPAM (Department of Investment and Public Asset Management); Secretary then: Tuhin Kanta Pandey
  • LIC was formed 1956 by merging 245 private insurers (LIC Act 1956)
Memory tricks

"4-9 May, list 17 May, 3.5%".

8.4 India on the world stage

6/10★ Must-learnG20 Presidency, BRICS expansion and space

In plain words

India held the G20 Presidency in 2023, and BRICS expanded; the card gives the dates, themes and key facts.

  • India's G20 Presidency → 1 Dec 2022 to 30 Nov 2023 | 18th Summit, 9–10 Sep 2023, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi | theme "One Earth, One Family, One Future" (Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam)
  • Outcomes → New Delhi Leaders' Declaration adopted by consensus; African Union made a permanent member (21st member, 9 Sep 2023); Global Biofuels Alliance launched
  • BRICS expansion → decided at the Johannesburg Summit (Aug 2023); Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, UAE joined from 1 Jan 2024; Indonesia joined Jan 2025 (11 members); partner-country category created at Kazan (Oct 2024)
  • Chandrayaan-3 → launched 14 Jul 2023; Vikram lander touched down near the lunar south pole on 23 Aug 2023 (India: 4th country to soft-land on the Moon, first near the south pole); Chandrayaan-2 (2019) failed at landing
  • Aditya-L1 → solar mission launched 2 Sep 2023
Memory tricks

G20 "1 Dec 22 → 9-10 Sep 23, AU = 21st". Chandrayaan: launch 14 July, land 23 August.

9.3 Indices and look-alikes

7/10☆ Good to knowBase years of key indices

IndexBase yearNote
CPI (new series)2024Replaced base 2012; first used for January 2026 data (released Feb 2026); basket items 299 → 358 (goods 259 → 308, services 40 → 50); 12 divisions; weights from the 2023-24 Household Consumption Expenditure Survey; food weight 45.86% → 36.75%
GDP / National Accounts2022-23Replaced 2011-12; new series published 27 Feb 2026
IIP (Index of Industrial Production)2022-23Replaced 2011-12; first release 1 Jun 2026 (April 2026 data, 4.9%); 1,042 products mapped to 463 item groups; 120 groups added and 64 dropped (e.g. kerosene, CFLs); quick estimates on the 28th
WPI (Wholesale Price Index)2022-23Replaced 2011-12; first release 15 Jun 2026 (May 2026 data); basket 697 → 957 items; weights: primary articles 22.76%, fuel and power 14.11%, manufactured products 63.13%; released by DPIIT with new Producer Price Indices (PPI); WPI to run for five years
Index of Core Industries (ICI)2022-23Replaced 2011-12; first release 20 Jul 2026 (June 2026 data); nine industries now (Iron Ore added to the earlier eight); top weights: electricity 30.93, refinery products 22.57, steel 17.58
Sensex1978-79 = 100Launched 1986
Nifty 503 Nov 1995 = 1000Launched 22 Apr 1996

Why it exists

  • Annual factory surveys report structural data with substantial time lags unsuitable for immediate monetary and business cycle monitoring.
  • A monthly volume index tracks real industrial activity trends and signals near-term economic performance quickly.

How it works

  • Statistical authorities collect monthly physical production volume reports from designated industrial enterprises across product baskets.
  • Physical outputs are indexed against historical base year volumes and weighted by sectoral gross value added contributions.
  • The composite index is released monthly to evaluate industrial growth across mining, manufacturing, and utility sectors.

More fixed facts

  • Index of Eight Core Industries Feb 2026: +2.3% (Jan +4%); core weight in IIP 40.27%; base 2011-12
  • New IIP basket: 1,042 products in 463 item groups; NIC-2025; adds minor minerals, rare earth minerals, gas supply, water supply, sewerage and waste; separate indices for renewable and non-renewable electricity; released with 28 days' lag

How it changed

  • June 2026: IIP base year 2011-12 → 2022-23; new series from 1 June 2026; TAC chaired by Dr Mridul K. Saggar (IIM Kozhikode)

Traps

  • The index evaluates physical volume of output produced rather than nominal rupee value or turnover.
  • Manufacturing carries the predominant weighting in the basket compared to mining and electric power utilities.

In the news

  • Oct 2026: IIP growth for August 2026
  • Jun 2026: New IIP series (base 2022-23) launched
  • Feb 2026: TAC on IIP base year revision submits report

10.1 Constitution, polity and amendments

  1. Which amendment changed the Preamble and what did it add?
    Show answer

    42nd Amendment, 1976: Socialist, Secular, Integrity.

  2. Original vs current count of Articles, Parts and Schedules?
    Show answer

    395, 22, 8 → about 448, 25 (Part VII repealed), 12.

  3. Which Articles form Part III, and what is the ladder of the six rights?
    Show answer

    Arts 12–35; Equality 14–18, Freedom 19–22, Exploitation 23–24, Religion 25–28, Cultural-Educational 29–30, Remedies 32 (5-4-2-4-2-1).

  4. Which writ for illegal detention, quashing an order, and challenging the right to hold office?
    Show answer

    Habeas Corpus; Certiorari; Quo Warranto.

  5. Art 32 vs Art 226?
    Show answer

    Art 32: Supreme Court, Fundamental Rights only. Art 226: High Courts, FRs and other legal rights.

  6. Which Articles did the 42nd Amendment add to the DPSP?
    Show answer

    39A (free legal aid), 43A (workers in management), 48A (environment).

  7. How many Fundamental Duties, and which amendments?
    Show answer

    11: ten by the 42nd (1976), the 11th by the 86th (2002).

  8. What are the committee sizes: PAC, COPU, Estimates?
    Show answer

    PAC 22 (15 LS + 7 RS); COPU 22; Estimates 30 (Lok Sabha only).

  9. What is the quorum, and which Article provides a joint sitting?
    Show answer

    One-tenth of members (Art 100); joint sitting Art 108, presided by the Speaker.

  10. Which Articles, Parts and Schedules do the 73rd, 74th and 97th Amendments relate to?
    Show answer

    73rd: Part IX, 11th Schedule (29 subjects). 74th: Part IXA, 12th Schedule (18). 97th: Part IXB (cooperatives).

  11. Which Articles cover National Emergency, President's Rule and Financial Emergency?
    Show answer

    352, 356, 360 (financial never used).

  12. What majority is needed for most amendments?
    Show answer

    Majority of total membership and two-thirds of those present and voting; federal features also need half of the state legislatures.

  13. Basic structure chain?
    Show answer

    Golaknath 1967 (no) → Kesavananda Bharati 1973 (13 judges, basic structure) → Minerva Mills 1980 (reaffirmed).

  14. Which judgments: Sec 66A struck down, privacy a Fundamental Right, electoral bonds struck down?
    Show answer

    Shreya Singhal 2015; Puttaswamy 2017 (9 judges); ADR 2024.

  15. Which amendment introduced GST, and which Articles?
    Show answer

    101st (2016); Arts 246A, 269A, 279A.

  16. Fifth vs Sixth Schedule?
    Show answer

    Fifth: 10 states, President declares Scheduled Areas, advisory TAC. Sixth: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram, Governor, Autonomous District Councils (26 + 4 = 30).

  17. Modes of acquiring and losing citizenship?
    Show answer

    Acquire: Birth, Descent, Registration, Naturalisation, Incorporation. Lose: Renunciation, Termination, Deprivation.

  18. Under which Act is the Census held, and which Entry?
    Show answer

    Census Act 1948; Entry 69, Union List.

  19. When is the Census 2027 reference date?
    Show answer

    1 Mar 2027 (1 Oct 2026 for snow-bound areas); houselisting from 1 Apr 2026.

  20. Maximum Bharat Ratna and Padma awards a year?
    Show answer

    Bharat Ratna 3; Padma 120 (excluding posthumous and foreign / NRI awardees).

  21. Which Article covers Karnataka, Mizoram and Nagaland (special provisions)?
    Show answer

    371J; 371G; 371A. Proposed 371K is for Ladakh (not enacted).

  22. Which constitutional status did NCBC get and when?
    Show answer

    Art 338B, 102nd Amendment 2018.

  23. Who chairs the NDMA, SDMA, DDMA?
    Show answer

    Prime Minister; Chief Minister; District Collector (co-chair an elected representative of the local authority).

  24. When was the Disaster Management Act enacted?
    Show answer

    23 Dec 2005 (notified 26 Dec 2005); amended in 2025 (Rajya Sabha passed 25 Mar 2025).

  25. What events led to the 2005 Act?
    Show answer

    Pant Committee 1999; Gujarat earthquake 2001 (NDMA recommended); MHA in charge 2002; tsunami 2004.

  26. NCMC and HLC: chairs?
    Show answer

    NCMC: Cabinet Secretary. HLC: Union Home Minister. Both statutory since the 2025 amendment.

  27. Which section covers NDRF force, NIDM, UDMA?
    Show answer

    Sec 44 (NDRF), Sec 42 (NIDM), Sec 41A (UDMA, 2025).

  28. NDRF and SDRF: legal basis and sharing?
    Show answer

    Sec 46 (NDRF) and Sec 48(1)(a) (SDRF); NDRF 100% central; SDRF 75:25, North-East and hill States 90:10.

  29. Which FC merged CRF and NCCF into NDRF and SDRF?
    Show answer

    13th Finance Commission (2009).

  30. 16th FC disaster provisions?
    Show answer

    SDRF + SDMF ₹2,04,401 crore for 2026-31, split 80:20; heatwaves and lightning recommended as notified disasters.

  31. Steps for central relief after a severe calamity?
    Show answer

    State memorandum → ministry check → Central Team → SC-NEC → High Level Committee → Finance Ministry releases.

  32. Sendai Framework: dates, targets, priorities?
    Show answer

    Adopted 18 Mar 2015 (Sendai); 2015–2030; 7 targets, 4 priorities; replaced Hyogo 2005.

  33. Mission Mausam: purpose and outlay?
    Show answer

    Seven-day forecasts for cyclones and floods; ₹2,000 crore; launched 14 Jan 2025 (IMD 150th year).

Growth, outlook and data releases

1/11★ Must-learnPLFS quarterly bulletin, July–September 2026

In plain words

The national statistics office's job survey for July to September 2026 shows more people working or looking for work, and unemployment for those aged 15 and above falling to 5.1% from 5.4% in the previous quarter.

  • By NSO under MoSPI; main source of labour force data; method revamped from January 2025 → quarterly indicators on Current Weekly Status (CWS)

Unemployment rate, overall5.1% (was 5.4% previous quarter)
Unemployment rate, rural4.3%

Urban regular wage/salaried share49.6%

UR 5.4 → 5.1; LFPR 55.5, WPR 52.7.

2/11★ Must-learnAnnual Survey of Industries (ASI) 2024-25 results

In plain words

The statistics ministry's yearly factory survey for April 2024 to March 2025 shows growth in machinery, factories and jobs. Five states produce over half of India's factory value added.

  • Released by MoSPI; reference period Apr 2024 – Mar 2025; data under Collection of Statistics Act, 2008 (amended 2017) and Rules of 2011
  • Gross value of plant and machinery (registered manufacturing): up 7.25%
  • Manufacturing corporate sector (over 89% of GVA): operating factories up 3.45%; persons engaged up 7.57%
  • Top 5 industries by employment (over 41%): food products, textiles, basic metals, motor vehicles, wearing apparel
  • Top 5 states by GVA (over 54%): Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh
Remember

top-5 states over 54% of GVA; top-5 industries over 41% of jobs.

3/11☆ Good to knowHSBC India Manufacturing PMI: 54.7 in October

  • 55.1 (Sept) → 54.7 (Oct); flash estimate was 54.9; compiled by S&P Global; above 50 = expansion
  • New export orders fastest in 6 months; input cost inflation lowest since February; selling-price rise weakest in just under 4 years; jobs up 2nd month; about 18% expect higher output in a year

Trade, FDI and tax

4/11☆ Good to knowPanel to lift uptake of RELIEF for exporters

  • Commerce Ministry → six-member sub-committee to improve fund use and uptake of RELIEF
  • Members from DGFT, Department of Commerce, Department of Financial Services, ECGC
  • RELIEF = Resilience and Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation → under ₹25,060 crore Export Promotion Mission (EPM)
  • Aim: shield exporters from higher freight and insurance costs and maritime disruption in Gulf and West Asian corridors

5/11★ Must-learnGST collections, October 2026: ₹2.31 lakh crore gross

Gross GST collected in October 2026 rose about 23% from a year earlier to 2.31 lakh crore rupees, helped by home demand and a big jump in tax on imports.

Social issue

6/11★ Must-learnCabinet: DA and DR raised 3% to 63% from 1 July 2026

In plain words

Central government employees and pensioners get a 3 percentage point rise in dearness allowance and relief, taking it to 63% of basic pay or pension.

  • DA (employees) and DR (pensioners): 60% → 63% of basic pay/pension; effective 1 Jul 2026
  • Cost ₹10,016.10 crore a year; benefits about 48.54 lakh employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners
  • Formula per 7th Central Pay Commission; revised twice a year (January, July)
Remember

60 → 63; 48.54 lakh employees, 68.71 lakh pensioners.

Banking

7/11☆ Good to knowPayments licences: Razorpay (GIFT City); Fibe (UPI)

  • Razorpay → final Payment Service Provider (PSP) licence from IFSCA to operate from GIFT City → cross-border money movement into and out of India under one framework; banking partners live: RBL Bank, ICICI Bank
  • GIFT City, Gandhinagar, on the Sabarmati → India's first IFSC
  • Fibe (formerly EarlySalary, digital lender) → NPCI approval as Third-Party Application Provider (TPAP) → UPI payments on its app

1/6★ Must-learnRBI sets up Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets (4 Nov)

In plain words

The Reserve Bank formed a committee of seven outside market experts, led by one of its Deputy Governors, to discuss how India's money, bond and currency markets work. It will meet at least once every quarter.

  • Announced in the Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies (October 2026); constituted 4 Nov 2026
  • Chair: Deputy Governor in charge of FMRD; 7 external members; meets at least once a quarter
  • Members: Ananth Narayan (ex-SEBI WTM, IIT Bombay); Shamsher Singh (FIMMDA chair, SBI DMD); Neeraj Gambhir (Axis Bank); Shailendra Jhingan (ICICI Bank); Aditya Bagree (Citibank India); Nand Kishore (CCIL); Ridham Desai (Morgan Stanley India)
  • Scope: money, G-sec, forex and related derivative markets → functioning, liquidity, resilience; trading, clearing, settlement and reporting infrastructure; emerging risks; issues referred by RBI
Remember

TCCFM = DG (FMRD) + 7 outsiders; quarterly.

SEBI

2/6★ Must-learnSEBI opens depositary receipts for REITs and InvITs; OFS cooling-off cut (2 Nov)

In plain words

Real estate trusts and infrastructure trusts can now issue receipts that trade on overseas exchanges in GIFT City, so foreign investors can buy them there. Separately, sellers of hard-to-trade private infrastructure trust units now wait 8 weeks instead of 12 around an offer for sale.

1. Depositary receipts (DRs) framework, twin circulars, 2 Nov 2026, immediate effect

  • DR = foreign-currency instrument issued abroad against Indian securities held with a domestic custodian → lets overseas investors trade Indian units
  • Permitted exchanges: India INX and NSE IX (both IFSC, GIFT City)
  • Listing in India + simultaneous DR issue → approval from Indian stock exchange and the international exchange
  • DRs held only by non-residents
  • Fresh DR issue → approval of at least 75% of votes cast by unitholders; not needed for a simultaneous initial offer in India + DR listing abroad
  • Units behind DRs cannot be priced below the price offered to Indian investors for a similar offering
  • Disclosures made on the international exchange → also filed with Indian exchanges within 24 hours; manager appoints a merchant banker
  • Privately placed InvITs: fresh DRs subscribed only by FIIs and corporate bodies

2. Offer for Sale (OFS) cooling-off, 2 Nov 2026, immediate effect

  • Illiquid privately listed InvITs: 12 weeks → 8 weeks (before and after the OFS)
SecuritiesCooling-off period
Most liquid2 weeks
Liquid4 weeks
Illiquid12 weeks
Illiquid privately listed InvITs8 weeks (was 12)
Exam angle

On which two exchanges can DRs on REIT/InvIT units be listed? What unitholder approval does a fresh DR issue need?

Remember

DR approval 75%; OFS ladder 2 – 4 – 12, and 8 only for illiquid private InvITs.

3/6★ Must-learnSEBI seeks LTCG relief in pre-Budget proposals (Budget 2027-28)

In plain words

The markets regulator has asked the government to stop taxing long-term gains of foreign portfolio investors on Indian shares. It also wants mutual fund investors to pay no such tax when they switch schemes after holding units for over a year.

  • FPIs → scrap LTCG tax on investments in Indian equities
  • Domestic MF investors → LTCG exemption on switching from one MF scheme to another, if units held more than 1 year

LTCG on equity: background

  • Reintroduced in Union Budget 2018-19 (Arun Jaitley) → ended exemption available since 2004; 10% on gains above ₹1 lakh, from 1 Apr 2018
  • Budget 2024-25 → 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh; effective 23 Jul 2024
Listed equityHoldingRate now
LTCGmore than 12 months12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh
STCG12 months or less20%

LTCG 10% → 12.5%; exemption ₹1 lakh → ₹1.25 lakh; STCG 20%.

In plain words

Before the UN climate summit in Turkiye, India said rich countries must provide climate finance that is predictable, mostly public and cheap, and that carbon markets and adaptation indicators should stay voluntary.

  • COP31: Antalya, Turkiye, 9–20 Nov 2026; priorities set out by Bhupender Yadav

8/29★ Must-learnVB–G RAM G Grievance Redressal Rules, 2026 notified

In plain words

The Rural Development Ministry set up a three-level complaint system for the rural jobs scheme. Complaints must be enquired into within 7 working days and settled within 15 days.

  • Notified by Ministry of Rural Development under the VB–G RAM G Act, 2025 (Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin))
  • Three levels set by States: Gram Panchayat → Block → District; District Programme Coordinator oversees district level
  • Filing: in person; speed post; designated Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI); phone or helplines
  • Physical complaints registered on DPI the same day (or next working day); none refused for format, language or method
  • Enquiry within 7 working days → resolution within 15 days → unresolved escalated to next level; appeals under Schedule I of the Act
  • VB–G RAM G Act in force 1 Jul 2026 → repealed MGNREGA, 2005; 125 days of wage work a year per rural household (was 100); wages weekly or within 15 days; unemployment allowance if work not given
  • Centrally Sponsored: Centre–State 60:40; NE and Himalayan 90:10; UTs without legislature 100% Centre; central share FY 2026-27 ₹95,692.31 crore
Remember

3 tiers; 7 days enquiry, 15 days resolution; 125 days of work (MGNREGA 100).

3/16★ Must-learnIndiaAI Mission: foundation models EKA-1, Dhir 2B and Dhir 5B launched

In plain words

The government launched three Indian-made AI models. EKA-1 works in all 22 scheduled Indian languages and English, and the two smaller Dhir models can run offline, even on phones.

  • Launched in New Delhi (MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan) under the IndiaAI Mission (MeitY); teams chosen under the Foundation Models pillar of the IndiaAI Innovation Centre
  • EKA-1 (Soket AI Labs): open sparse hybrid model, 26.3 bn parameters, trained on about 7.5 trillion tokens; all 22 scheduled languages + English; maths, coding, reasoning, agentic uses (BFSI, cybersecurity)
  • Dhir 2B and Dhir 5B (ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations): about 2 bn and 5 bn parameters; open-source; offline, document automation; can run air-gapped and on mobile phones
Remember

EKA-1 = Soket, 26.3 bn; Dhir = ZenteiQ, 2B and 5B.

6/16★ Must-learnCabinet approves 2-year "Second Tour of Duty" for Agniveers

In plain words

Agniveers not picked for regular service after their four years can now serve two more years if they wish. After six years they can be enrolled as regular soldiers if they meet the selection criteria.

  • Union Cabinet; Ministry of Defence; Agnipath Scheme
  • First 4 years → 25% offered regular service on merit
  • Remaining 75% → optional extra 2 years = Second Tour of Duty
  • After 6 years → eligible for regular enrolment (willingness + selection criteria); second tour with enhanced emoluments
  • Announced by CDS Gen N.S. Raja Subramani as the first batch nears 4 years
  • Agnipath (14 Jun 2022): age 17.5–21; pay ₹30,000 (year 1) → ₹40,000 (year 4); life cover ₹48 lakh; Seva Nidhi on exit about ₹11.71 lakh, tax-free
Remember

4 + 2 = 6 years; 25% regular, 75% get the second tour.

Indices, rankings and reports

4/8★ Must-learnWorld Gold Council: India gold demand Q3 2026; central bank buying

In plain words

Indians bought less gold by weight in July to September 2026 but spent more money on it because prices were higher. India is still the second-biggest market for gold bars and coins after China.

  • India demand Q3 2026: 162.5 tonnes (down 29% on year); value ₹2.42 lakh crore (up 3%)
  • Bars and coins = India's largest gold investment channel; India 2nd-largest bar and coin market after China, about 21% of global demand
  • Price drivers: weaker rupee; higher global gold price; higher import duty → basic customs duty on gold and silver 5% → 10%; overall customs duty on gold 15%
  • Central banks (Q3): China 63 t (largest disclosed buyer); Poland 41 t (2nd); Russia sold 19 t (only major seller)
  • WGC HQ: London
Remember

volume down 29%, value up 3%; India's share of bar and coin demand 21%.

6/8★ Must-learnUNEP Adaptation Gap Report 2026

In plain words

The UN environment agency says rich countries give far too little money to help poorer countries adapt to climate change. Developing countries need about 305 billion dollars a year but got 28.2 billion dollars in 2024.

  • Need: $305 bn a year; developed-country funding 2024: $28.2 bn (+$1 bn on year)
  • Brazil climate talks 2025 → triple adaptation finance to $120 bn a year by 2035 → still leaves a gap of over two-thirds; needs projected $420 bn a year by 2035
  • UNEP HQ: Nairobi; COP31: Turkey, 9–20 Nov 2026
Remember

need 305, got 28.2; target 120 by 2035, need 420 by 2035.

Schemes at a glance

1/6★ Must-learnCabinet: ₹2,814 crore CAPEX Support Scheme for critical mineral processing

In plain words

The government will pay part of the cost of four new plants that turn lithium and nickel into battery-grade material, so India depends less on imports.

MinistryMines
Outlay₹2,814 crore (100% central budget); capital support ₹2,800 crore + admin ₹14 crore
Period5 years, FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31
Beneficiaries4 plants: 2 lithium, 2 nickel
Subsidy30% of eligible investment, within caps
LithiumNickel
Min capacity per plant30,000 t50,000 t
Total capacity60,000 t1,00,000 t
Max support per beneficiary₹500 crore₹900 crore
Total allocation₹1,000 crore₹1,800 crore
  • Approved by Union Cabinet on 4 Nov 2026; output for EVs, BESS, electronics, defence, speciality steel
  • Lithium: ores and concentrates (not brines) → battery-grade products; nickel: Class-1 nickel or battery-grade nickel sulphate + cobalt recovery
  • Selection: technical qualification → financial bid → least-cost criterion (lowest capex support sought); 2 per mineral
  • Paid in 3 tranches linked to capex and equity (25% → 50% → commissioning); commission within 3 years of Letter of Award (support tapers after that), maximum 5 years
  • Monitoring: Governing Council (chair: Mines Secretary) → Techno-Financial Committee → Project Management Agency
  • Linked: National Critical Mineral Mission (Jan 2025); Critical Mineral Recycling Scheme ₹1,500 crore (approved 3 Sep 2025); 64 critical mineral blocks and 11 exploration licence blocks auctioned; 24 critical minerals identified
Remember

2,814 crore, 4 plants, 30% subsidy; lithium cap 500, nickel cap 900.

2/6★ Must-learnCabinet: ₹14,500 crore Viability Gap Funding for grid-scale energy storage

In plain words

The government will fund part of the cost of new power storage, such as pumped hydro and big batteries, to add 92 gigawatt-hours of storage by 2030-31.

MinistryPower
Support₹14,500 crore; estimated investment ₹97,600 crore
PeriodFY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31
Target92 GWh new storage = 170% of present grid-scale capacity; need 411 GWh by 2031-32
MixPumped storage 60 GWh; BESS 30 GWh; alternative technologies 2 GWh
  • Allotment through tariff-based competitive bidding (TBCB) → public and private DISCOMs eligible for VGF on BESS and pumped storage
  • BESS → minimum 40% domestic content requirement; alternative-technology projects → public and private entities
  • Earlier (Sept 2023): VGF for BESS → 4,000 MWh by 2030-31; outlay ₹9,400 crore; budget support ₹3,760 crore; VGF up to 40% of capital cost
Remember

14,500 crore → 92 GWh (60 + 30 + 2); BESS DCR 40%.

Growth, outlook and data releases

1/68★ Must-learnIndia GDP growth: who projected what

In plain words

Several big institutions have forecast how fast India's economy will grow this year, and their figures differ slightly. This card helps you tell whose number is whose, because exams like to mix them up.

Source Figure Note
World Bank (FY27) 7.1% up from 6.6% (April 2026 forecast)
UNCTAD (calendar 2026) 7.3% fastest-growing large economy
RBI (FY27) 7.1% raised by 40 bps (basis points)
Ministry of Finance (Q2 FY27, Jul–Sep nowcast, October review) 7.35% after 7.8% in Q1; the September review had said 7.3%
RBI (Q2 FY27) 7.2%
IMF (FY27, October WEO) 7% up from 6.4% (July)
  • Actual Q1 FY27 (Apr–Jun 2026) growth: 7.8% (National Statistical Office, NSO estimate).
  • Remember: World Bank & RBI both 7.1% for FY27; UNCTAD's 7.3% is for calendar 2026, MoF's Q2 nowcast is 7.35% in its October review (7.3% in the September review).

2/68★ Must-learnWorld Bank: India Development Update (Oct 2026), growth + AI

In plain words

The World Bank raised its growth forecast for India and said artificial intelligence could become a major driver of development. It matters because the report shows India is adopting these tools, but still more slowly than the United States.

  • FY27 India GDP forecast: 6.6% → 7.1%; South Asia 2026 forecast: 6.9%.
  • Report: India and Artificial Intelligence: Seizing the Development Opportunity.
  • Private AI investment: $1.2 bn (2024) → $4.1 bn (2025), more than 3×.
  • Global Capability Centre (GCC) professionals: 1.9 mn (2024) → 2.36 mn (2025).
  • India = top 10 emerging markets in AI readiness. Strengths: large technical workforce, globally integrated IT sector, Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI).
  • Firms using AI (as of 6 Oct 2026): India 23% vs US 43%.
  • World Bank Group, via AgriConnect, investing in "small AI" tools (targeted, locally adapted, low-resource settings).

3/68★ Must-learnUNCTAD Trade and Development Report 2026

In plain words

The United Nations trade and development body published its yearly report on the world economy and trade. It expects the world to slow down while India stays the fastest-growing large economy.

  • UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD): est. 1964, HQ Geneva, 195 members.
  • Global trade growth: 4.4% (2025) → 4% (2026).
  • Global GDP growth: 2.9% (2025) → 2.6% (2026) → 2.7% (2027).
  • India: 7.3% in 2026, fastest among major economies.
  • Asia = 59% of global growth in 2026.
  • AI drives trade dynamism but gains are highly concentrated; 2026 trade value rise is price-led (energy shocks, export controls, investment screening, supply-chain conditions).

4/68★ Must-learnCapital expenditure (CAPEX) 2026 survey

In plain words

The government statistics office is surveying how much big private companies plan to spend on new investment. This spending shows how much big companies are willing to invest.

  • Ministry: Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI); conducted by NSO.
  • Period: Oct–Dec 2026; focus: capex of large private corporate enterprises.
  • Static (NSO): set up by government resolution 1 June 2005; constituted 12 July 2006; based on Rangarajan Commission (2001); Chairperson + 4 part-time members + 1 ex-officio member.

5/68★ Must-learnIMF reports, October 2026 (WEO and Asia-Pacific outlook)

In plain words

The International Monetary Fund updated its forecasts and now expects India to grow faster than it said earlier. The report also explains how India coped with the oil supply trouble caused by the conflict in West Asia.

  • India GDP growth: FY27 7% (July estimate 6.4%); FY28 7% (July estimate 6.7%).
  • World growth: 2026 3.1% (up from 3% in July); 2027 3.4% (unchanged).
  • Remember: IMF 7% vs World Bank/RBI 7.1% for FY27.
  • Regional Economic Outlook, Asia and Pacific (October 2026): India's oil diversification helped it cope with West Asia conflict disruptions; India, Japan, South Korea sourced oil outside West Asia, restoring supplies to pre-conflict levels. Diesel and aviation fuel prices rose more sharply than crude.

  • India = fastest-growing major steel market: demand +7.9% in 2026; China demand −2%.
  • World Steel Association (worldsteel): Belgium-based industry body.

Banks and approved agencies that import gold, silver and platinum now pay a small import tax on them. This was done because the earlier exemption ended, which puts these imports on the same footing as other ways of bringing in the metals.

26/68★ Must-learnIndia–Mauritius tax treaty amended: Principal Purpose Test (PPT)

In plain words

India changed its tax treaty with Mauritius so that people cannot use Mauritius just to avoid paying tax. The treaty exists so that income is not taxed twice, and the new test stops it from being misused.

  • Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) = bilateral treaty so the same income is not taxed in both countries.
  • PPT: treaty benefit can be denied if obtaining it is one of the principal purposes of an arrangement; aims at treaty misuse, tax avoidance and evasion.
  • Protocol signed 7 Mar 2024, Port Louis; now notified under Section 159(1), Income-tax Act, 2025.

29/68★ Must-learn57th GST Council meeting (8 Oct 2026)

In plain words

The council that decides goods and services tax rules made the system gentler and simpler. It removed the power to arrest for certain offences, reduced some penalties, and moved refunds towards being handled automatically by the system.

  • Who: GST Council (chair Nirmala Sitharaman), Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. What: process reforms + decriminalisation. Affects: all taxpayers.
  • Arrest powers withdrawn: omit Section 69, CGST Act 2017. Prosecution threshold ₹1 cr → ₹5 cr; Section 132 narrowed (clause c only for fake-ITC without goods/services/invoice). Max general penalty (Section 125) ₹25,000 → ₹10,000.
  • Refunds (Section 54) to become system-based: Phase 1 = auto refund of excess cash-ledger balance, acknowledgement window 15 → 10 days, 90% of zero-rated/inverted-duty claims sanctioned provisionally; Phase 2 = auto sanction for zero-rated supplies.
  • Optional Annual Return Quarterly Payment (ARQP) for B2C-only taxpayers up to ₹5 cr turnover; e-invoicing extended to reverse-charge supplies from unregistered persons and import of services (turnover ₹5 cr+); GSTAT aligned with Tribunals Reforms Act, 2026.

30/68★ Must-learnIndia trade data, April–September 2026-27

In plain words

This shows how much India sold to the world and bought from it in the first half of the financial year. Because India bought more than it sold, it has a trade gap, which is the difference between the two.

  • Total exports (merchandise + services): $476.20 bn (+13.84%); total imports $551.13 bn (+15.68%); trade deficit $74.93 bn.
  • Merchandise exports: $259.89 bn (+18.51%); services exports: $216.31 bn (+8.69%).
  • Fastest-growing merchandise exports in September 2026: electronic goods 70.44%; other cereals 49.88%; handicrafts (excl. handmade carpets) 43.19%.
  • September 2026 merchandise alone: exports $44.40 bn (+23.04%, from $36.08 bn); imports $74.61 bn; merchandise deficit narrowed to $30.21 bn (from ~$33 bn). April–September merchandise imports $437.53 bn (+16.31%).
  • Partners (April–September): US = largest merchandise export destination ($50.81 bn, up from $45.73 bn); China = largest trading partner (two-way trade $91.76 bn), then US ($83.14 bn).
Exam angle

Which merchandise export grew fastest in September 2026?

31/68★ Must-learnGST registration for small e-commerce sellers from 1 November; new RCM e-invoice categories

In plain words

Small online sellers can get a simpler GST registration. They can sell in other states through the e-commerce platform's warehouse without opening their own shop or office there.

  • Facility recommended by the 57th GST Council; enabled from 1 Nov 2026; legal basis: new Rule 14B, CGST Rules, 2017.
  • Optional, for small sellers of goods supplying only through Electronic Commerce Operators (ECOs).
  • Seller can register in other states by declaring the platform's warehouse as principal place of business; ITC (input tax credit) passed on: not more than ₹2.5 lakh a month.
  • Seller must already have a physical presence and GST registration in at least one state (the home state).
  • GSTN e-invoice categories for Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM): RCM-DOM (specified domestic supplies from unregistered persons) and RCM-IMP (imports of services). Lets eligible businesses raise self-invoices and get Invoice Reference Numbers (IRNs) via Invoice Registration Portals (IRPs); threshold: turnover ₹5 crore and above; testing live on all six e-invoice portals.
  • RCM = recipient, not supplier, pays GST on specified transactions.
  • Static: GST introduced 1 July 2017; 101st Constitution Amendment Act, 2016 (passed as the 122nd Amendment Bill, 2014).
Exam angle

Which rule governs the simplified GST registration for small e-commerce sellers?

Remember

Rule 14B; ITC cap ₹2.5 lakh a month; RCM e-invoice threshold ₹5 crore.

32/68★ Must-learnForeign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS) 2026

In plain words

The tax department gave small taxpayers a one-time chance to declare foreign assets or income they had not reported. What they pay depends on how the asset or income was earned.

  • Launched by the Income Tax Department; one-time disclosure of foreign assets and income left out of ITRs (Income Tax Returns); valuation date 31 March 2026; legal basis Section 133, Finance Act, 2026.
Route Limit Payment
Foreign assets from explained sources, not shown in ITR schedule Up to ₹5 crore (as on 31 Mar 2026) Flat fee ₹1 lakh
Foreign assets or income never offered to tax Up to ₹1 crore Tax 30% + additional amount equal to the tax = 60% of declared value or income
Exam angle

What is the total effective payment for foreign income never offered to tax under FAST-DS?

Remember

60% = 30% tax + equal 30% additional amount; flat route = ₹1 lakh.

Foreign exchange rules

40/68★ Must-learnNew FEMA rules for freelancers and influencers

In plain words

New rules now cover people in India who earn money from foreign clients, such as freelancers and online creators. They must record these earnings with their bank and bring the money into India within a fixed time.

  • Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026; effective 1 Oct 2026.
  • Change: export of services now under the Export Declaration Form (EDF) via authorised dealer (AD) banks (earlier only goods and software exporters).
  • Declare full value of services exported; file within 30 days from end of the month in which invoices are raised.
  • Realisation and repatriation: foreign-currency invoice → 9 months; rupee invoice → 12 months.
  • Invoices up to ₹10 lakh: self-declaration to bank is enough to close record, even if client pays less.
  • Unpaid > 1 year past due date → further foreign work only against full advance payment.
  • Remember: EDF = reporting/compliance, not a new tax.
  • Rules supersede the 2015 regulations: one unified EDF for goods, services and software. Realisation period cut: 15 → 9 months (foreign currency), 18 → 12 months (rupee). For goods via EDI ports, EDF is deemed filed with the shipping bill. New Regulation 20: ADs can handle pre-1 Oct 2026 cases that needed RBI approval.

41/68★ Must-learnChild marriage in India

In plain words

Child marriage means marrying someone before the legal age, and India still has a very large share of such marriages in the world. The card shows where it is most common and the law and campaign meant to end it.

  • Global target: end child marriage by 2030 (UN SDG 5, Gender Equality).
  • India ≈ 1 in 3 child brides worldwide; ≈ 1 in 5 young women married before 18.
  • Five states with > half of India's child marriages: UP → Bihar → West Bengal → Maharashtra → Madhya Pradesh.
  • Law: Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 → minimum age 18 (women), 21 (men).
  • Campaign: Child Marriage Free India (2024).
  • UNICEF: est. 11 Dec 1946, HQ New York.
  • Related: California AB 1267 (signed 30 Sep 2026) sets 18 as minimum marriage age with no exceptions, effective 1 Jan 2027.

46/68★ Must-learnSpecial Drawing Rights (SDR) and IMF 2027 review

In plain words

Special Drawing Rights are a kind of reserve money created by the International Monetary Fund that countries can hold and exchange for real currencies. The card explains which currencies make up its value and when it will next be reviewed.

  • SDR = international reserve asset created by IMF in 1969; not a currency; supplements members' forex reserves.
  • Basket: 16 currencies → 5 (1981) → 4 (after euro) → 5 again with Chinese renminbi.
  • Current basket: US dollar, euro, renminbi, yen, pound sterling.
  • Value = weighted average of basket; interest rate = weighted average of short-term rates. Dollar weight dominant.
  • Reviewed every 5 years; next review due by July 2027.
  • Holders: IMF members + 20 prescribed multilateral/international financial institutions.
  • India link: founding member of Project Nexus (Bank for International Settlements, BIS); UPI in 11 countries (40+ expected); multicurrency RTGS (Real Time Gross Settlement) payments in under 60 seconds.

47/68★ Must-learnRBI registers Indiabulls as Core Investment Company (CIC)

In plain words

The Reserve Bank of India approved a company as a Core Investment Company, which is a special kind of finance company that mainly holds shares in the other companies of its own group. The card gives the tests a company must pass to be treated this way.

  • CIC = a type of Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) holding investments in group companies.
  • Criteria: assets ≥ ₹100 cr; ≥ 90% of net assets in group companies; ≥ 60% in equity shares of group companies.

  • After deal: Government 15% + LIC 19% = 34% combined.

52/68★ Must-learn'Bangkok Blueprint' to fight cyber fraud

In plain words

Two world finance bodies launched a plan to help countries and banks fight online fraud and scams, which cost the world a huge amount every year. It is a set of guidelines for working together, not a binding rule.

  • IMF + World Bank, launched at annual meetings in Bangkok: Blueprint for Fraud-Resilient Financial Services.
  • A framework for guidance and collaboration, not formal IMF–World Bank policy guidance.
  • Digital fraud and scams cost about $1 trillion a year (≈ 3% of global GDP). Asia-Pacific scam gangs defrauded residents of at least $88 bn in 2025 (United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, UNODC).

October 2026 · Section 2Regulatory Bodies, PIB, Circulars and Notifications35 items · 23 ★ must-learn · 12 ☆ good to know

RBI

1/35★ Must-learnMonetary Policy, October 2026 (63rd MPC meeting)

In plain words

The Reserve Bank of India raised its main lending rate for the first time in nearly four years and changed its stance to a tighter one. This tells banks and borrowers that cheap loans are unlikely for now and that the central bank is worried about prices rising.

  • Who: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra; met 5–7 Oct 2026. Members: Dr Nagesh Kumar, Saugata Bhattacharya, Prof Ram Singh, Dr Poonam Gupta, Dr Indranil Bhattacharyya.
  • What changed: repo rate 5.25% → 5.50% (+25 bps) = first hike in nearly 4 years. Stance: Neutral → Calibrated Tightening (rate cuts off the table near-term; next move can be hike or pause).
Rate Now
Repo 5.50% (was 5.25%)
Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) 5.25%
Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) 5.75%
Bank Rate 5.75%
  • Timeline: cut to 5.25% on 5 Dec 2025 → hike to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026. Previous hike: 8 Feb 2023 (to 6.50%).
  • Why hiked: inflation concerns, supply-side pressure, demand-side risks. Second-round effects = supply shock (energy/food) spreads into broad price-setting and expectations. Global cue: US Fed hiked 25 bps in September.
  • Next MPC: 2–4 Dec 2026. Forex reserves: $734.6 bn (early Oct 2026).
  • Inflation target: CPI (Consumer Price Index) 4% ± 2% (2–6%); Gazette notification of 25 Mar 2026 renewed it for 5 years, through March 2031.
Period Real GDP projection CPI inflation projection
FY27 7.1% 5.2%
Q2 FY27 7.2% 4.9%
Q3 FY27 6.9% 6.0%
Q4 FY27 6.8% 5.7%
Q1 FY28 7.1% 5.6%
  • Remember: GDP projection raised by 40 bps; CPI peaks in Q3 FY27 (6.0%).

2/35★ Must-learnStatement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies (7 Oct 2026)

In plain words

The Reserve Bank of India announced several changes to make financial data and markets work better. People will be able to share their financial information more easily and see their bank deposits and share holdings together in one statement.

  • Who/what: RBI.
  • Account Aggregator (AA) framework: interoperability among NBFC-AAs; customers can access and share data from any Financial Information Provider (FIP) through any NBFC-AA of their choice.
  • Bank deposits to appear in Consolidated Account Statement (CAS) via NBFC-AAs: demat holders see demat holdings + bank deposits in one place; non-demat customers also get a consolidated view.
  • Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets: forum between RBI and market participants; covers money, Government-securities (G-Sec) and forex markets, plus derivatives and infrastructure.

3/35★ Must-learnCRR daily maintenance raised

In plain words

Banks must keep a fixed part of their deposits with the Reserve Bank of India as cash. The rule now forces them to hold almost the full required amount every single day, which leaves them less room to manage their cash and can make borrowing costlier.

  • Who: RBI under Section 42(1), RBI Act, 1934. Affects: scheduled banks.
  • Minimum daily Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) maintenance: 90% → 99% of prescribed CRR, from 16 Oct 2026. Current CRR: 3%.
  • Effect: less flexibility in daily cash management; may tighten liquidity and raise funding costs.
  • CRR = share of Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) kept with RBI; compliance is judged on fortnightly average, daily floor now 99%.

4/35★ Must-learnForex derivatives tightened; dollar window for oil firms

In plain words

The Reserve Bank of India limited how banks and companies can use currency derivatives and made banks set aside extra cash for some of them. The aim is to limit risky bets on the rupee.

  • Who: RBI. Affects: authorised dealers, users of rupee derivatives.
  • No rebooking of a rupee FX derivative (deliverable or non-deliverable) once cancelled; rollovers at maturity still allowed.
  • Hedging without proving underlying exposure: $100 mn → $5 mn (all AD banks together); same cut for exchange-traded currency derivatives (all exchanges together).
  • New Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR): for rupee-linked FX derivative contracts above $2 mn notional → AD must keep cash reserve with RBI = 20% of rupee equivalent of notional.
  • Clarification (mid-Oct): FERR is held in the bank's CRR account with RBI, over and above mandatory CRR; maintained daily per eligible transaction, until one day after the contract ends; records kept for RBI audit.
  • Rupee near all-time low → RBI special dollar window for 3 state-run Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs): IOC, HPCL, BPCL, via designated banks; from 12 Oct 2026 until further notice.

5/35★ Must-learnFloating Rate Bond (FRB) 2028 coupon

In plain words

The government sells bonds whose interest rate changes over time. This card gives the interest rate for the current six months and explains how it is worked out from recent short-term borrowing rates.

  • RBI fixed FRB 2028 rate at 6.45% for 4 Oct 2026 – 3 Apr 2027.
  • FRB 2034: rate 7.26% for 30 Oct 2026 – 29 Apr 2027 (6.45% in the previous half-year); announced 29 Oct.
  • Linked to 182-day T-Bill yield: average weighted average yield of last 3 auctions + fixed spread 0.64 pp. Reset every 6 months; interest paid half-yearly.

6/35★ Must-learnBank shareholding norms eased

In plain words

The Reserve Bank of India made it easier for mutual funds, insurers and pension funds to own a large share in banks without asking permission again and again. They still have to report big changes and can lose approval if they break the conditions.

  • Who: RBI. Affects: mutual funds, insurers, pension funds investing in banks.
  • One-time approval to hold up to 10% of paid-up share capital or voting rights (aggregate basis).
  • Earlier: fresh approval needed to increase stake if holding fell below 5%.
  • Bank can apply on behalf of qualifying person from its promoter group. Approval can be revoked for non-compliance or "not fit and proper".
  • Any move above/below 5% to be reported to RBI and bank within 3 working days.

7/35☆ Good to knowBPTP penalty

  • RBI compounded penalty ₹4.84 cr on BPTP Ltd and directors: FEMA violations in FDI received in 2007–08.
  • Compounding: Section 15, FEMA, 1999; paying within the period under 15(2) ends pending proceedings.

8/35★ Must-learnRBI special USD-INR forex swap window

In plain words

The Reserve Bank of India opened a special window to swap dollars for rupees, which brought a large amount of foreign currency into the country. Different types of foreign deposits and loans used it, and some windows have already closed.

  • Operational from 8 Jun 2026: FCNR(B) deposits (3–5 year), External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs), Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCBs).
  • Inflows $143.5 bn (to 18 Sep 2026): FCNR(B) about $133 bn, OFCBs $5.32 bn, ECBs $5.3 bn (market estimate for FCNR(B): $90–100 bn).
  • FCNR(B) window closed 31 Aug (original 30 Sep); OFCB/ECB window open to 31 Dec 2026. Yes Bank raised about $2 bn.

9/35★ Must-learnRBI: Credit Valuation Adjustment (CVA) Framework Directions, 2026

In plain words

The Reserve Bank of India told banks to keep extra capital against the risk that the other side of a derivative deal fails to pay. This makes banks safer, and the rule starts from next April.

  • Who: RBI, under Section 35A, Banking Regulation Act 1949. What: capital against CVA risk; effective 1 Apr 2027. Affects: commercial banks (not Small Finance, Payments or Local Area Banks).
  • CVA = adjustment to risk-free derivative price for counterparty default. Default method BA-CVA (basic approach: reduced and full versions). Banks with non-centrally-cleared derivatives notional ≤ ₹10 lakh cr may set CVA capital = 100% of counterparty credit risk capital. CVA RWA = capital charge × 12.5.
  • Excludes trades with QCCPs (qualifying central counterparties) and SFTs.

10/35★ Must-learnRBI Master Direction on Note Sorting Machines

In plain words

The Reserve Bank of India set clear rules for machines that check and sort banknotes, including when a note is too dirty or damaged to be used again. Banks must use only certified machines and replace old ones by a fixed date.

  • Issued by RBI under Sections 35A and 56, Banking Regulation Act, 1949; consolidates rules on note authentication and fitness sorting.
  • Fit note = genuine, clean enough to recycle; unfit = physical condition poor or phased-out series (always unfit).
  • Applies to banks' note processing, sorting and authentication machines (own or through agents).
  • Unfit if: soiling, limpness, dog-ears (>100 mm²), holes (>8 mm²), stains (total >500 mm² or single >200 mm²), tears (vertical 4×8 mm, horizontal 4×15 mm, diagonal 4×18 mm), crumples (>5 mm), decolouration. Repair material ≥100 mm² area, ≥50 μm thick or ≥10 mm wide → suspect/reject.
  • Banks must buy only BIS-certified machines (IS 18663:2024, published 19 Mar 2024); discontinued models phased out by 30 Jun 2027.
Exam angle

Which BIS standard governs note sorting machines, and what is the phase-out deadline?

Remember

IS 18663:2024; deadline 30 June 2027.

11/35★ Must-learnRBI Master Circular: credit facilities to SCs and STs

In plain words

The Reserve Bank of India gathered all its instructions on giving loans to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes into one document. It tells banks to treat these borrowers fairly and lists cheap-loan and guarantee schemes meant for them.

  • Applies to all scheduled commercial banks incl. Small Finance Banks; consolidates instructions going back to 1978.
  • Key rules: special weightage to SC/ST in block and district credit plans; no deposit demanded for loans under government poverty-alleviation or self-employment schemes; subsidy released upfront; rejections decided at next higher level with reasons.
  • DAY-NRLM (Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission): 50% of beneficiaries from SC/ST.
  • Differential Rate of Interest (DRI) scheme: loan up to ₹15,000 at 4% p.a.; at least 40% of DRI advances to eligible SC/ST borrowers.
  • Credit Enhancement Guarantee Scheme for Scheduled Castes (CEGSSC): guarantee cover ₹15 lakh to ₹5 crore; tenure up to 7 years or repayment period, whichever is earlier.
Exam angle

What are the DRI scheme loan limit and interest rate?

Remember

DRI = ₹15,000 at 4%; CEGSSC = ₹15 lakh–₹5 cr.

12/35★ Must-learnRBI: Bank Rate raised, penal interest on CRR/SLR shortfall revised

In plain words

The Reserve Bank of India raised the rate at which it lends to banks in the short term. Because the penalty banks pay for falling short of required reserves is tied to this rate, that penalty also became higher.

  • Bank Rate: 5.50% → 5.75% (+25 bps), effective immediately.
  • Penal interest on shortfall in Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) and Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) is linked to the Bank Rate, so it also rose.
Remember

Bank Rate = MSF rate = repo + 0.25 = 5.75%.

13/35☆ Good to knowRBI Governor: five priorities for financial stability

  • Governor Sanjay Malhotra: no imminent signs of stress, but prolonged stability can encourage excessive risk-taking and leverage.
  • Five priorities: (1) strengthen systemic resilience (endogenous vs exogenous shocks); (2) identify new systemic risks (geopolitics, cyberattacks, tech failures, supply chains, climate); (3) improve granular data, esp. on Non-Banking Financial Institutions (NBFIs); (4) build system-wide resilience incl. critical third-party providers; (5) encourage innovation (AI, tokenisation) without eroding trust.
  • Trust anchors to preserve: sound institutions, settlement finality, singleness of money, financial integrity.

14/35☆ Good to knowRBI rejects all bids at Treasury Bill auction

  • Government planned ₹23,000 cr (91-day ₹8,000 cr; 182-day ₹8,000 cr; 364-day ₹7,000 cr); all 224 bids rejected amid rising short-term yields; first complete rejection since March 2026.
  • Static: T-Bills sold by price-based auction (multiple price method) through RBI's E-Kuber; tenors 91, 182, 364 days; retail allocation capped at 5% of notified amount.

15/35★ Must-learnAccount Aggregator network must be interoperable by 31 December 2026

In plain words

Account aggregators are licensed firms that pass a person's financial data between banks and lenders, only with the person's permission. RBI wants these networks to work with each other by the end of 2026.

  • RBI made the Account Aggregator (AA) network interoperable; deadline 31 Dec 2026; aim: fewer customer drop-offs, easier access to financial data, less operational burden on institutions.
  • AA = RBI-licensed entity moving financial data between institutions only with customer consent; it cannot read or store the data.
  • FIP (Financial Information Provider) holds data, e.g. a bank; FIU (Financial Information User) asks for data, e.g. a lender; Sahamati = RBI-recognised self-regulatory organisation (SRO) for the AA ecosystem.
  • Key figures: 17 Account Aggregators; 176 FIPs.
Exam angle

What is Sahamati, and by when must AAs be interoperable?

Remember

FIP = provider (bank); FIU = user (lender); deadline 31 Dec 2026.

16/35★ Must-learnRBI: new operational-risk and leverage-ratio norms from 1 April 2027

In plain words

RBI changed how banks must work out the capital they hold against operational losses and against their total exposure. Both sets of rules apply from April 2027.

  • Operational risk capital: built on the Business Indicator (BI) with three components: Interest, Lease and Dividend (ILDC), Services (SC), Financial (FC).
  • Loss component = 15 times average annual operational losses, net of recoveries; banks generally use 10 years of loss data; at least 5 years allowed for first-time Internal Loss Multiplier (ILM).
  • Leverage ratio framework revised to align with the Basel Committee (BCBS) 2017 standard; exposure measured across on-balance-sheet, derivative, securities financing and off-balance-sheet items; must be kept at all times.
  • Indian branches of G-SIBs that miss their buffer face capital conservation requirements, based on the Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) risk-based ratio and the Tier 1 leverage ratio.
Category of bank Minimum leverage ratio
Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) 4%
Other banks 3.5%
Indian branches of Global Systemically Important Banks (G-SIBs) 3.5% + applicable leverage ratio buffer
Exam angle

What is the minimum leverage ratio for Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs)?

Remember

D-SIBs 4%; other banks 3.5%; G-SIB branches 3.5% + buffer. Both effective 1 Apr 2027.

17/35☆ Good to knowRBI: Puducherry Co-operative Urban Bank curbs; overseas-investment scrutiny

  • Puducherry Co-operative Urban Bank: restrictions for six months from close of business 21 Oct 2026 (deteriorating finances, supervisory concerns); withdrawal cap ₹5,000 per depositor; insurance up to ₹5 lakh via DICGC (HQ Mumbai; limit raised from ₹1 lakh on 4 Feb 2020).
  • Overseas Direct Investment (ODI): RBI reportedly gave major banks a checklist to report ODI above US$1 bn and deals above 4 times the investor's net worth; no new restriction, only tighter scrutiny, as the rupee weakens.
  • ODI = equity, debt and guarantees; test is control of a foreign entity or more than 10% of its paid-up equity.

19/35★ Must-learnCredit Risk-o-Meter (colour-coded) mandatory

In plain words

The market regulator now requires a simple colour-coded meter showing how risky a debt investment is. This helps ordinary investors understand a credit rating at a glance before they put their money in.

  • Who: SEBI. Affects: issuers, Online Bond Platform Providers (OBPPs), investors.
  • Applies to listed and proposed-to-be-listed: Non-Convertible Securities (NCS), Commercial Papers, Securitised Debt Instruments, Security Receipts, Structured Debt/Market-Linked Debentures; public issues and private placements.
  • Maps ratings AAA to D into 6 colour-coded levels ("Lowest Credit Risk" → "High to Very High Risk of Default").
  • Several ratings → shows the lowest. OBPPs update within 24 hours of rating change; source only from SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agencies; show before investment buttons.
  • Display in: offer documents, abridged prospectus, Private Placement Memorandums, advertisements, OBPP site/app.

20/35★ Must-learnNew settlement formula and fast-track route

In plain words

The market regulator changed how it works out the amount someone pays to settle a case without a full trial, and created a quick route for small cases. It makes settlements fairer and faster.

  • Who: SEBI. Affects: entities settling enforcement cases.
  • New formula: base amount linked to minimum penalty for the violation, adjusted for stage of proceedings, gravity, aggravating/mitigating factors, legal costs.
  • Fast-track settlement for amounts up to ₹10 lakh: two types → violation-based and monetary-threshold-based.
  • Disgorgement (wrongful gains, losses avoided, losses caused to investors) accounted separately.

21/35★ Must-learnInvestor awareness messages by brokers (Project Jagrook)

In plain words

The market regulator is making stock brokers show messages that warn and educate investors on their websites and apps. It is part of an investor awareness effort that begins around a special global week for investors.

  • Who: SEBI. Affects: stock brokers.
  • 5–31 Oct 2026 (World Investor Week): websites must show awareness messages + risk disclosures; trading apps voluntary (if shown, risk disclosure optional).
  • From 1 Nov 2026: messages on website landing page; on trading apps mandatory with risk disclosures on alternate days.
  • Static: International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO): members regulate > 95% of world markets; Board has 35 regulators; 8 policy committees. SEBI is on the Board, all 8 policy committees and the Assessment Committee; also in Growth and Emerging Markets Committee and Asia Pacific Regional Committee.

22/35☆ Good to knowDocument Number Verification System revamped

  • SEBI made "Subject Matter" a mandatory field to verify physical letters/notices; aligned with E-Office Outward Number format.
  • Details needed: outward number, issuing official, date, subject, recipient name.

23/35★ Must-learnClosing Auction Session (CAS) revised

In plain words

The stock market is changing how the last minutes of trading work. A short auction at the end of the day will now decide the closing price.

  • Who: SEBI. Affects: exchanges, traders, derivatives users.
  • CAS: 3:30–3:40 PM, every trading day (10 minutes); randomly timed close between 3:38 and 3:40 PM.
  • Orders: 3:31–3:36 PM market + limit; after 3:36 PM limit only.
  • Derivatives trade till 3:45 PM (except index derivatives on expiry days). Post-close session 3:50–4:00 PM at closing prices.
  • Expiring derivatives settle at VWAP (Volume Weighted Average Price) of last 30 minutes of continuous trading (3:00–3:30 PM).
  • Phases: Phase 1 = 7 Dec 2026; Phase 2 = 8 Feb 2027.

24/35★ Must-learnPortfolio Managers Regulations, 2026 + PRIM route

In plain words

The market regulator replaced its older rules for professionals who manage investments for clients and added a new way for them to invest in mutual funds. It gives these managers wider choice of what to invest in.

  • Who: SEBI. Affects: portfolio managers (PMS), clients.
  • SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2026 replace the 2020 rules; effective 1 Apr 2027.
  • Managers may invest in IPOs, debt primary issues, listed securities, money market instruments, mutual funds; also foreign securities, unlisted securities, exchange-traded derivatives.
  • PRIM = Portfolio Managers Route for Investing in Mutual Fund Units: clients' money into direct plans; products: ETFs, index funds, Specialised Investment Funds (SIFs); minimum ₹25 lakh; entities offering only PRIM need net worth ₹2 cr.
  • Independent fund managers allowed (registered manager keeps liability). Graduates now eligible as Principal Officers.

25/35★ Must-learnCommon Advertisement Code (CAC)

In plain words

The market regulator made one common set of advertising rules for all the firms it supervises. Celebrities can promote a company but cannot make promises or claims about specific products, and firms cannot pass the cost of such advertising to their customers.

  • Who: SEBI. Affects: stock brokers, depository participants, investment advisers, research analysts, online bond platform providers, portfolio managers, mutual funds/AMCs.
  • Celebrities may promote the brand/entity, not specific products or services with inducements or claims.
  • Celebrity endorsement costs cannot be passed to clients or charged to mutual fund schemes. Prescribed disclaimers mandatory.
  • Ratings/rankings only from a Past Risk and Return Verification Agency.

26/35☆ Good to knowSEBI proposals (draft stage)

  • Monitoring agencies (track use of IPO funds): fine ₹50,000 per instance of company non-cooperation. Timeline: exchanges notice within 30 days → promoters' notice after 15 days → demat freeze of promoters after 10 more days. Company cannot change monitoring agency until non-cooperation is cured.
  • SME IPO norms: market-cap based. Up to ₹1,000 cr must list on SME platform; ₹1,000–4,000 cr may opt. Operating profit ₹3 cr average over 3 years (was ₹1 cr in 2 of 3 years). Minimum application ₹2 lakh → ₹1 lakh; minimum lot value ₹25,000; trading lot proposed at 1 share.
  • Remember: cap on general corporate purposes use (₹10 cr) removed, 15% of issue limit stays; promoters' lock-in 1 year; non-promoter pre-issue capital lock-in 1 year → 6 months.

27/35★ Must-learnSEBI: IPO-size relaxation extended to 31 March 2027, plus other measures

In plain words

SEBI is letting companies change the size of the new-share part of their IPO by a bigger amount without redoing paperwork, for another few months. It also warned investors about fake stock-tip groups.

  • IPO relaxation: companies may revise the fresh issue component by up to 50% without fresh draft offer documents; extended to 31 March 2027 (IPOs opening on or before that date); asked by the Association of Investment Bankers of India (AIBI).
  • Normal rule: a change of more than 20% in issue size needs fresh draft documents. Applies only to fresh issue, not Offer for Sale (OFS).
  • Margin relief against Early Pay-in (EPI): clearing corporations will not collect margins on a client's later buy or sell positions in cash segment up to the value of securities for which EPI was accepted; real time; value = lower of securities pay-in made and securities sold; not for trade-for-trade securities.
  • BSE IPO fast-tracking widened from top 10 to top 30 companies (by average daily market capitalisation), from 23 Oct 2026.
  • Market Infrastructure Institutions (MIIs): proposed automatic approval route to deploy funds; annual cap = lower of 5% of net worth (31 March) or regulatory minimum net worth; net worth must stay at least 1.5× minimum; clearing corporations excluded.
  • Research analysts: call recording with institutional investors no longer mandatory; records kept 5 years.
  • SEBI warned against unregistered stock-tip groups on invitation-only WhatsApp.
Exam angle

Up to what percentage can the fresh-issue part of an IPO be revised without fresh draft documents?

Remember

Relaxed 50% vs normal 20%; fresh issue only, not OFS; till 31 Mar 2027.

  • Route 1: sponsor ensures MF Lite AMC net worth at least ₹35 cr (falls to above ₹25 cr after 5 straight profitable years).
  • Route 2: ₹75 cr infused at registration; then maintain above ₹50 cr (falls to above ₹25 cr after 5 profitable years).

29/35★ Must-learnSEBI: FPI KYC review made less frequent

In plain words

Foreign portfolio investors will have their customer checks reviewed less often. Annual reviews become every two years and three-yearly reviews become every eight years.

  • Circular dated 30 Oct 2026; effective 1 Dec 2026
  • KYC review periodicity: 1 year → 2 years; 3 years → 8 years (Category I FPIs and regulated Category II FPIs from non-high-risk jurisdictions get 8 years)
  • Unchanged: SWAGAT-FI FPIs (10 years); GS-FPIs (as per RBI periodicity for their bank accounts)
Exam angle

New maximum KYC review cycle for FPIs (other than SWAGAT-FI)? (8 years)

31/35★ Must-learnASCI guidelines on AI-generated ad content

In plain words

The advertising standards body now requires ads to say clearly when content made by artificial intelligence could influence buyers. This lets people know when they are seeing fake people, voices or events.

  • Who: Advertising Standards Council of India (ASCI; est. 1985, Mumbai). Effective 29 Dec 2026.
  • Labelling mandatory where synthetically generated content (SGC) materially influences consumers (AI influencers, likeness/voice replication, fabricated events). Sponsored AI suggestions: "Sponsored by [Brand]".
  • No label for routine edits, decorative effects, ad copy, subtitles and translations.

In plain words

Large cooperative societies that work in more than one state will now have their accounts checked using one standard report format, like the one companies already use. This makes audits more uniform and easier to compare.

  • Mandated by the Ministry of Cooperation; uniform, risk-based statutory audit reporting for Multi-State Co-operative Societies (MSCS); powers from Section 73(6), MSCS (Amendment) Act, 2023.
  • Modelled on the corporate Companies (Auditor's Report) Order (CARO); framed with inputs from RBI, ICAI, CAG and MSCS; audit data to be linked to the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) portal.

MSCARO is modelled on CARO (companies).

1/21★ Must-learnG7 coordinated oil release

In plain words

Major rich countries agreed to release oil from their stocks over the next few months to keep fuel supply steady. It shows countries acting together to protect the world economy from fuel shortages.

  • G7 (chair France, Macron) and partners to release 100 million barrels of crude and diesel over 4 months (diesel front-loaded in first 20 days); coordinator: International Energy Agency (IEA).
  • Background: in Mar 2026 the IEA pledged 400 mn barrels (largest ever); previous record 182.7 mn (2022, after Russia's invasion of Ukraine).

16/21★ Must-learnClimate reports: NDC Synthesis Report 2026 and adaptation finance

In plain words

A United Nations report says countries' current climate promises will cut emissions only a little by 2035, far short of what is needed. Another report says the world is on course for much more warming than the 1.5°C target.

  • UNFCCC 2026 NDC Synthesis Report: current pledges cut global greenhouse gas emissions only 6% below 2019 levels by 2035; 9% with conditional elements fully implemented.
  • NDCs plus long-term targets imply about 1.7°C–2.3°C warming by 2100; net-zero targets between 2040 and 2070, majority 2050. Paris Agreement adopted 2015; countries set their own Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).
  • UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026: current policies mean 2.8°C; warming now about 1.4–1.5°C; window to avoid breaching 1.5°C has closed, overshoot likely.
  • Adaptation: India's first Adaptation Communication (2023) estimates ₹56.68 trillion needed by 2030; UNEP Adaptation Gap Report 2025: developing countries need over USD 310 bn a year by 2035, at least 12 times current flows.
Exam angle

By how much will current pledges cut emissions below 2019 levels by 2035, per the NDC Synthesis Report?

Remember

6% (current pledges) vs 9% (with conditional); 1.7–2.3°C.

The body that conducts India's main government recruitment exams completed one hundred years. It matters because it is the constitutional institution that selects officers fairly, and the card traces how it began and grew.

  • Origin: 1 Oct 1926, first Public Service Commission (advisory; members appointed by Secretary of State). Roots: Government of India Act, 1919; Lee Commission recommended a statutory body.

6/82★ Must-learnShram Samvad: labour codes awareness campaign

In plain words

The labour ministry began a three-month campaign to explain the four new labour laws to workers and employers across the country. The new laws replaced many older laws, so people need to know what has changed for them.

  • Who: Ministry of Labour and Employment (Mansukh Mandaviya); 90 days from 28 Sep 2026; industrial clusters in 316 districts, all 36 States/UTs.
  • 4 Labour Codes (Wages 2019; Industrial Relations 2020; Social Security 2020; Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions 2020) effective 21 Nov 2025, rationalising 29 central laws.
  • Wages Code: minimum wages statutory for all sectors. IR Code: Fixed Term Employment with equal benefits.

Agriculture, food and rural

19/82★ Must-learnCap on anti-cancer drug margins

In plain words

The government limited how much shops and middlemen can add to the price of certain cancer medicines. This should make these costly medicines cheaper and save patients and families a lot of money.

  • Trade margins on non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs capped at 30% of MRP; Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers; implemented by National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA).
  • Impact: prices may fall up to 70%; savings ≈ ₹2,500 cr a year.
  • Covers 137 drugs (Trade Margin Rationalisation under Paragraph 19, Drugs (Prices Control) Order 2013); revised prices from 9 Nov 2026; check prices on NPPA website or Pharma Sahi Daam app. Builds on a 2019 pilot capping margins on 42 anti-cancer drugs at 30%.

20/82★ Must-learnNational PNG Drive 3.0

In plain words

The government launched a drive to bring cooking gas through pipes to a large number of homes. A single website will help customers and gas companies deal with each other.

  • By Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and PNGRB (Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board); launched by Hardeep Singh Puri.
  • Oct 2026 – 31 Mar 2027; target 50 lakh domestic piped natural gas (D-PNG) connections.
  • Unified PNG Portal: single digital platform for PNG customers and city gas distribution entities.

21/82☆ Good to knowKhet Bachao Abhiyan – Rabi 2026

22/82★ Must-learnMSP for Rabi crops, Marketing Season 2027-28

In plain words

The government raised the minimum prices at which it buys winter-season crops from farmers for the next season. These prices protect farmers from falling market rates and encourage them to grow pulses and oilseeds as well as wheat.

  • Who: Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA); all 6 mandated Rabi crops. | Crop | New MSP (₹/quintal) | Rise | Margin over cost | |---|---|---|---| | Wheat | 2,610 (from 2,585) | 25 (lowest) | 106% (highest) | | Barley | 2,286 (from 2,150) | 136 | 58% | | Gram | 5,958 (from 5,875) | 83 | 59% | | Lentil (masur) | 7,390 (from 7,000) | 390 | 92% | | Rapeseed and mustard | 6,613 (from 6,200) | 413 | 96% | | Safflower | 7,215 (from 6,540) | 675 (highest) | 50% |
  • Basis: MSP at least 1.5× All-India weighted average cost of production (Budget 2018-19). Higher pulses/oilseed MSP = crop diversification.
  • Payout for procuring 324 lakh tonnes in 2027-28: ₹90,962 cr.

23/82☆ Good to knowAgriculture: targets and procurement

  • Foodgrain target 2026-27: 373.93 mn tonnes (2025-26 output 376.56 mn tonnes); Rabi target 177.72 mn tonnes. Announced by Shivraj Singh Chouhan at the National Agriculture Conference – Rabi Campaign 2026.
  • Context: strengthening El Niño, uneven monsoon → district-level Rabi plans on a water budget; ICAR groundwater assessment; pulses and oilseeds in low-rain areas.
  • Fertiliser: stock above 16.3 mn tonnes (12.2 last year); states' Rabi need about 38 mn tonnes.
  • Price Support Scheme (PSS), Kharif 2026-27: ₹5,547.99 cr MSP procurement of pulses and oilseeds → UP ₹3,992.57 cr (tur, moong), Karnataka ₹1,107 cr (soybean, moong, sunflower), Telangana ₹448.42 cr (soybean, moong).

24/82★ Must-learnNational Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) continued for 5 years; schemes renamed

In plain words

The government renewed its main scheme of pensions for the elderly, widows, disabled people and poor families for five more years and gave its parts new names. It also lowered the level of disability needed to qualify, so more people can benefit.

  • Union Cabinet: outlay ₹53,428 crore, 2026-27 to 2030-31; 3.20 crore beneficiaries in all 36 States/UTs; nodal: Department of Rural Development.
  • NSAP → Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana. IGNOAPS (old age) → PM Vridhavastha Pension Yojana; IGNWPS (widow) → PM Vidhawa Pension Yojana; IGNDPS (disability) → PM Divyangjan Pension Yojana; National Family Benefit Scheme → PM Parivar Labh Yojana.
  • Disability pension: ₹375 (age 0–79), ₹625 (80+); benchmark disability cut 80% → 40%; eligibility now from birth.
  • Static: NSAP launched 15 Aug 1995; Article 41 (Directive Principles); 100% Central funding.
Exam angle

What is the new minimum disability for pension under NSAP?

Remember

Disability benchmark 80% → 40% (RPwD Act, 2016).

The rural development ministry greatly expanded the list of works that can be done under the rural employment guarantee law. It lets villages choose from more kinds of work, such as water conservation, roads and disaster preparation.

  • Four pillars: water security 128 (34%); core rural infrastructure 111 (30%); livelihood infrastructure 98 (26%); disaster preparedness 38 (10%).
  • Agriculture-related works: 181, of which 52 are individual-beneficiary works.

How many permissible works are now notified under VB–G RAM G?

Infrastructure, transport and energy

29/82★ Must-learnExempted FASTag guidelines (PwD vehicles)

In plain words

New rules say which vehicles of people with disabilities can use highway toll tags without paying. A person with a higher level of disability gets the free pass for a longer period before it must be renewed.

  • Effective 2 Oct 2026; governed by National Highways Fee Rules, 2008.
  • Disability 70–100% → valid 5 years; 40% to <70% → valid 3 years; renewal allowed after expiry (eligibility permitting).
  • Static: UDID (Unique Disability ID) card number has 18 characters.

30/82★ Must-learnPorts and waterways

In plain words

Several news items about ports and river transport are grouped here, including a plastic-free oil terminal and the first goods shipped by river from Assam to Bangladesh. It matters because it shows India reviving old water routes and making ports cleaner.

  • Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal (Mumbai Port Authority) declared plastic-free on 2 Oct 2026 (Sarbananda Sonowal). Static: Major Port Authorities Act, 2021 (in force 3 Nov 2021) replaced Major Port Trusts Act, 1963.
  • First international cargo (methanol, from Assam Petro-Chemicals) flagged off: Bogibeel Terminal (Dibrugarh) → Pangaon Port, Dhaka, via National Waterway-2 (Brahmaputra), reviving the route after ~80 years. Skill centre at Bogibeel: ₹200 cr, train 50,000 youths in 10 years.

31/82★ Must-learnIndia–EU green shipping corridor coalition

In plain words

India and the European Union launched a group to make shipping routes greener. It also sets goals for ports to use more renewable energy and to handle much more cargo over the coming decades.

  • Unveiled at Sagarmanthan 2026 (3rd; Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways + ORF); theme "Blue Geographies, New Aspirations: Trade, Technology and Trust at Sea".
  • Renewable share in major ports' energy: over 60% by 2030, above 90% by 2047.
  • Green hydrogen hubs: Deendayal (Kandla), Paradip, V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin). Target: port capacity ×4 to 10 bn tonnes by 2047.

32/82★ Must-learnFASTag Annual Pass crosses 1 crore

In plain words

More than ten million people bought a yearly pass that lets non-commercial vehicles cross highway toll booths without paying each time. It makes paying tolls simpler for ordinary car owners.

  • Launched 15 Aug 2025 (NHAI, about 1,150 fee plazas); non-commercial vehicles; 1 year or 200 crossings, whichever first.
  • Fee ₹3,000 → ₹3,075 from 1 Apr 2026; bought via Rajmargyatra app or NHAI site; activated within 2 hours.
  • Static: FASTag uses RFID; valid 5 years; IHMCL implements, NPCI runs NETC clearing house; all lanes FASTag lanes since 15/16 Feb 2021; no valid tag = 2× fee; helpline 1033.

41/82★ Must-learnDraft Bharat Stage VII (BS-VII) emission norms

In plain words

The government proposed stricter pollution rules for new vehicles, to be introduced step by step from 2029. For the first time, they also limit dust from brakes and tyres and require electric-vehicle batteries to last.

  • Draft notification by the Road Transport and Highways Ministry amending the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989; aligned with Europe's Euro 7.
  • Phased from April 2029 to April 2035: cars and SUVs (category M1) April 2029; small goods vehicles and pick-ups 2030; buses and heavy vehicles April 2031; two-wheelers to be notified separately.
  • Particulate size threshold 23 nm → 10 nm; first-ever limits on brake-wear and tyre-abrasion emissions; battery-durability rules for electric vehicles. India has followed BS-VI since April 2020 (skipped BS-V).
Remember

BS-VII from April 2029 (cars first); India skipped BS-V.

Owners of very old, polluting trucks and buses in Delhi-NCR get discounts and cheaper loans if they scrap them and buy a cleaner BS-VI or electric vehicle.
