Environment, wildlife and heritage

48/82★ Must-learnProject Cheetah: five cubs at Kuno

In plain words

A cheetah born in India gave birth to five cubs in a national park in Madhya Pradesh. India brought cheetahs back after they died out here, so each birth in the wild shows the project is succeeding.

  • Indian-born female cheetah gave birth to 5 cubs at Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh.
  • Static: launched 2022; cheetah extinct in India 1952; India = first country to attempt reintroduction of an extinct large carnivore; Namibia batch first, South Africa batch 2023.

49/82★ Must-learnIndia's Ramsar sites reach 103

In plain words

Two more wetlands in India were added to the list of internationally important wetlands, taking the total to over one hundred. Wetlands protect water, wildlife and nearby people, so this recognition helps conserve them.

  • Added: Sukhna Lake (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (Uttar Pradesh).
  • Ramsar Convention: 1971. Most sites: Tamil Nadu (20). Largest: Sundarban (West Bengal, 4.23 lakh ha). Smallest: Renuka (Himachal Pradesh, 20 ha).
  • First Indian sites (1981): Chilika (Odisha), Keoladeo (Rajasthan). Montreux Record: Keoladeo, Loktak (Manipur).
  • Country ranking: UK 176, Mexico 144, India 103.

50/82★ Must-learnIndia's UNESCO Tentative List: now 81 sites

In plain words

India keeps a waiting list of places it may nominate for UNESCO World Heritage status. Three more sites were added, so the list now has 81 places.

  • Three new sites added: Karst-Mud-Volcano Complex of Baratang (Andaman and Nicobar); Andaman Subduction Volcanoes, Narcondam and Barren Islands; Sirpur Cultural and Archaeological Landscape (Mahasamund, Chhattisgarh; east bank of the Mahanadi; ancient Shripur, capital of Kosala under the Sharabhapuriya dynasty, later Panduvamshi).
  • List now 81 sites: 59 cultural, 3 mixed, 19 natural.
  • Static: India has 45 World Heritage Sites (37 cultural, 7 natural, 1 mixed): 6th globally, 2nd in Asia-Pacific; latest = Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath (Varanasi).

Sabarmati, Sevagram, Aga Khan Palace).
  • Tentative List inclusion is a prerequisite for World Heritage nomination.

59/82★ Must-learnWHO–UNICEF JMP report on school WASH (2015–2025)

In plain words

A report by the United Nations health and children's agencies found that many schoolchildren around the world still have no proper toilets, and India has the largest number of such children. It matters because it shows how much work remains to give every child clean water and sanitation at school.

  • Progress on Drinking Water, Sanitation and Hygiene in Schools 2015-2025; JMP = Joint Monitoring Programme (monitors WASH SDG targets).
  • India: 50 mn children with no sanitation service at school, the highest, of 244 mn globally. Top 5: India 50, Nigeria 34, Ethiopia 26, DR Congo 11, Indonesia 8 (mn).
  • Global: 460 mn lack basic sanitation at school. India: schools with no sanitation down 14%; basic water coverage up above 4% a year; 2030 trajectory: water 84%, sanitation 81%, hygiene 79%.

81/82★ Must-learnFrontier Nagaland Territorial Authority Bill, 2026 gets President's assent

In plain words

Six eastern districts of Nagaland get their own elected authority with powers over many subjects, as a step short of the separate state their people had demanded.

  • President Droupadi Murmu assented; Bill passed unanimously by Nagaland Assembly (earlier March version deferred after MHA sought clarity)
  • Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority for 6 districts: Tuensang, Mon, Longleng, Kiphire, Noklak, Shamator
  • 62 members: 40 elected (one-third of seats for women), 2 nominated by Governor, 20 MLAs of the area ex-officio (no vote); term 5 years; powers over 46 subjects; executive council max 9
  • Follows Memorandum of Agreement of 5 Feb 2026 (Centre, Nagaland, Eastern Nagaland Peoples' Organisation = ENPO); ENPO demanded a separate state since 2010
Exam angle

How many members does the Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority have?

Remember

62 = 40 elected + 2 nominated + 20 MLAs; 6 districts; 46 subjects.

Science and Technology

1/32★ Must-learnNexCAR19: India's first indigenous CAR-T therapy

In plain words

India now has its own treatment for certain blood cancers, which uses a patient's own immune cells that are changed to attack the cancer. It was developed by Indian institutions and is the first of its kind approved in the country.

  • CAR-T = chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy (immunotherapy using patient's own cells); for B-cell cancers (leukaemia, lymphoma).
  • Built by IIT Bombay + Tata Memorial Centre + ImmunoACT; first CAR-T approved by CDSCO (Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation).

  • IIT Madras team AgniRath (vehicle Aagneya) took 3rd at Sasol Solar Challenge 2026 (South Africa, biennial): 1,192.6 km in 8 days; first Indian team to win a trophy.

  • University of Kerala (Geology): Mars-like sites in Tamil Nadu and Chile's Atacama; melanterite at Neyveli, gypsum at Atacama and Tiruchirappalli badlands (hydrous sulphate minerals).

4/32★ Must-learnNational Supercomputing Mission (NSM)

In plain words

India is building powerful supercomputers across the country as part of a national mission. Dozens are already running and the plan is to add more, built with Indian technology.

  • 40 supercomputers, 68 PF (Sep 2026); target 50 systems, above 123 PF. Launched Apr 2015, outlay about ₹4,500 cr; DST + MeitY; implemented by C-DAC Pune and IISc Bengaluru.
  • PARAM Rudra series (indigenous Rudra servers by C-DAC); PARAM Shavak (supercomputing-in-a-box). Backbone: National Knowledge Network. Static: PARAM 8000 (1991).

  • TakeMe2Space: India's first networked orbital data centre mission, Falcon 9 (Waymaker 2), 2028; 2 satellites × 100 kg. SatLeo Labs TAPAS-1: commercial thermal-imaging CubeSat payload.
  • CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad: AI translation for CAG documents (launched at Hindi Diwas closing). BHASHINI: 36 text languages, 23 voice, 35 international; Hindi Pakhwada 14–29 Sep 2026.

6/32★ Must-learnNational Quantum Mission and quantum links

In plain words

India has a government mission to build quantum technology, which is used for very secure communication and powerful computers. It has already reached steps such as a long-distance secure link.

  • NQM: Cabinet 19 Apr 2023; ₹6,003.65 cr (2023-24 to 2030-31); DST. 1,000 km quantum-secure communication achieved in 3 years (8-year target 2,000 km). Targets 50–1,000 qubit computers.
  • 4 Thematic Hubs: Computing – IISc Bengaluru; Communication – IIT Madras (+ C-DoT); Sensing and Metrology – IIT Bombay; Materials and Devices – IIT Delhi.
  • QNu Labs + BISAG-N + IIT Gandhinagar: India's first free-space QKD link, 5.56 km (device Armos; platform Vedic Kavach; QBER < 5%). India's bioeconomy ~$196 bn (from $10 bn in 2014); target $300 bn by 2030 (Jitendra Singh).

  • IMD Cyclone Warning and Marine Weather DSS (WebGIS) dedicated to nation; IMD DG Mrutyunjay Mohapatra is 3rd Vice-President of WMO; IMD founded 1875.
  • CAIK (Centre for AI in Keralam, Thiruvananthapuram): MeitY–IndiaAI CoE; implementing agency Digital University Kerala; first cohort 15 startups.
  • CoRover.ai (BharatGPT) selected by NeGD for unified agentic AI bot platform; DigiLocker first use.
  • GATE 2027: new paper Robotics and Automation (total 30); 6, 7, 13, 14, 20, 21 Feb 2027; CBT; score valid 3 years.
  • NASA Perseverance odometer 45.22 km (11 Oct) beat Opportunity's 45.16 km; landed Jezero Crater 18 Feb 2021.

8/32★ Must-learnCERVAVAC: first Indian HPV vaccine WHO-prequalified

In plain words

A vaccine made in India that protects against a virus linked to cervical cancer has been approved by the World Health Organization for purchase by international health programmes. This matters because it can be supplied to many countries at a lower cost.

  • Serum Institute of India (SII), Pune; first Indian-made quadrivalent Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine to get WHO prequalification.
  • Gender-neutral; licensed in India for ages 9–26; prevents cervical cancer and other HPV-related disease.
Exam angle

Which Indian company makes CERVAVAC?

12/32★ Must-learnGSLV-F18 launches NVS-03 navigation satellite

In plain words

India launched a new satellite for its own navigation system, NavIC, on 30 October. It was the twentieth flight of the GSLV rocket.

  • Launched 30 Oct 2026, 23:51 IST, from the Second Launch Pad, Sriharikota; 20th GSLV flight
  • NVS-03: third second-generation NavIC satellite, about 2,232 kg, placed in geosynchronous transfer orbit
  • Adds the L1 signal to the existing L5 and S signals

14/32★ Must-learnDefence Accounts Department (DAD): 279th Annual Day

In plain words

The department that handles the accounts and payments of the defence forces celebrated its yearly day and launched new computer systems. These systems help money reach the right place on time and make pensions and pay easier to handle.

  • Launched by Rajnath Singh at DRDO Bhawan. IT initiatives: SAKSHAM with Indian Army Financial Information System; revamped National Compilation System; Treasury Single Account (TSA) in MoD (Just-In-Time fund release; via PRISM; integrated with RBI e-Kuber).
  • Others: SAMPURNA (revenue procurement), SAMAR-SETU (Agniveer pay), SPARSH (pension). Publications: COSHE 2026 (Comprehensive Statistical Handbook on Defence Expenditure), Raksha Lekha Bharati, Market Intelligence Report 2025-26.

15/32★ Must-learnNavy and Coast Guard

In plain words

The navy and coast guard received new ships, such as a support ship that supplies other warships and a patrol vessel. Most of them are built in India, which shows the country's growing ability to build its own ships.

  • Fleet Support Ship-1 'Surya' launched at Hindustan Shipyard Ltd (HSL), Visakhapatnam (18 months after steel cutting); keel of FSS-5 laid; first of 5 FSS. Static HSL: Jala Usha (1948) first ship built in independent India; Miniratna Category-I in 2025; 2nd biggest shipyard after Cochin.
  • INS Mangrol, 3rd ASW Shallow Water Craft by Cochin Shipyard, commissioned 12 Oct at Naval Dockyard Mumbai; > 80% indigenous; named after minesweeper INS Mangrol (M85, served till 7 Apr 2004).
  • ICGS Ajit: 7th of 8 Adamya-class Fast Patrol Vessels (Goa Shipyard); launched 9 Oct; for Okha, Gujarat.

16/32★ Must-learnContracts and trials

In plain words

The defence ministry signed deals and tested equipment such as ship-launched missile systems and a high-flying balloon-like platform for watching from the sky. It shows India buying and developing its own defence equipment.

  • BrahMos Aerospace: ₹661.50 cr contract for fire control systems and launchers for Navy ships; Buy (Indian-IDDM) category. BrahMos = Brahmaputra + Moskva.
  • DRDO flight trial of High-Altitude Platform (HAPS) (lighter-than-air, stratospheric surveillance) at Nyoma, Ladakh: reached 21 km AMSL, stayed at 20 km for > 30 min; developed by ADRDE Agra, made by OPF Kanpur. Static DRDO: est. 1 Jan 1958.
  • HAL Koraput: 2,000th aero-engine delivered; second Shakti engine line (₹218 cr) for Dhruv ALH and Prachand LCH.
  • MoD–Bharat Electronics Ltd (BEL): nearly ₹770 cr for Improved Low Level Light Weight Radar (LLLR-I); detects fighter-sized targets, mini-drones and micro-drones.
  • DRDO + CSIR-CGCRI (Kolkata): ₹50 cr, 4-year project on indigenous lightweight bulletproof glass-ceramic for armoured vehicles (30–50% lighter); target multi-shot AK-47 protection from 100 m (BIS V and VI).

17/32★ Must-learn'Bharat Rice' for the Army

In plain words

The army began supplying rice for its soldiers through a national cooperative, including to forward posts. It shows several government bodies working together to feed the forces.

  • Launched by Indian Army for defence forces (Rajnath Singh and Pralhad Joshi present); led by Directorate General of Supplies and Transport.
  • Supplier: NAFED (National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India); FY 2026–27; 10 kg and 30 kg bags for forward posts.
  • Followed about 18 months of coordination (Army, FCI, NAFED, Department of Food and Public Distribution).

18/32★ Must-learnINS/MPV Samarthak

In plain words

The navy began using a new multi-purpose ship, the first of four, built by an Indian company. It is part of India building more of its navy's ships at home.

  • First of 4 Multi-Purpose Vessels (MPVs); commissioned at Naval Base Karwar on 16 Oct (as reported).
  • Builder: Larsen & Toubro, Kattupalli (Tamil Nadu). Motto: "Victory is Our Sole Aim" (Sanskrit).

19/32★ Must-learnMoD contracts: GSAT-7C and Varunastra

In plain words

The defence ministry signed large deals for a military communication satellite for the air force and heavy torpedoes for the navy. Both will be made in India, so the money supports the country's own industry.

  • Total over ₹4,000 cr.
  • GSAT-7C satellite (Indian Air Force): over ₹2,500 cr, with New Space India Limited (NSIL), Bengaluru.
  • Varunastra heavy-weight torpedoes (Indian Navy): over ₹1,500 cr, with Bharat Dynamics Ltd, Hyderabad; indigenous ship-launched anti-submarine torpedo by Naval Science and Technological Laboratory (NSTL).

In plain words

India finished fourth at the Asian Games in Japan and won team golds in cricket, kabaddi and hockey. The card shows the top rankings and the memorable wins.

Rank Nation Gold Silver Bronze Total

Hockey: women beat China 1–0 (Lalremsiami, 10th min) = first gold since 1982 (44 years); men beat Malaysia 5–1 = 5th men's gold (1966, 1998, 2014, 2022, 2026).

Boxing 6 (3 G, 3 B). Gold: Lovlina Borgohain (75 kg), Parveen Hooda (65 kg), Ankush Panghal (men's 80 kg)

Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down as captain of India's women's cricket team and Smriti Mandhana took over. It matters because she led the team to its first one-day World Cup win.

Nobel Prizes 2026

1/13★ Must-learnWinners

In plain words

The Nobel Prizes honour people who made the greatest contributions in science, literature, peace and economics. The card lists this year's winners and what each one was rewarded for.

Prize Winner(s) For
Physiology or Medicine (Karolinska) Karl Deisseroth (USA), Peter Hegemann, Georg Nagel (Germany) light-gated ion channels, optogenetics
Physics (Royal Swedish Academy) Francis Halzen (Belgian-born) IceCube Neutrino Observatory (South Pole), high-energy astrophysical neutrinos
Chemistry (Royal Swedish Academy) Henri B. Kagan (France), Kenso Soai (Japan) nonlinear effects and self-catalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis
Peace (Norwegian Nobel Committee) Navanethem "Navi" Pillay (South African jurist, Indian Tamil origin) accountability for war crimes, crimes against humanity, genocide; judge at ICTR and ICC
Literature (Swedish Academy) Anne Carson (Canadian) oeuvre creating new forms in dialogue with classical tradition
Economic Sciences (Sveriges Riksbank Prize) Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford (both USA) microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation; 12 mn kronor shared equally
  • Prize amount (Physics, Literature): 12 mn Swedish kronor (~$1.2 mn).
  • Static: Nobel will of Alfred Nobel 1895; first awarded 1901; Economics prize (Sveriges Riksbank Prize, est. 1968, first 1969) is not from the 1895 will.

10/13★ Must-learnGlobal Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2026 (UNDP + OPHI)

In plain words

A United Nations report measures poverty not just by income but by health, education and living conditions. It shows that India has cut such poverty sharply, while the number of poor people in the world rose for the first time.

  • Three dimensions: Health, Education, Standard of Living; scale 0–1 (higher = poorer).
  • Coverage: 108 countries, 6.3 bn people; 1.2 bn in acute multidimensional poverty (18.9%); 617 mn are children; 83% rural.
  • First rise in numbers since MPI began in 2010. 33 countries halved MPI in under 15 years.
  • Highest: Chad 0.517 (incidence 84.2%), then Niger, CAR, Burundi, Madagascar. Lowest: Serbia 0.000, Azerbaijan, Armenia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan.
  • India: MPI 0.283 → 0.069 (2005/06 → 2019/21, 14.5 years); incidence 55.1% → 16.4%.
  • Static: SDG target 1.2 = halve poverty in all dimensions by 2030.

11/13★ Must-learnWorld Bank Poverty and Equity Brief (October 2026)

In plain words

The World Bank's report shows how many Indians live below different poverty lines and how this fell over the years. It shows big progress, with the poor now mostly in a few regions and in rural areas.

Line Result
Lower-middle-income line ($4.20/day) 57.7% (2011) → 16.1% (2023), 496 mn lifted out; projected 14.2% (2026) → 12.1% (2028)
Extreme poverty ($3/day) 27.1% (2011) → 2.6% (2023)
Upper-middle-income line ($8.30/day) about 80% below it in 2023
  • Rural 19.3% vs urban 8.6% (2023). UP to West Bengal belt = about 57% of India's poor.
  • Employment up about 134 mn (2017–2023), nearly twice the working-age population growth.

12/13★ Must-learnUNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026: The Point of Return

In plain words

A United Nations environment report says the world can no longer realistically keep warming within the safest limit, and that countries must cut pollution quickly. It shows how far present policies fall short.

  • 1.5°C with no/limited overshoot is no longer achievable; return to 1.5°C by 2100 still possible via deep cuts + CO₂ removal (about 320 Gt CO₂ to remove and store).
  • Warming by 2100: current policies 2.8°C; commitments met 2.6°C; plus net-zero pledges 2.1°C.
  • Needed cuts vs baseline: 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035, 69% by 2040; about 6% a year (2025–2035).

13/13★ Must-learnGlobal Hunger Index (GHI) 2026

In plain words

The Global Hunger Index scores countries on how much hunger and malnutrition they have, and India is in the "serious" group. It matters because it shows India still has a lot of child malnutrition compared with other countries in South Asia.

  • India 100th of 122 countries, score 24.1 = ‘serious’ (tied with Ethiopia); in the serious category since 2012; score 25.8 in 2018.
  • India: undernourishment 9.8%, child stunting 29.3%, child wasting 19.0% (highest in South Asia). Four indicators: undernourishment, child wasting, child stunting, child mortality; 0 = best, 100-point scale.
  • South Asia ranks: Sri Lanka 53rd, Nepal 72nd, Bangladesh 84th, Pakistan 106th, Afghanistan 108th. Highest score: Somalia 47.0. Global score 18.1 (moderate). Report: No Security without Food Security (Welthungerhilfe, Helvetas, IFHV).
  • Bands: ≤9.9 low; 10–19.9 moderate; 20–34.9 serious; 35–49.9 alarming; 50+ extremely alarming.
Exam angle

What was India's rank and category in the GHI 2026?

Remember

India 100th/122, score 24.1, serious; Pakistan 106th.

Growth, outlook and data releases

1/72★ Must-learnGross GST collection, August 2026: ₹1,99,853 crore

In plain words

This is the total tax the government collected from the Goods and Services Tax in August. It is a quick health check of how much buying and selling is happening in the economy.

  • Gross GST (Goods and Services Tax) collection Aug 2026 → ₹1,99,853 crore
  • YoY growth 14.8% → nearly ₹2 trillion
  • MoM: lower than ₹2.11 lakh crore in July 2026
  • Data released by Ministry of Finance

2/72★ Must-learnJCR upgrades India’s sovereign rating to A-

In plain words

A Japanese rating agency raised its opinion of how safely India repays its debts by one step. A better rating usually lowers the cost of borrowing from abroad.

  • Japan Credit Rating Agency (JCR) → India’s long-term FC and LC issuer ratings BBB+ → A- (one notch), outlook Stable
  • Country ceiling also raised one notch to A
  • First return to the ‘A’ category in 35+ years
  • Last ‘A’ rating: Moody’s A2 in 1988, lost in the 1990–91 Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis
Exam angle

Which agency upgraded India to A- in Sept 2026, and when was India last rated in the A category?

Remember

JCR = Japan agency; BBB+ → A-; ceiling → A.

3/72★ Must-learnFY27 GDP growth forecasts raised (Moody’s, ADB, S&P, Fitch, OECD)

In plain words

Several global agencies raised their guess for how fast India's economy will grow this year, because it handled the Middle East conflict better than expected. Such forecasts shape investor confidence in India.

  • ADB (Asian Development Outlook, Sept 2026): FY27 7.0% (from 6.6% in July); FY28 7.1% (cut from 7.3%); driver: Q1 FY27 growth 7.8%
  • Moody’s: FY27 7.0% (from 6.0%) as India proved more resilient to the Middle East conflict; retains Baa3, stable
  • S&P Global: 7.0% (from 6.6%), warns of H2 moderation; Fitch: 6.9% (from 6.4%); OECD: 7.1% (↑ 80 bps)
Remember

ADB 7.0 | Moody’s 7.0 | S&P 7.0 | Fitch 6.9 | OECD 7.1.

4/72★ Must-learnCurrent Account Deficit (CAD) widens to $4.2 bn in Q1 FY27

In plain words

India spent more foreign money than it earned from the world, and the gap grew a little. The card also shows how foreign investment and reserves moved in the same period.

  • Reserve Bank of India (RBI) BoP data, April–June 2026
  • CAD: USD 4.2 bn = 0.5% of GDP (Q1 FY26: USD 3.4 bn = 0.4%)
  • Foreign Direct Investment (FDI): USD 6.1 bn (USD 5.2 bn a year ago)
  • External Commercial Borrowings (ECB): USD 1.0 bn (USD 5.5 bn a year ago)
  • Forex reserves (BoP basis, excl. valuation): ↓ USD 8.1 bn (vs ↑ USD 4.5 bn)
  • Forex reserves (nominal, incl. valuation): ↓ USD 22.5 bn (vs ↑ USD 29.8 bn)

5/72☆ Good to knowRBI Quarterly BSR-2 on deposits, June 2026

  • Basic Statistical Return (BSR)-2: quarterly, branch-wise data from Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs), excl. Regional Rural Banks
  • Covers type of deposits, sector-wise ownership, age-wise individual deposits, maturity, size and rate-range of term deposits, number of employees
  • Deposits with SCBs grew 11.5% YoY (11.3% a year ago)
  • Household sector largest holder: 58.8% of deposits

6/72☆ Good to knowMutual funds’ overseas equity holdings up 37.5% in FY26

  • RBI data: MF overseas equity holdings ↑ 37.5% YoY → ₹93,602 crore (March-end 2026)
  • Cause: mark-to-market gains in global rally + investor interest in overseas schemes
  • US share 63.5% (₹59,403 crore); Luxembourg ↑ 39%; Ireland ↑ 31.6%
  • MF foreign liabilities ↑ 3.3% to USD 31.5 bn; overseas assets ↑ 23.9% to USD 10.2 bn
  • AMC (Asset Management Company) foreign liabilities ↑ 18.1% to USD 8.7 bn; Japan + Canada ≈ 80% of FDI in AMCs

7/72☆ Good to knowIndia becomes Asia’s 4th-largest REIT market

  • Overtakes Hong Kong by market value for the first time (Cushman & Wakefield analysis)
  • Japan USD 101.4 bn → Singapore 76.7 bn → Chinese mainland 32.1 bn → India → Hong Kong 17.4 bn
  • REIT = Real Estate Investment Trust

8/72★ Must-learnIndia’s forex reserves hit record $785.7 bn

In plain words

The country's savings of foreign currency and gold reached the highest level ever. A big cushion like this helps India handle shocks and keeps the rupee steadier.

  • Week ended 4 Sept 2026: ↑ record $44.9 bn to $785.706 bn (all-time high)
  • India is the 4th-largest holder after China, Japan, Switzerland
  • Components: Foreign Currency Assets (largest), Gold, SDRs (IMF-created Special Drawing Rights), Reserve Position with IMF

9/72☆ Good to knowAgriculture and allied sectors grow 3.6% in Q1 FY27

  • MoSPI (Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation) data: GVA growth 3.6% (Q1 FY26: 4.4%; ↓ 0.8 pp)
  • Likely cause: lower animal husbandry/livestock output due to floods and extreme heat in April–June 2026

10/72★ Must-learnCentre cuts FY27 gross market borrowing to ₹15.99 lakh crore

In plain words

The government decided to borrow less from the bond market than planned this year. Less borrowing means less pressure on interest rates and a smaller strain on its budget.

  • Borrowing reduced by ₹1.2 lakh crore from budget estimate ₹17.2 lakh crore
  • Exact total ₹15,99,506 cr; H2 plan ₹7,86,000 cr (incl. ₹15,000 cr Sovereign Green Bonds) via 23 weekly auctions; tenors 3, 5, 7, 10, 15, 30, 40, 50 yrs; greenshoe ₹2,000 cr; H2 WMA limit ₹50,000 cr
  • FY27 fiscal deficit target 4.3% of GDP

11/72☆ Good to knowHSBC India Manufacturing PMI falls to 52.8 in August

12/72★ Must-learnGDP Q1 FY2026-27: real growth 7.8%

In plain words

This is the official report on how much the economy grew in the first three months of the financial year. The card also explains the difference between the value of everything produced and the value added by producers.

Exam angle

Remember

13/72☆ Good to knowGDP concepts from the PIB explainer

  • Double deflation: output and inputs deflated separately; real GVA = real output − real intermediate consumption (production side; IMF-preferred)
  • If input prices rise faster than output prices the implicit GVA deflator can turn negative — not a fall in manufacturing prices
  • Implicit GDP deflator = (GDP at current prices ÷ GDP at constant prices) × 100; derived from 300+ item deflators, so need not track CPI/WPI
  • GDP discrepancy = balancing item between production and expenditure approaches; large nominal–real gap in mining can just reflect mineral price rises

42/72★ Must-learnGovt notifies zero charges on UPI transactions up to ₹2,000

In plain words

The government said small digital payments will stay free of charge. It keeps everyday payments cheap for people and shows how fees apply on larger shop payments.

  • Notified by Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance; legal basis Section 10A, Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007
  • UPI (Unified Payments Interface) transactions up to ₹2,000: no direct/indirect charges → keeps ≈ 96% of UPI volume zero-charge
  • Person-to-Person (P2P) UPI stays free
  • P2M (Person-to-Merchant) above ₹2,000 → MDR 0.4%; for ₹75,000 and above, capped at ₹300 per transaction
  • MDR (Merchant Discount Rate) = fee a merchant pays to accept digital payments
  • All RuPay debit card payments exempt from charges; no blanket MDR on merchants
  • Flat ₹5 MDR for transactions above ₹2,000 in railways, telecom, insurance, fuel, agri inputs; capital markets (MFs, brokers) 0.02% capped ₹300; small merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh/month by UPI QR keep zero MDR
  • MDR applies to only ≈4% of merchant transactions; 5% of MDR collections go to a small-merchant UPI fund; MDR is not a government tax
  • MDR on UPI payments above ₹2,000 attracts 18% GST
  • UPI & Services Steering Committee (22 members) examining MDR: led by NPCI CEO Dilip Asbe and Executive Director Sohini Rajola
Exam angle

Up to what amount are UPI transactions made free of charge, and what is the MDR above it?

Remember

Free ≤ ₹2,000; MDR 0.4%; cap ₹300 from ₹75,000.

66/72★ Must-learnIRDAI proposes overhaul of insurance distribution framework

In plain words

The insurance regulator wants a simpler way for insurers to sell policies, with limits on how much they can spend and clearer rules to stop wrong selling. The aim is to make insurance cheaper and fairer for buyers.

  • Simpler 3-tier distribution architecture, lower Expense of Management (EoM) limits, revised commissions, tougher mis-selling safeguards

1/35★ Must-learnRBI launches three surveys for monetary policy inputs

In plain words

The central bank started three surveys asking households how they expect prices to move and how confident they feel. The answers help it decide on interest rates.

  • IESH: Inflation Expectations Survey of Households → 19 cities
  • UCCS: Urban Consumer Confidence Survey → 19 cities
  • RCCS: Rural Consumer Confidence Survey → 31 states and UTs (current perception + one-year-ahead view)
  • Purpose: inputs on inflation expectations and consumer confidence for monetary policy

2/35☆ Good to knowRBI lets urban co-op banks buy IDPIC shares for membership

  • Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) may acquire equity of Indian Digital Payment Intelligence Corporation (IDPIC) where needed for membership
  • Added to the list of permitted membership investments (para 107(1) amended)

3/35★ Must-learnRBI draft SOP: temporary debit hold on money-mule and cyber-fraud accounts

In plain words

The central bank proposed a clear step-by-step rule for banks when an account is suspected of being used for fraud. Banks would put a temporary hold on the suspicious payment instead of freezing everything, and the customer gets time to explain.

  • Draft Reserve Bank of India (Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions; effective 1 April 2027 or earlier
  • Applies to commercial banks and all urban co-operative banks; not to nodal, pool, escrow or special-purpose accounts
  • Bank places a Temporary Debit Hold on a suspected money-mule transaction (or entire account) → max 60 days (unless law enforcement says otherwise)
  • Account holder notified immediately (digital) or by end of next day, with reasons, removal process and officer contact
  • Suspected transaction threshold ₹1,000+; holder gets 20 days to explain; bank decides within 10 days of explanation, or 30 days from hold if none
  • Banks need technology to detect fraud, link with National Cybercrime Reporting Portal’s Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System, and a grievance mechanism
Remember

Hold max 60 days; explain in 20 days; decide in 10 (or 30 if silent).

4/35★ Must-learnRBI revises market-risk capital framework (trading book vs banking book)

In plain words

Banks keep some investments to trade quickly and others to hold for long. New rules stop banks from moving items between the two just to need less safety capital, and they also adjust how foreign currency holdings are counted.

  • Effective 1 April 2027; aligns with revised Basel III; stops arbitrage between trading and banking books
  • Reclassification that lowers capital → bank holds the difference as an additional capital surcharge
  • Banks may exclude structural (non-dealing) FX positions from Net Open Position (NOP): overseas subsidiaries, joint ventures, associates, branches, IFSC Banking Units and Offshore Banking Units in SEZs; kept at least 6 months
  • Specific-risk capital charge 12% on certain non-equity capital instruments, regardless of rating
  • Debt MFs/ETFs with ≥90% debt AUM → look-through to underlying; below 90% → treated like equity; CDMDF contributions 9% charge
Debt MF / ETF typeCapital treatment
≥90% AUM in debt + disclosure/valuation norms metAssessed on underlying debt securities
<90% in debt, or norms not metTreated like equity
CDMDF (Corporate Debt Market Development Fund) contributions, certain others9% capital charge

5/35★ Must-learnRBI: bulk deposit rate disclosure from 1 October 2026

In plain words

From this date, banks must publish their deposit rates every morning, including rates for very large deposits. This lets customers compare banks and prevents hidden or unfair rates.

  • Banks must disclose deposit rates, including bulk deposits, in advance on their website
  • Daily disclosure by 10:00 AM each business day; grace of 10 minutes → latest 10:10 AM
  • Banks may offer differential bulk-deposit rates based on the differential run-off rate under the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) framework
  • Run-off rate = % of deposits/funding expected to be withdrawn in a 30-day stress period

6/35★ Must-learnRBI keeps 9-month export-realisation limit; withdraws 15-month relaxation

In plain words

Exporters must bring the money they earn from selling abroad back to India within a fixed time. The central bank kept this time limit and cancelled an extra relaxation, with a longer period only when the sale is in rupees.

  • Exporters must realise and repatriate export proceeds within 9 months
  • Applies to goods, services and goods sent to overseas warehouses (clock runs from sale for warehouse exports)
  • FEMA amendment: 12 months if exports are invoiced/settled in Indian rupees
  • Earlier repatriation raises dollar supply in the domestic forex market

7/35★ Must-learnRBI fixes H2 FY27 Ways and Means Advances limit at ₹50,000 crore

In plain words

The central bank gave the government a short-term overdraft limit for the second half of the year. It covers gaps when government spending comes before its income.

  • Period Oct 2026 – Mar 2027; WMA = temporary assistance to the Centre for receipt–payment mismatches
  • Fresh market loan floatation may be initiated at 75% utilisation = ₹37,500 crore

17/35★ Must-learnDemat 2.0: SEBI pilot for tokenised corporate bonds

In plain words

The market regulator is testing bonds that exist as digital tokens instead of paper or ordinary electronic entries. This could make buying, holding and settling bonds faster, and the first such bonds have already been sold.

  • Announced at Global Fintech Fest 2026; bond created as a digital token on a distributed ledger (DLT), ledger owned by depositories
  • Covers issuance, holding, trading and settlement; linked to RBI’s wholesale CBDC (e₹) via the Unified Market Interface
  • First tokenised corporate bonds on NSE Electronic Bidding Platform (EBP):
    • Issuers REC Ltd (₹500 crore, first) and Larsen & Toubro (₹500 crore) → ₹1,000 crore total
    • REC pilot issue under SEBI Regulatory Sandbox: coupon 7.30%, tenor 1 year 9 months, pay-in, allotment and listing on the same day
  • IIFL Finance: first non-PSU NBFC tokenised bond, ₹25 crore, bidding on Metropolitan Stock Exchange of India
  • A tokenised bond stays a normal corporate bond (issuer, coupon, maturity, legal obligations); only its representation is a token on a ledger, not a cryptocurrency
Remember

First tokenised bonds: REC + L&T = ₹500 + ₹500 crore.

18/35★ Must-learnSEBI revises commodity derivatives position limits and penalties

In plain words

The regulator changed how much of a farm commodity one trader may hold and how much penalty a trading member pays for crossing the limit. The idea is to make trading easier while still stopping anyone from controlling prices.

  • Penalty per day: violation over 2% of limit → 2% of (excess × closing price) or ₹2,00,000, whichever lower; up to 2% → ₹10,000 cap; proceeds go to exchange Investor Protection Fund; >3 instances in a month → one-day square-off mode / double penalty
  • “Broad commodity” = non-sensitive agri commodity meeting either deliverable supply ≥ 10 lakh MT or value ≥ ₹5,000 crore (5-yr average); earlier both were needed
  • Client-level limits for agri commodities doubled: Broad 2%, Narrow 1%, Sensitive 0.5% of deliverable supply
  • Narrow → Broad: keeps 1% for 1 year, may later go to 2%
  • Penalty: violation >2% → lower of calculated or ₹2 lakh; ≤2% → lower of calculated or ₹10,000
  • More than 3 violations in a month → 1-day square-off mode + additional penalty

16/32★ Must-learnUK recognises India’s Carbon Credit Trading Scheme for carbon-tax relief

In plain words

Britain agreed that India's carbon trading scheme counts for relief from its carbon tax on imports. This protects Indian exporters from paying twice for the pollution caused by making their goods.

  • Qualifies for pricing relief under UK’s carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM); to cut burden on Indian exporters; Bureau of Energy Efficiency funds scheme through fees
  • EU CBAM: carbon tax on carbon-intensive imports (steel, cement, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity, hydrogen); part of “Fit for 55”; fully implemented 1 Jan 2026
  • India reserved third-party rights in the Russia–EU CBAM dispute at WTO (World Trade Organization: est. 1 Jan 1995, HQ Geneva, Marrakesh Agreement 1994)

17/32★ Must-learnIndia–MERCOSUR: talks to expand the Preferential Trade Agreement

In plain words

India and a South American trading bloc are talking about widening an existing trade deal that gives lower taxes on selected goods. A new rule also accepts electronic certificates that show where goods are made.

  • PTA signed 2004, in force 1 June 2009; tariff concessions on 450 lines (India) and 452 (MERCOSUR)
  • Protocol: electronic Certificates of Origin have equal validity (amends Article 16, Annex III)
  • MERCOSUR (Southern Common Market): est. 1991, secretariat Montevideo; founders Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay; Venezuela (joined 2012, suspended); Bolivia full member July 2024

18/32★ Must-learnIndia joins IAEA’s ATLAS initiative for nuclear power at sea

In plain words

India joined a global effort to study small nuclear reactors that could power ships and floating power plants. It is meant to prepare safe rules for using nuclear energy at sea.

  • Atomic Technologies Licensed for Applications at Sea (ATLAS): launched Washington DC, Sept 2026; Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) for shipping and floating nuclear plants
  • IAEA: est. 1957, HQ Vienna, 182 members, DG Rafael Grossi

19/32★ Must-learnG20: Energy Abundance Ministerial and summit dates

In plain words

Energy ministers of the world's largest economies agreed on goals such as getting energy to every home. The card also gives the date and place of the next leaders' summit.

  • India endorsed consensus on household energy access, faster infrastructure approvals, water reuse, resilient critical-mineral supply chains
  • 2026 G20 Leaders’ Summit: 14–15 Dec 2026, Trump National Doral, Miami; UK confirms Manchester for 2027
  • G20: est. 1999 after the 1997–98 Asian crisis; 19 countries + EU + AU (AU permanent member since 2023 New Delhi Summit); ≈85% of global GDP

20/32★ Must-learnInaugural P4M Summit at the UN

In plain words

Countries that support working together through the United Nations held the first meeting of a new group. India helped lead it and pointed to shared problems such as fuel, food, fertiliser and money.

  • 21 Sept 2026, UN HQ New York (UNGA 81 sidelines); P4M = Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace and Prosperity
  • India co-sponsor (EAM S. Jaishankar) with Australia, Barbados, Brazil, Canada, EU, Kenya
  • Jaishankar flagged the “4F” crisis: Fuel, Food, Fertilizer, Finance

21/32★ Must-learnG4 foreign ministers press for UN Security Council reform

In plain words

Four countries that all want a permanent seat on the main United Nations security body met to push for reform. They argue the council no longer reflects today's world.

  • UNSC: 15 members; P5 (US, UK, France, Russia, China) with veto; 10 non-permanent elected for 2 years

19/75★ Must-learnDecentralised Grain Storage Plan in the cooperative sector

In plain words

This plan builds grain stores and processing units at village cooperative societies. Farmers can then store crops near home instead of travelling far or selling in a hurry.

  • Pilot launched 31 May 2023; storage, processing, procurement at PACS (Primary Agricultural Credit Societies) level; implementing agency NCDC (National Cooperative Development Corporation)
  • Converges AIF (Agriculture Infrastructure Fund), AMI, SMAM and PMFME; silo sizes 50, 100, 200 MT
  • AMI subsidy 25% → 33.33%; margin money 20% → 10%; with 3% AIF interest subvention effective rate = 1%
  • Pilot: 11 PACS in 11 states (9,750 MT); by July 2026: 1,012 PACS identified, godowns done in 313 (1.80 lakh tonnes)

    • Painted Haveli Towns of Shekhawati (Rajasthan)
  • Later addition (5 entries) → total 78:
    • Bagh Cave Paintings (Buddhist murals)
    • Group of Temples of the Chambal Valley
    • Udaigiri Caves (Gupta-era)
    • Ginnorgarh (tribal legacy)
    • Sites of Satyagraha: serial transnational proposal with South Africa
  • Rangpur–Sivasagar = capital of the Ahom dynasty (ruled ≈600 years; founder Chaolung Sukapha, 1228 CE → 1826)
  • Charaideo Moidams (Ahom royal burial mounds) inscribed 2024 = India’s 43rd World Heritage Site
Remember

73 → 78 is two steps (4 sites, then 5 entries).

India completed four years of its programme to bring cheetahs back from other countries. The card shows how many cheetahs now live in India and where.

  • Population 52 (32 born in India); 49 at Kuno, 3 at Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary

Permission to build ports and dredge now stays valid for longer. This reduces the need to reapply again and again for big sea projects.

This is a very rare large bird that lives mainly in Rajasthan's desert. The card lists the legal protection it has, which shows how close it is to disappearing.

India launched a satellite that takes pictures of the earth from a very high orbit. The images help farmers and disaster teams get timely information.

India and France are building a satellite that measures heat on the earth's surface. It helps spot water shortage in crops and manage natural resources.

Indices, rankings and reports

5/8★ Must-learnGlobal Gender Gap Index 2026 (WEF): India 131st

In plain words

This yearly report compares how equally women and men are treated in 145 countries. India stayed at the same position, so it did not move up or down.

  • World Economic Forum, 20th edition, 145 economies; 4 dimensions: economic participation, education, health & survival, political empowerment
  • Top: Iceland (17th year), Finland, Norway, Namibia, UK; bottom: Chad (145th), Iran, Pakistan, DR Congo, Algeria
  • India: rank 131st (unchanged), score 0.645 (64.5%) vs global 69.2% (↑ 0.4 pp)
  • India sub-indices: economic 41.2%, education 96.6%, health 95.6%, political 24.5% (lowest score, but India’s best-ranked sub-index: 67th globally); labour-force parity 44.1%
  • In South Asia India trails Bangladesh (79th), Maldives (119th), Nepal (120th), Bhutan (121st), Sri Lanka (129th)
Exam angle

What is India’s rank in the Global Gender Gap Index 2026, and which sub-index gives India its best global rank?

Remember

131st, score 0.645; political empowerment has the best rank (67th) though a low score (24.5%); education has the highest score (96.6%).

September 2026 · Section 8Government Schemes and Static Links14 items · 5 ★ must-learn · 9 ☆ good to know

Schemes at a glance

1/14★ Must-learnModified UDAN scheme: MoUs with 22 states

In plain words

The government plans to carry on its scheme for cheaper flights to small towns, and will sign agreements with many states. It will build more airports and helipads in remote and hilly places.

  • Ministry of Civil Aviation to sign MoUs with 22 states for next phase of Regional Connectivity Scheme UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik; original launch Oct 2016)
  • Cabinet-approved for 10 years (FY27–FY36), outlay ₹28,840 crore; 100 airports from unserved airstrips + 200 helipads in hilly, remote, island, aspirational regions

2/14☆ Good to knowMission for Cotton Productivity

  • Union Cabinet outlay ₹5,659 crore, 2026–27 to 2030–31
  • Cotton (“White Gold”): India first in area (114.84 lakh ha), second in production and consumption; top states Maharashtra, Gujarat, Telangana, Karnataka

3/14★ Must-learnShipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme (SBFAS) 2.0

In plain words

The government extended and enlarged its scheme to help Indian shipyards build ships at home. More local shipbuilding means less dependence on foreign yards.

  • Extended up to 2036 with revised outlay ₹24,736 crore to support domestic shipbuilding

4/14★ Must-learnEmergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0

In plain words

The government approved a new round of a guarantee scheme that helps small businesses and airlines borrow emergency money from banks. The government promises to cover most of the loan if it is not repaid.

  • Approved 5 May 2026; implemented by NCGTC (National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company); credit up to ₹2.55 lakh crore; valid till 31 March 2027 or limit reached
  • Borrowers: MSMEs, eligible non-MSMEs, scheduled passenger airlines; guarantee 100% (MSMEs) / 90% (non-MSMEs, airlines); no guarantee fee
  • Support: up to 20% of peak Q4 FY26 working capital (cap ₹100 crore) for MSME/non-MSME; airlines up to ₹1,500 crore (equity needed beyond ₹1,000 crore)
  • Rate: EBLR (MSMEs) or MCLR + up to 0.75%, ceiling 9%; NBFC loans max 13%; tenor 5 yrs + 1-yr moratorium (airlines 7 + 2)
  • Status 20 Aug 2026: 6,73,979 guarantees, ₹2,50,024 crore; MSMEs 97.3% by number
  • History: ECLGS started 2020 (Aatmanirbhar Bharat); phases 1.0–4.0 issued 1.19 crore guarantees worth ₹3.68 lakh crore; closed 31 March 2023

5/14★ Must-learnVibrant Villages Programme (VVP)

In plain words

This programme develops villages along the border with better roads, power and services so people stay and the border areas feel secure. It has two parts that cover different states.

  • Launched 2023; nodal Ministry of Home Affairs; ₹11,639 crore for 2,616+ border villages
  • VVP-I: Centrally Sponsored, ₹4,800 crore, 662 villages in Arunachal, Himachal, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, Ladakh; launched 10 April 2023 at Kibithoo
  • VVP-II: Central Sector, ₹6,839 crore (FY25–FY29), 1,954 villages in 15 states + 2 UTs including Rajasthan; approved 2 April 2025, launched 20 Feb 2026 at Nathanpur, Assam
  • Replaces sunset-phase BADP (Border Area Development Programme, 1986-87); India’s land border >15,000 km (Bangladesh 4,096.7 km, China 3,488 km, Pakistan 3,323 km)

  • Mission Poshan 2.0 (Budget 2021-22) merges POSHAN Abhiyaan (March 2018), Anganwadi Services/ICDS and Scheme for Adolescent Girls
  • Poshan Tracker launched 1 March 2021; 13.99 lakh Anganwadi Centres, 8.94 crore beneficiaries (31 July 2026); PMMVY completes 10 years

  • PM-AJAY merges PMAGY + SCA to SCSP + BJRCY (since 2021-22)

9/14☆ Good to knowDDU-GKY 2.0 and PM-AJAY

  • DDU-GKY (launched 25 Sep 2014, under DAY-NRLM): rural youth 15–35; SC/ST 50%, women 33%, PwD 5%; 2.0 notified May 2025; min training 576 hours; placement min 6 months
  • DDU-GKY: 18.47 lakh trained, 12.43 lakh placed; Budget 2026-27 ₹750 cr; Roshni (LWE/aspirational districts), Himayat (J&K, Ladakh)
  • RSETI: 647 institutes, trained 63.47 lakh since 2009; age 18–50
  • PM-AJAY: 100% centrally sponsored, from 2021-22; 3 components: Adarsh Gram (47,243 villages), Grants-in-Aid (₹1,730 cr+), Hostels (785 done); village criterion 40% SC and 500+ population

10/14★ Must-learnAB PM-JAY and ABDM at 8 years

In plain words

The main health insurance scheme for poor families completed eight years, and the card shows how many people have used it. It also covers the digital health ID system and progress on literacy for adults.

  • AB PM-JAY launched 23 Sep 2018; ₹5 lakh per family; 13.25 crore admissions worth ₹2.03 lakh crore; budget 2026-27 ₹9,500 cr; SECC 2011 based
  • ABDM (Sept 2021): 97.61 crore ABHA IDs, 119.95 crore records (17 Sep 2026)
  • ULLAS/NILP: target 5 crore (2022-27), outlay ₹1,037.90 cr; fully literate: Ladakh, Mizoram, Goa, Tripura, HP, Chandigarh, A&N, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, J&K; PM POSHAN 11.20 crore students
  • Literacy: 74.04% (2011); PLFS 2025 81.1%

  • Bulk Drugs (2020): ₹6,940 cr, 41 products; Pharmaceuticals (2021): ₹15,000 cr; Medical Devices (2020): ₹3,420 cr, 4 segments, 5% incentive on incremental sales for 5 years

  • NHPR mobile app; NHCX payer implementation guide; Secure Data Environment (NHA + IISc Bengaluru); auto-adjudication framework for PM-JAY
  • ABDM model districts: Bihar, Ladakh, DNH; National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission (2023, goal 2047); ELDERLINE 14567 (1 Oct 2021, under AVYAY)

13/14☆ Good to knowNSFDC Udyam Nidhi Yojana and NFSC

  • NSFDC (SC corporation): UNY loans to projects up to ₹5 lakh, 90% (₹4.5 lakh); interest 5% to channel, beneficiary pays 13% (co-ops)/15% (SFBs); 5 years incl. 3-month moratorium
  • NFSC: since 2005-06, 2,000 fellowships/yr (1,500 humanities + 500 science); NSFDC is central nodal agency
  • India Cine Hub: NFDC single-window portal (NFDC est. 1975)

14/14☆ Good to knowPRIP second call

Growth, outlook and data releases

1/27★ Must-learnRBI gold holdings and deployment of reserves (end-March 2026)

In plain words

The Reserve Bank now keeps more than three-quarters of its gold inside India. Gold also forms a larger share of the country's foreign exchange reserves than six months earlier.

  • Half-Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves
  • Gold: 880.52 tonnes; 680.05 tonnes held in India (77.23%; 59.2% a year ago); 197.67 tonnes with Bank of England and BIS; 2.80 tonnes as gold deposits
  • Gold share in total reserves (dollar value): 13.92% (end-September 2025) → 16.70% (end-March 2026)
  • Foreign currency assets $552 billion: 84.31% in securities; 8.48% deposits with other central banks and BIS; 7.21% deposits with commercial banks overseas
Exam angle

How much gold does RBI hold, and what share is in India? (880.52 tonnes; 77.23%)

2/27★ Must-learnForex reserves, FDI and RBI dollar sales

In plain words

India's foreign exchange reserves fell in mid-May after rising the week before. Over the last financial year the Reserve Bank sold more dollars than it bought, and gross foreign direct investment reached a record.

  • Reserves: week ended 8 May +$6.295 bn to $696.988 bn; week ended 15 May -$8.094 bn to $688.894 bn
  • Reserves = foreign currency assets + gold + SDRs + reserve position in IMF; foreign currency assets are the largest part
  • RBI in spot forex market, 2025-26: bought $142 bn, sold $195 bn; net sale $53.13 bn, highest in a financial year
  • Gross FDI 2025-26: record $94.53 bn (+17%); net FDI $7.65 bn (2024-25: $959 million)
  • LRS outward remittances 2025-26: $28.9 bn (-2%; 2024-25: $29.6 bn); limit $250,000 per financial year; scheme began in 2004
  • Outward FDI, April 2026: $5.6 bn (-10.8% from $6.33 bn a year ago; March 2026: $5.08 bn); components: equity, loans, guarantees
  • March 2026: ECB filings halved to $5.43 bn; overseas travel spending $1.09 bn of total LRS $2.59 bn
Exam angle

RBI's net dollar sale in 2025-26? ($53.13 bn)

Remember

Gross FDI $94.53 bn is the record; net FDI is only $7.65 bn.

6/27★ Must-learnFiscal and statistical reforms for states

In plain words

States that manage their debt and borrowing well can earn extra central money for capital spending. States are also asked to update the base year used to measure their economies.

  • SASCI incentive pool of ₹3,000 crore for fiscally disciplined states: debt management 50%, borrowing discipline 30%, transparency 20%
  • States to adopt benchmark issuance, buybacks or switches, and a medium-term debt strategy (MTDS) with RBI, approved by state cabinet and published by 15 December 2026
  • Borrowing calendar deviation capped at 10%; Q4 borrowing at most 30% of annual issuance; large states up to ₹250 crore, mid-sized ₹200 crore, small and NE ₹100-150 crore
  • MoSPI: states to move GSDP base year to 2022-23 (from 2011-12), in line with national accounts
Exam angle

Highest weight in the SASCI fiscal incentive? (debt management, 50%)

8/27★ Must-learnStatistics reforms: new IIP series and GDP release date

In plain words

The statistics office is moving the index of factory output to a newer base year with a larger list of products. It also moved the yearly release date of full-year growth figures to early June.

  • IIP base year 2011-12 → 2022-23; new series from 1 June 2026; TAC chaired by Dr Mridul K. Saggar (IIM Kozhikode)
  • New IIP basket: 1,042 products in 463 item groups; NIC-2025; adds minor minerals, rare earth minerals, gas supply, water supply, sewerage and waste; separate indices for renewable and non-renewable electricity; released with 28 days' lag
  • GDP provisional estimates and Q4 estimates moved from last working day of May to 7 June each year (2026: 5 June)
  • GSVA guideline with base 2022-23 for states (Sub-Committee on Regional Accounts, Prof. Ravindra H. Dholakia)
Exam angle

New base year of the IIP? (2022-23)

Trade, FDI and tax

9/27★ Must-learnGold, silver and platinum: customs duty raised to 15%

In plain words

The government more than doubled the tax on imported gold and silver to cut such imports and save foreign exchange. It also tightened rules on silver bars and on duty-free gold for jewellery exporters.

  • From 13 May 2026: gold and silver 6% → 15% (basic customs duty 10% + AIDC 5%); platinum 6.4% → 15.4%; also dore, coins, findings
  • Spent catalysts or ash with precious metals: concessional 4.35%
  • Silver bars of 99.9% purity or more moved from "free" to "restricted" import (licence needed)
  • DGFT: duty-free gold under Advance Authorisation capped at 100 kg; next authorisation only after 50% of export obligation is met; physical inspection for first-time applicants
  • India: 2nd largest gold consumer (after China), imports about 90% of its gold; largest silver consumer; gold ore resources Bihar 43%, Rajasthan 24.92%, Karnataka 20%; Karnataka produces 97%
Exam angle

New effective customs duty on gold? (15%: 10% basic duty + 5% AIDC)

Remember

Budget 2024-25 had cut it from 15% to 6%; it is back to 15%.

In plain words

Foreign firms with a small Chinese shareholding can now invest in India without prior government approval. Proposals in some key manufacturing areas from neighbouring countries will be decided within sixty days.

  • Finance Ministry notification under FEMA: overseas firms with Chinese shareholding up to 10% may invest through the automatic route
  • Background: 2020 curbs on FDI from countries sharing a land border with India (Press Note 3)
  • Updated SOP: proposals from China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, Afghanistan in 40 sub-sectors (6 segments: capital goods, electronic components, advanced battery components, polysilicon and wafers, rare earth processing, rare earth magnets) decided within 60 days
  • FDI 2025-26: US overtakes Mauritius as 2nd largest source (equity over $11 bn); Singapore stays first
Exam angle

Chinese shareholding up to what level qualifies for the automatic route? (10%)

13/27★ Must-learnEnergy: renewables, ethanol and fuel standards

In plain words

India ranks third in the world for clean power capacity, and new fuel standards allow petrol with up to thirty per cent ethanol. The government is also pushing local manufacturing for clean energy equipment.

  • Morgan Stanley: India 3rd in installed renewable capacity (after China, US); non-fossil capacity 262.7 GW, above 50% of total
  • Domestic solar module capacity 74 GW (March 2025); cell capacity 9 → 25 GW; FY25 module imports about $1.6 bn, 60-80% from China
  • BIS standards: IS 19850:2026 for E22, E25, E27, E30 petrol; IS 18698:2026 for DME-blended LPG
  • Ethanol: about 515 crore litres supplied in first half of ESY 2025-26 against 1,059 crore litres contracted (about 49%); maize the main feedstock
  • Maruti Suzuki unveils India's first flex-fuel WagonR able to run on 100% ethanol (E100)
  • Power Ministry: local content for HVDC substations phased: 30% by FY28 → 40% FY30 → 50% FY32 → 60% FY35
  • SECI tender for 5 lakh tonnes a year of green methanol under SIGHT (National Green Hydrogen Mission): electrolysers ₹4,440 crore, green hydrogen ₹13,050 crore

Which standard covers E22 to E30 petrol? (IS 19850:2026)

RBI

1/20★ Must-learnFEMA (Authorised Persons) Regulations, 2026

In plain words

The Reserve Bank issued new rules on who may deal in foreign exchange and what each type of dealer may do. No new licences will be given to stand-alone money changers, and dealers must meet minimum net worth and turnover levels.

  • Notification dated 30 April 2026; in force from Gazette publication on 6 May 2026; applications through PRAVAAH portal to the RBI regional office
  • Fresh authorisation only in three categories; no fresh FFMC applications (only those already under process)
CategoryWhoPermitted activitiesMinimum net worth
AD Category-IBank licensed by RBIAny current and capital account transaction permissible under FEMA-
AD Category-IIBank or NBFC; or FFMC / Forex Correspondent working at least two years with average annual forex turnover of ₹50 crore in the previous two financial yearsNon-trade current account transactions (not gift and donation); foreign trade up to ₹25 lakh per transaction₹10 crore
AD Category-IIIEntity dealing in forex incidental to its business, or offering innovative products that involve forexAs stated in its authorisation₹2 crore
FFMCExisting ones and pending applicationsBuy foreign currency notes and travellers' cheques; sell them for foreign travel; agent under MTSS₹25 lakh (single branch); ₹50 lakh (multiple branch)
  • Applicant: company under Companies Act 2013; at least 50% of directors and KMPs with qualification and experience in financial services
  • Minimum annual forex turnover (other than banks and NBFCs): AD Category-II ₹50 crore, FFMC ₹10 crore; to be reached within two years, then maintained
  • Net worth shortfall restored within six months; operations to start within six months of authorisation; prior RBI approval for change in management, control or ownership above 50%
  • AD Category-I and II may appoint a Forex Correspondent (FxC) for money changing on a principal-agent model
  • Appeal within 45 calendar days of rejection or revocation; Appellate Authority order within 60 calendar days
Exam angle

Cap on one foreign trade transaction for AD Category-II? (₹25 lakh)

Remember

Net worth: AD Category-II ₹10 crore, AD Category-III ₹2 crore.

2/20★ Must-learnQuarterly profits in CET1 capital: condition removed

In plain words

Banks may count the profit earned during the year towards their core capital every quarter. An older condition tied to provisions for bad loans has been removed.

  • RBI Amendment Directions, 8 May 2026, immediate effect: commercial banks (Fifth Amendment), SFBs (Fourth Amendment), payments banks (Second Amendment)
  • Removed: incremental NPA provisions in any quarter of the previous year must not deviate more than 25% from the four-quarter average
  • Conditions now: quarterly financial statements audited or under limited review; eligible profit by formula
  • EPt = NPt - 0.25 × D × t (EPt: eligible profit up to quarter t; NPt: net profit up to quarter t; D: average dividend paid in the last three financial years; t: 1 to 4)
  • Cumulative net loss up to the quarter-end fully deducted from CET1
Exam angle

What is D in the formula? (average dividend paid in the last three financial years)

3/20★ Must-learnInvestment Fluctuation Reserve (IFR): ended for commercial banks

In plain words

Banks kept a special reserve as a cushion against a fall in the value of their investments. Commercial banks and local area banks no longer need it, while small finance, payments, rural and co-operative banks still do.

  • Commercial banks and LABs: IFR requirement discontinued from 18 May 2026; balance as on 17 May 2026 moved "below the line" to Statutory Reserve, General Reserve or balance of Profit and Loss Account
  • Foreign bank branches: balance goes to statutory reserves kept in Indian books or remittable surplus retained in Indian books
  • IFR: buffer against depreciation in the value of investments
Bank typeIFR rule
Commercial banks, LABsDiscontinued
SFBs, payments banksAt least 2% of AFS and FVTPL (including HFT) portfolio; built from realised gains on sale of investments; transfer from net profit after mandatory appropriations
RRBsAt least 2% of HFT and AFS portfolio
UCBsMinimum 5% of investment portfolio (book value of HFT and AFS); balance above 5% may be drawn down
RCBsNot less than 5% of investments in the Current category
Exam angle

From which date was the IFR discontinued for commercial banks? (18 May 2026)

Remember

2% for SFBs, payments banks and RRBs; 5% for co-operative banks.

4/20★ Must-learnCo-operative bank directors: three-year cooling-off

In plain words

A director who has served ten years in a row on the board of a co-operative bank must stay away for three years before returning to the same board. The rule covers both urban and rural co-operative banks.

  • RBI Governance Amendment Directions 2026 for UCBs and RCBs; immediate effect
  • Continuous tenure of 10 years → re-appointment on the same bank's board (election, co-option or otherwise) only after a cooling-off of 3 years
  • During cooling-off: no association with the bank except as member or customer; may be a director of another bank if eligible
  • Continuous tenure includes service before a break of less than three years; service before a break of three years or more is not counted
  • Banking Laws (Amendment) Act 2025: maximum continuous tenure 8 → 10 years, from 1 August 2025
Exam angle

Cooling-off period for a co-operative bank director after ten continuous years? (three years)

5/20★ Must-learnRBI surplus transfer for 2025-26 (623rd Central Board meeting)

In plain words

The board of the Reserve Bank decided to give the central government its highest ever yearly surplus. It also set more money aside as a buffer against risks.

  • 623rd meeting, Mumbai, 22 May 2026; chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra
  • Surplus to Central Government: ₹2,86,588.46 crore, highest ever (previous year ₹2.68 lakh crore)
  • Contingent Risk Buffer (CRB) kept at 6.5% of balance sheet; revised Economic Capital Framework range 4.5% to 7.5%; transfer to CRB ₹1,09,379.64 crore (previous year ₹44,861.70 crore)
  • Balance sheet +20.61% to ₹91,97,121.08 crore (31 March 2026); gross income +26.42%; expenditure before risk provisions +27.60%
  • Net income before risk provision and transfer to statutory funds: ₹3,95,972.10 crore
Exam angle

At what level is the CRB maintained for 2025-26? (6.5% of the balance sheet)

Remember

CRB range is 4.5% to 7.5%; the level chosen is 6.5%.

6/20★ Must-learnUSD/INR buy/sell swap auction of $5 billion

In plain words

The Reserve Bank buys dollars from banks now and sells them back after three years. This puts rupees into the banking system for that period.

  • Aim: inject long-term rupee liquidity into the banking system
  • Auction on 26 May 2026; tenor 3 years; near leg 29 May 2026, far leg 29 May 2029; minimum bid $10 million, then multiples of $1 million
  • AD Category-I banks sell dollars to RBI and agree to buy back the same amount at the end of the swap
  • Buy/sell swap → RBI buys dollars now, rupee liquidity rises; sell/buy swap → RBI sells dollars now, rupee liquidity falls
  • Terms fixed in advance, so no exchange-rate risk
Exam angle

Tenor of the $5 billion swap? (3 years)

7/20★ Must-learnCountercyclical capital buffer (CCyB) not activated

In plain words

This buffer is extra capital that banks build in good times and use in bad times to keep lending. The Reserve Bank reviewed the indicators and decided not to switch it on now.

  • RBI decision after review and empirical analysis of CCyB indicators
  • Activated when systemic risk from excess credit growth builds up; main indicator: credit-to-GDP gap, used with supplementary indicators
  • Framework set by RBI guidelines in February 2015
  • Two aims: build extra capital in expansion to draw down in stress; curb indiscriminate lending in credit booms
  • Idea came after the 2008 global financial crisis: proposed by GHOS, the oversight body of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision
Exam angle

Main indicator for the CCyB? (credit-to-GDP gap)

8/20★ Must-learnRBI draft: loan recovery conduct and locking of financed phones

In plain words

The Reserve Bank proposed rules on how lenders may recover overdue loans. A lender could restrict a phone bought on loan only after the loan is ninety days overdue and two notices have been sent.

  • Proposed to apply from 1 October 2026
  • Lender may restrict functions of a mobile phone only when the loan financed that device, and only after the account is 90 days past due
  • First notice when the loan is 60 days overdue, giving at least 21 days to pay; second notice of 7 days before any restriction
  • Wrongful blocking or delay in restoring: compensation of ₹250 per hour
  • Recovery agents: certification through IIBF or affiliated institutes; borrower told before a recovery visit and when the agency is changed
  • No contact outside 8 am to 7 pm; no abuse, threats, harassing family or shaming on social media; recovery call records kept at least six months
Exam angle

Compensation for wrongful blocking of a device? (₹250 per hour)

Remember

60 days overdue: first notice (21 days); then 7-day notice; restriction only after 90 days past due.

9/20★ Must-learnRBI draft: Pillar 3 disclosures by banks

In plain words

The Reserve Bank proposed that all commercial banks publish their capital and risk figures in common formats. The figures would sit in a separate part of each bank's website and stay there for at least ten years.

  • Draft Capital Adequacy Amendment Directions 2026; comments till 2 June 2026; quarterly disclosures from the quarter ending 30 September 2026
  • Aim: reduce information asymmetry and make banks' risk profiles comparable; Pillar 3 of Basel framework = market discipline through disclosure
  • Applies at the top consolidated level of the banking group; otherwise standalone; covers listed and unlisted banks and foreign bank branches
  • Common templates for capital adequacy, capital composition and RWAs; figures in ₹ crore; board-approved disclosure policy
  • Key statistics each quarter: CET1, total capital, RWAs, leverage ratio, LCR, NSFR
  • Separate "Regulatory Disclosure Section" on the bank's website; archive for at least 10 years
Exam angle

Which Basel pillar deals with market discipline through disclosure? (Pillar 3)

10/20☆ Good to knowRBI: other drafts, actions and announcements

  • Draft on specified non-financial assets (SNFAs): lender may take ownership of immovable collateral once the account is NPA and other recovery routes are found unviable
  • Outward remittance: prior approval removed for tie-ups between AD Category-I banks and non-bank entities offering non-trade current account remittances on digital platforms; AD bank stays responsible for FEMA, KYC and grievance redressal
  • Sarvodaya Co-operative Bank (Mumbai): licence cancelled; banking business stopped from 12 May 2026; DICGC pays up to ₹5 lakh per depositor
  • Penalties: Yes Bank ₹31.80 lakh (no system to use the KYC Identifier of CKYCR); Hinduja Housing Finance ₹1.80 lakh (management change above 30% of directors without prior approval)
  • Primary dealers: each of the 21 PDs to trade at least ₹4 lakh crore of bonds in the financial year, up 48%
  • Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta (Columbia Indian Economy Summit 2026): average state-level per capita income could approach high-income threshold by 2046-47

SEBI

11/20★ Must-learnSEBI: "Significant Indices" and registration of index providers

In plain words

The market regulator defined which stock indices are large enough to be regulated. Firms that provide such indices must register with it.

  • Under SEBI (Index Providers) Regulations 2024; applies to indices of securities listed on Indian exchanges
  • Significant index: daily average cumulative AUM of mutual fund schemes tracking it above ₹20,000 crore for each of the past six months, ending 30 June and 31 December
  • Stays on the list unless below the threshold for three years (six consecutive half-yearly reviews)
  • Providers to apply for registration within six months of the circular; an entity registered with SEBI in another capacity must form a separate legal entity within two years
  • Exempt: providers whose indices RBI has notified as significant or authorised benchmarks
Exam angle

AUM threshold for a significant index? (₹20,000 crore)

12/20★ Must-learnSEBI: nomination in demat accounts and mutual fund folios

In plain words

From September, an investor who opens a demat account or mutual fund folio alone must name a nominee or formally opt out. Up to three nominees are allowed.

  • Circular of 29 May 2026; effective 1 September 2026
  • Single accounts and folios opened on or after that date: nomination mandatory unless an opt-out declaration is given
  • Joint accounts and folios: nomination optional; consent of all joint holders needed to give or change a nominee
  • Up to 3 nominees; shares not specified → equal split; odd lot goes to the first nominee
  • After the investor's death, nominees may continue in the same account or open separate ones
Exam angle

Maximum number of nominees? (3)

13/20★ Must-learnSEBI advisory on AI vulnerability-detection tools; cyber-suraksha.ai

In plain words

The market regulator warned firms that new artificial intelligence tools can find and exploit weak points in computer systems at speed and scale. It formed a task force to examine these risks.

  • Advisory to regulated entities on tools such as Claude Mythos: weak points can be found and exploited at speed and scale
  • Task force cyber-suraksha.ai: MIIs, QRTAs, regulated entities and other stakeholders; to examine AI risks, frame mitigation strategies, share threat intelligence
  • Asked of entities: regular vulnerability assessment and security audits under CSCRF; examine all SOC alerts, including low-priority ones; SOAR playbooks with SIEM; system hardening, least privilege, ZTNA
  • M-SOC (set up by NSE and BSE; 24x7 monitoring): eligible entities not yet on board must expedite onboarding
Exam angle

Name of the SEBI task force on AI cyber risks? (cyber-suraksha.ai)

14/20★ Must-learnSEBI: 30-day lag for price data used in education

In plain words

People who only teach about markets may use share price data that is at least thirty days old. Earlier the data had to be three months old.

  • Uniform lag of 30 days for sharing and using price data for educational purposes; from 1 July 2026
  • Earlier (January 2025): entities solely in education could use only three-month-old data
  • NISM: price data with a one-day lag, only for its simulation lab
  • MIIs and intermediaries to sign legal agreements with those who receive the data
  • An educator must not name a security (or a code name) while indicating future price, advice or recommendation using data of the preceding 30 days
Exam angle

Time lag for price data in educational content? (30 days)

15/20★ Must-learnSEBI proposals: GARUDA for AIFs and open-market buybacks

In plain words

The market regulator proposed a faster route for investment funds to launch schemes. It also proposed time and spending rules for companies that buy back their shares on stock exchanges.

  • GARUDA (Green-Channel: AIF Rollout Upon Document Acknowledgement): AIF scheme may launch within 10 working days of filing its placement memorandum through a merchant banker, unless SEBI objects (now 30 days)
  • Buyback through stock exchanges (additional proposals after PMAC consultation): complete within 66 working days of offer opening; at least 40% of buyback size to be used in the first half of the offer period
  • PMAC had recommended six months and 50%
  • Also proposed: freeze promoters' shares at ISIN level during the buyback; electronic intimation to shareholders within one working day of the public announcement
Exam angle

What does GARUDA allow? (AIF scheme launch within 10 working days of filing)

Remember

GARUDA: 10 working days; buyback: 66 working days.

Other regulators and bodies

18/20★ Must-learnPFRDA: NPS investment, retirement income and annuity exit

In plain words

The pension regulator let pension money be invested in rupee bonds of one more international bank. It also introduced phased withdrawals after retirement and allowed annuity surrender in two cases.

  • Investment: NPS funds may buy rupee bonds of the New Development Bank from 13 May 2026 (earlier only IBRD, IFC, ADB); applies to government and private sector NPS; NDB set up in 2015 by BRICS
  • Retirement Income Scheme (RIS): phased withdrawal through drawdown options; payouts monthly, quarterly or annual; up to age 85 or as chosen at exit; tools: Systematic Payout Rate (SPR), Systematic Unit Redemption (SUR); "RIS Steady" fund lowers equity exposure with age
  • Minimum annuity: non-government subscribers 40% → 20% of corpus; government subscribers 40%
  • Corpus up to ₹8 lakh: full withdrawal; ₹8 lakh to ₹12 lakh: up to ₹6 lakh as lump sum
  • Annuity surrender allowed in two cases: critical illness of annuitant or a family member; policy issued before 24 October 2024 with an explicit surrender clause
Exam angle

Which new issuer's rupee bonds can NPS funds buy? (New Development Bank)

Remember

Minimum annuity: 20% for non-government, 40% for government subscribers.

The pension regulator launched a simple version of the national pension scheme for workers in the informal sector. Local agents get a fixed fee for each person they enrol.

  • Incentive: ₹100 per subscriber enrolled through CSC-VLEs, BCs, Pension Sakhis, PACS; valid till 31 March 2027
  • NPS investments now follow SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations 2015 (replacing PFRDA's 2019 guidelines), immediate effect
  • Motilal Oswal AMC approved as NPS pension fund sponsor; Karnataka Grameena Bank wins PFRDA award (142% of APY target)

Governance, law and institutions

1/12★ Must-learnSupreme Court and judiciary

In plain words

The number of Supreme Court judges was raised to thirty-eight. The court also ruled that emergency trauma care is part of the right to life.

  • Supreme Court strength raised from 34 to 38 judges including the CJI (33 → 37 excluding the CJI), through the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment, amending the 1956 Act
  • SC: trauma care is part of the right to life under Article 21; persons forcibly given acid are "acid attack victims" under the RPwD Act 2016
  • CJI Surya Kant: "One Case One Data" (all court levels in one system) and AI chatbot "Su Sahay" (NIC with SC Registry)
  • Sikkim: India's first paperless judiciary state
  • CIC: BCCI not a public authority under Section 2(h) of RTI Act (reverses 2018 order)

1/10★ Must-learnSpace missions and firsts, May 2026

An Indian start-up launched the first satellite that combines a camera and a radar on one platform. India's second Moon mission also found signs that ice may lie below the surface near the lunar south pole.

  • Sweden joins India's Venus Orbiter Mission (approved 2024; launch planned March 2028); Norway signs MoU with ISRO
  • Red Balloon Aerospace Mission SANA: India's first indigenous super-pressure stratospheric platform (VISTA, about 25 km; Vijayawada); India joins US, France, Japan, China
  • Department of Space approves Common Technical Facilities: Khoraj near Ahmedabad (Gujarat) and Space Vehicles Cluster at Thoothukudi (Tamil Nadu); IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka
  • Karnataka: India's first state-led Centre of Excellence for Space Technology, Bengaluru
  • India's first DORIS ground beacon at IIT Kanpur (French satellite-tracking system)

5/8★ Must-learnWorld Migration Report 2026 (IOM): India top remittance receiver

In plain words

Indians working abroad sent home more money than migrants of any other country. India has been the top receiver of such money since 2010.

  • India received $137.67 bn in 2024: world's top receiver and only country above $100 bn; top since 2010 ($53.48 bn then)
  • Next: Mexico $67.64 bn, Philippines $40.28 bn, France $38.78 bn, Pakistan $34.91 bn; top senders: US $103.18 bn, Saudi Arabia $46.56 bn, Switzerland $40.11 bn
  • International migrants 304 million in 2024 (3.7% of world population; 2.9% in 1990); global remittances $905 bn
  • Largest corridors: Mexico-US first; India-UAE 5th, India-US 6th
  • IOM: HQ Geneva; Director General Amy Pope; 174 member states
Exam angle

Remittances received by India in 2024? ($137.67 bn)

6/8★ Must-learnSRS Statistical Report 2024 and NCRB Crime in India 2024

In plain words

The population survey shows Indian women now have fewer than two children on average, and fewer babies die before their first birthday. Crime records show overall crime falling but cyber crime rising.

  • SRS 2024 (Registrar General of India, MHA): TFR 1.9 (below replacement 2.1 for the fifth year; rural 2.1, urban 1.5); crude death rate 6.4; IMR 25 → 24 (Kerala lowest, 8); under-five mortality 28; sex ratio at birth 918 (2022-24)
  • Share of deaths: motor vehicle accidents 2.9% → 3.2%
  • NCRB Crime in India 2024: cases 62.41 lakh → 58.85 lakh (-6%); crime rate 418.9 per lakh; cyber crime +18% (rate 6.2 → 7.3); crimes against women 4.41 lakh (-1.5%); Telangana highest rate against women
  • Traffic deaths: about 546 a day; most in UP (27,071), Tamil Nadu (20,390), Maharashtra (19,475)
  • NCRB set up 1986 (Tandon Committee, National Police Commission, MHA task force 1985)
Exam angle

India's TFR in SRS 2024? (1.9)

Remember

Replacement level is 2.1; rural TFR is exactly 2.1, urban 1.5.

7/8★ Must-learnEnergy and climate reports

In plain words

Global energy agencies expect record energy investment in India this year, mostly in solar power and refineries. Another report counts India's new carbon trading scheme among the largest carbon markets.

  • IEA World Energy Investment 2026: India record $170 bn in 2026; 11% a year growth over five years (solar PV +25%, refining +23%); $3 in renewables and nuclear per $1 in fossil power; nuclear target 100 GW by 2047 (now 9 GW)
  • World Bank State and Trends of Carbon Pricing 2026 (13th): pricing covers 29% of GHG emissions; revenues above $107 bn (2025); India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (2026) is intensity-based, built on PAT; only China ETS, EU ETS and Korea ETS cover more
  • WMO Global Annual-to-Decadal Update (UK Met Office): 2026-2030 at 1.3-1.9°C above 1850-1900; 86% chance one year beats 2024; 75% chance five-year average crosses 1.5°C
  • IRENA roadmap: electricity 35% of final energy by 2035; grid investment $0.5 tn → $1 tn a year (2026-35); renewables 18.4 TW by 2035
  • CEEW and Project InnerSpace: India geothermal potential 450 GW of power
  • UNEP-GlobalABC buildings report: buildings about 37% of global CO2 emissions

India's energy investment in 2026 as per IEA? ($170 bn)

2/5★ Must-learnViksit Bharat-G RAM G Act, 2025 in force from 1 July 2026

In plain words

A new law replaces the rural employment guarantee scheme from July and raises the guaranteed work from one hundred to one hundred and twenty-five days a year.

  • Replaces MGNREGA 2005, which stands repealed from 1 July 2026; passed by Parliament in December 2025
  • Guarantee raised from 100 to 125 days a year; work within 15 days of application; delay compensation 0.05% of unpaid wages a day
  • Administrative expenditure 6% → 9%; four work areas: water security, core rural infrastructure, livelihood infrastructure, extreme-weather mitigation
  • Funding: 90:10 NE and Himalayan states; 60:40 other states; 100% Centre for UTs without legislature; FY27 provision ₹95,692.31 crore
Exam angle

Days of guaranteed work under VB-G RAM G? (125)

3/5★ Must-learnKharif MSP 2026-27, FRP and crop estimates

In plain words

The government raised support prices for summer crops and set the sugarcane price. Official estimates show a record harvest of food grains this year.

  • MSP for 14 Kharif crops raised; highest absolute rise: sunflower seed ₹622, cotton ₹557, nigerseed ₹515, sesamum ₹500 a quintal
  • Sugarcane FRP 2026-27: ₹365 a quintal at 10.25% recovery (2.81% higher; cost A2+FL ₹182)
  • Third Advance Estimates 2025-26: record foodgrains 376.563 MT (+5.3%); rice 154.024 MT, wheat 120.657 MT, maize 55.093 MT, oilseeds 43.059 MT, sugarcane 500.063 MT
  • "Khet Bachao Abhiyan", 1-30 June 2026, for balanced fertiliser use; target natural and organic farming on at least 25% of farmland
  • SEHAT Mission (ICAR and ICMR): Science Excellence for Health through Agricultural Transformation
  • IMD: 2026 monsoon forecast cut to 90% of LPA (LPA 87 cm, 1971-2020); El Niño concern
Exam angle

Which Kharif crop got the highest absolute MSP rise for 2026-27? (sunflower seed, ₹622 a quintal)
