Growth, outlook and data releases

1/46★ Must-learnIndia growth forecasts: World Bank, ADB, IMF, UN ESCAP, Moody's (April 2026)

In plain words

Several global institutions published their estimates of how fast India's economy will grow. These forecasts shape how investors, banks and policymakers plan for the year ahead.

  • World Bank (twice-yearly South Asia regional update, before IMF-WB Spring Meetings): India FY26 7.6% (+1.1 pt vs Oct 2025), FY27 6.6% (+0.3 pt); FY25 7.1%
    • South Asia (calendar year): 2025e 7.0 → 2026f 6.3 → 2027f 6.9; excluding India: 3.9 → 4.1 → 4.9
  • ADB (Asian Development Outlook, April 2026): Asia 4.7% in 2026, 4.8% in 2027 (cut from 5.1% for both years); India 6.9% (2026), 7.3% (2027)
  • UN ESCAP (Economic and Social Survey of Asia and the Pacific 2026; published every year since 1947): India 6.4% (2026), 6.6% (2027); inflation 4.4% (2026), 4.3% (2027)
    • South and South-West Asia grew 5.4% in 2025 (5.2% in 2024), led by India
    • Greenfield FDI announced (first three quarters): India $50 bn > Australia $30 bn > Korea $25 bn > Kazakhstan $21 bn
AgencyIndia 2026India 2027Note
World Bank7.6% (FY26)6.6% (FY27)fiscal-year basis
ADB6.9%7.3%Asia cut to 4.7%
UN ESCAP6.4%6.6%inflation 4.4%
IMF (WEO, April 2026)6.5% (FY27)6.5% (FY28)up from 6.4%

Which agency cut Asia's 2026 growth to 4.7%? (ADB)

Remember

Do not mix fiscal-year (World Bank, RBI) and calendar-year (ADB, ESCAP) figures.

2/46★ Must-learnIMF April 2026 World Economic Outlook: India slips to 6th largest economy

In plain words

The International Monetary Fund now ranks India lower in the world list of biggest economies when measured in US dollars. The ranking is expected to improve again as India overtakes Japan.

  • India 4th → 6th in nominal GDP rankings (US-dollar terms; local-currency GDP converted at current exchange rates)
  • 2026 GDP ranking: US $32.38 tn > China $20.85 tn > Germany $5.45 tn > Japan $4.38 tn > UK $4.26 tn > India $4.15 tn
  • India to pass Japan by 2028 ($5.06 tn vs $4.74 tn); decisive move to 3rd by 2031 ($6.79 tn vs Japan $5.13 tn); $6.17 tn by 2030
Exam angle

Which economy is India projected to overtake in 2028? (Japan)

3/46★ Must-learnInflation, March 2026

In plain words

Inflation measures how fast everyday prices rise, and two main gauges track it: one for what households buy and one for wholesale goods. The household gauge now uses a newer base year, which changes what goes into the basket and how it is weighed.

  • CPI (MoSPI): 3.4% (Feb 2026: 3.21%); new base year 2024
  • CPI 2024 series: rural 3.63%, urban 3.11%; basket items 299 → 358 (goods 259 → 308, services 40 → 50); 12 divisions; published by MoSPI through NSO
  • WPI: 3.88% y/y, fastest in over three years (oil, food, manufactured goods); base year 2011-12
  • WPI weights: manufactured products 64.23%, primary articles 22.62%, fuel and power 13.15%; food index 24.38%; DPIIT releases it on the 14th of each month
Remember

CPI base is now 2024; WPI base is still 2011-12.

4/46★ Must-learnIndex of Eight Core Industries, March 2026

In plain words

Eight key industries, such as coal, steel and electricity, produce the basic inputs for the rest of the economy. Tracking them gives an early signal of how factories and industry as a whole are doing.

  • ICI -0.4% y/y (provisional); April-March 2025-26 cumulative 2.6%
  • Eight core industries = 40.27% of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP); base 2011-12
  • Weights: refinery products 28.04, electricity 19.85, steel 17.92, coal 10.33, crude oil 8.98, natural gas 6.88, cement 5.37, fertilisers 2.63; compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser (DPIIT/Commerce)
  • March 2026 fell in fertilisers, crude oil, coal and electricity

5/46☆ Good to knowReliance Industries: first Indian firm with annual net profit above $10 billion

  • Milestone reported for FY2025-26

6/46★ Must-learnPMI and exports

In plain words

Purchasing managers' surveys ask firms whether business is getting better or worse, so a reading above 50 means growth. Along with record exports, this shows the economy was still expanding.

  • Manufacturing PMI (S&P Global): 53.9 in March 2026 (56.9 in Feb); HSBC Services PMI 57.5; above 50 = expansion
  • Exports record $860 bn in FY2025-26 (Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal)
  • MoSPI proposes an Index of Services Production for the formal sector using GST data, base year 2024-25

7/46★ Must-learnIIP, female workforce and DPI roadmap

In plain words

These are three snapshots of the economy: factory output for the month, more women taking part in work, and a government think-tank plan to build digital public systems. Together they show where growth and jobs are coming from.

  • IIP March 2026: 4.1% (February 5.2%); quick estimate released on the 28th of each month; base 2011-12; use-based groups: capital, basic, intermediate, infrastructure goods, consumer durables and non-durables
  • Female labour force participation: 23.3% (2017-18) → 40% (2025); worker ratio 22% → about 39%; female unemployment 5.6% → 3.1% (Labour Minister Mandaviya)
  • NITI Aayog DPI@2047 (27 April 2026; with EkStep Foundation and Deloitte): DPI 2.0 (2025-35) livelihood-led growth, DPI 3.0 (2035-47) broad prosperity; eight sector transformations; DPI adds about 1% of GDP, could reach 4% by 2030

8/46★ Must-learnManufacturing hubs and export target

In plain words

The government wants India to make far more goods by building planned industrial zones with ready roads, power and logistics. It also set a big goal for total exports and arranged a way to track progress sector by sector.

  • Manufacturing about 16-17% of GDP, 27 mn+ workers; value added about 12.5% of GDP; goal: share ≥25% as India goes from $3.7 tn to $30-35 tn by 2047 (per capita $18,000)
  • Public capex ₹2 lakh cr (FY15) → ₹12.2 lakh cr (FY27 BE)
  • NICDP: 20 industrial smart cities approved (7 corridors, 13 states); 4 completed: Dholera (Gujarat), Shendra-Bidkin (Maharashtra), Greater Noida (UP), Vikram Udyogpuri-Ujjain (MP)
  • PM MITRA parks: 7 (TN, Telangana, Gujarat, Karnataka, MP, UP, Maharashtra); Bulk Drug Parks: Gujarat, Himachal, Andhra
  • Budget 2026-27: 3 chemical parks; Biopharma SHAKTI ₹10,000 cr/5 yrs (3 new NIPERs, 7 upgraded, 1,000+ clinical trial sites)
  • MSMEs: 7.47 crore units, 35.4% of manufacturing output, 48.58% of exports, 31.1% of GDP, 32.82 crore jobs
  • Ranks: CIP (competitive industrial performance) 37th (2023); Global Innovation Index 38th (2025)
  • PM Gati Shakti master plan: 44 central ministries + 36 states/UTs; IIPDF funds transaction advisers; NIEI = National Infrastructure Enablement Index
  • Export target: $2 tn by 2030-31 = $1 tn goods + $1 tn services; Export Monitoring Framework (sectors: engineering, textiles, electronics, pharma, chemicals, services); each action under a Nodal Joint Secretary
Remember

Remember: $2 tn = 1 + 1 (goods + services).

9/46★ Must-learnBase year 2022-23: GSVA and DDP guidelines

In plain words

Gross domestic product is measured against a base year, and the national statistics office moved that base to a newer year so the numbers reflect today's economy. States and districts now need matching rules so their own figures can be compared fairly.

  • MoSPI revised National Accounts base year to 2022-23; draft uniform guidelines for GSVA (Gross State Value Added) and DDP (District Domestic Product); Sub-Committee on Regional Accounts chaired by Prof. Ravindra H. Dholakia under ACNAS
  • ASISSE: first Annual Survey of Incorporated Services Sector Enterprises, ref. year FY2024-25; GSTN sampling frame; 1.21 lakh+ enterprises; under Collection of Statistics Act 2008

10/46☆ Good to knowTextile demand survey 2024

  • Market size ₹4.89 lakh cr (2010) → ₹14.95 lakh cr (2024), CAGR 8.3%; domestic ₹12.02 lakh cr; per capita ₹2,119 → ₹6,066; MMF/blended 52.2%, cotton 41.2%, silk 5.2%, wool 1.3%; women 55.5% of purchases; released by Giriraj Singh

11/46☆ Good to knowIndia third in renewable capacity

  • IRENA RE Statistics 2026 (data Dec 2025): India 3rd globally in RE installed capacity, ahead of Brazil (earlier edition: 4th)

Trade, FDI and tax

12/46★ Must-learnFDI equity inflows, April-December FY26

In plain words

Foreign direct investment is money from abroad put into Indian businesses. This card shows which countries and states received or sent the most in the first nine months of the year.

  • Top source: Singapore $17.6 bn (37%); then US 16%, Mauritius 10% (data: DPIIT, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade)
  • Cayman Islands FDI up five times: $422 mn → $2 bn
  • Top states: Maharashtra $15.38 bn, Karnataka $11.15 bn

13/46★ Must-learnIncome Tax Act 2025 in force (1 April 2026): Form 130 and TRACES 2.0

In plain words

India's new income tax law took effect and changed the forms and words people use, such as the paper an employer gives to show tax already cut from salary. It aims to make tax records easier to check and match.

  • Form 130 replaces Form 16 (employer's TDS certificate); now discloses the rate of tax deducted so employees can verify TDS
  • "Assessment year" replaced by "tax year"; fields added: email, phone, country code
  • TDS reporting moves to TIN 2.0, replacing the OLTAS-based system
  • TRACES 2.0 (TDS Reconciliation Analysis and Correction Enabling System), launched by the Income Tax Department: one dashboard for Form 26AS, AIS (Annual Information Statement) and TDS credits
Exam angle

What replaced Form 16 under the new Act? (Form 130)

14/46★ Must-learnGross GST, March 2026

In plain words

Goods and Services Tax collection is a quick health check of spending and trade across the country. Collections kept growing both in the month and over the full year.

  • March 2026: +8.8% to over ₹2 lakh crore
  • FY2025-26: ₹22 lakh crore, +8.3% over ₹20 lakh crore in FY25

15/46☆ Good to knowCBIC: drawback on re-export of SEZ goods cleared to DTA

  • Goods cleared from SEZ units to the Domestic Tariff Area on payment of duty, then re-exported, count as "imported goods" for duty drawback under Section 74, Customs Act 1962
    • Conditions: easy identification and proof of duty payment

16/46★ Must-learnChina becomes India's top trading partner in FY26

In plain words

China became India's biggest trading partner, taking the place the United States held for years. India buys far more from China than it sells, which leaves a large trade gap.

  • Bilateral trade $151.1 bn; China overtakes the US (top partner for four straight years till 2024-25)
  • India's trade deficit with China widened to $112.16 bn

17/46☆ Good to knowTrade measures

  • Duty-free import of yellow peas extended to 31 March 2027
  • Mundra Port (APSEZ): record 6,008 cars on a single vessel; India's largest car-export hub

18/46★ Must-learnExports and trade balance, FY2025-26

In plain words

India sold more to the world than the year before, but it also imported even more goods. The gap in goods trade was partly covered by a large surplus in services.

  • Merchandise plus services exports $860.09 bn vs $825.26 bn (+4.22%)
  • Merchandise trade deficit $333.19 bn (FY25: $283.50 bn); services surplus $213.89 bn ($188.84 bn)
  • Fastest export growth: China (36.66%), Spain, Hong Kong, Vietnam, Sri Lanka; import growth led by China, USA, Hong Kong, Peru (78.08%), UK

19/46★ Must-learnRELIEF scheme for exporters (West Asia disruption)

In plain words

War in West Asia raised shipping and insurance costs for Indian exporters. This scheme repays part of those extra costs, mainly to small exporters, so they can keep selling abroad.

  • Resilience and Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation, launched 19 March 2026 under the Export Promotion Mission; nodal agency ECGC
  • Covers freight surge, insurance premium and war-risk costs; reimbursement for MSME exporters
  • Egypt and Jordan added to eligible destinations; fresh ECGC Whole Turnover Policy on or after 16 March 2026 qualifies for Component II (circular 15 April)

20/46★ Must-learnStartup India: record recognitions and Fund of Funds 2.0

In plain words

More new startups than ever were officially recognised in a year, creating jobs across the country. A second government fund is being set up to invest in startups through professionally managed funds.

  • 55,200+ startups recognised in FY26 (highest ever; +51.6%); total 2.23 lakh by 31 March 2026 with 23.36 lakh direct jobs; 48% have a woman director or partner
  • Startup India launched 16 Jan 2016; leaders: Maharashtra, Karnataka, UP, Delhi, Gujarat
  • FoF 2.0: corpus ₹10,000 cr for SEBI-registered AIFs across 16th and 17th Finance Commission cycles; implementing agency SIDBI; selection by Venture Capital Investment Committee; DPIIT issues guidelines
    • FoF 1.0: ₹7,000 cr to 135+ AIFs, which invested ₹26,900 cr in 1,420+ startups
  • Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups: cover per borrower ₹10 cr → ₹20 cr
  • FoF 2.0 guidelines (DPIIT): invests only through SEBI-registered Category I and II AIFs; total government fund-of-funds money in one AIF at most 50%; implementing agency cost capped at 0.50% a year; two-stage selection (SIDBI screening, then VCIC); unused money earns repo-rate interest; returns go to the Consolidated Fund of India

21/46☆ Good to knowDGFT Norms Committees

  • Seven committees fix input-output norms (SION) for Advance Authorisation and DFIA duty-free imports; technical members raised 12 → 22; fortnightly meetings

22/46☆ Good to knowNITI Aayog Trade Watch Quarterly (7th edition, Q3 FY26)

  • Merchandise exports +1.6%, imports +7.9%, services exports +7.8%
  • Gems and jewellery: India's exports $29.5 bn (7.8% of world); Surat is the world's largest cutting and polishing hub

23/46★ Must-learnIndia-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement

In plain words

India signed a trade deal with New Zealand that removes taxes on Indian goods entering that market. It also opens limited work and travel options for Indians and brings promised investment.

  • Duties on 100% of Indian exports eliminated from entry into force; leather and footwear tariff 5% → 0; first FTA chapter on Health and Traditional Medicine (AYUSH)
  • Agra makes about 75% of India's leather footwear (GI tag, One District One Product)
  • India's 9th trade agreement in recent years; New Zealand commits $20 bn investment; trade about $1.3 bn; India opens 70% of tariff lines (95% of NZ trade)
  • Mobility: Temporary Employment Entry visa (quota 5,000, stay up to 3 years); Working Holiday visa for 1,000 young Indians a year (12 months)

24/46★ Must-learnRoDTEP, RoSCTL and SEZ-to-DTA relief

In plain words

These are three government schemes that help exporters and factories in special zones by returning taxes or lowering duties. They keep Indian goods competitive abroad and help idle factory capacity find buyers at home.

  • RoDTEP revised schedules: Notification 15/2026-27 (30 Apr 2026); Appendix 4R (DTA exports) and 4RE (AA/EOU/SEZ); 194 tariff lines (142 added, 50 deleted, 2 modified); effective 1 May 2026; RoDTEP continued 1 Apr - 30 Sep 2026
  • RoSCTL (Rebate of State and Central Taxes and Levies): apparel and made-ups, extended to 30 Sep 2026 (or till 16th Finance Commission cycle approval); started 7 March 2019; zero-rating principle
  • SEZ → DTA concessional duty (Notification 11/2026-Customs, 31 Mar 2026, Section 25(1)): valid 1 Apr 2026 - 31 Mar 2027; cap 30% of highest FOB export value in last 3 years; min 20% value addition; no drawback; excludes agriculture, gems and jewellery, toys, petroleum, vehicles; Development Commissioner's certificate; faceless assessment
Remember

Remember: SEZ Act Section 30 treats SEZ to DTA clearance as an import.

25/46★ Must-learnPLI for large-scale electronics and India-Australia ECTA

In plain words

A government incentive scheme helped India go from importing mobile phones to making and exporting them in large numbers. A trade agreement with Australia has also grown exports there.

  • PLI LSEM (2020): mobile production ₹2.14 lakh cr (FY20) → ₹5.5 lakh cr (FY25); exports ₹0.27 → ₹2 lakh cr; India = 2nd largest mobile maker; 300+ units; top export CY2025: smartphones
  • India-Australia ECTA: signed 2 April 2022; Indian exports $4 bn (FY21) → $8.5 bn (FY25); trade $24.1 bn (FY25); India gave 70.3% of tariff lines (90.6% of trade value); Australia 100%; all Indian exports duty-free from 1 Jan 2026; organic MRA 24 Sept 2025

26/46★ Must-learnGeM crosses ₹18.4 lakh cr GMV

In plain words

Government Marketplace is an online shop where government offices buy goods and services directly. Its total sales have grown, with small firms, women-led firms and startups winning a large share.

  • Cumulative GMV ₹18.4 lakh cr; FY2025-26 GMV above ₹5 lakh cr; MSEs 68% of orders, 47.1% of GMV; 11 lakh+ MSEs got ₹2.36 lakh cr; women-led MSEs ₹28,000 cr+; startups ₹19,000 cr+; state procurement +38.3%

29/46★ Must-learnTextile exports FY2025-26

India's textile and clothing exports grew a little over the year, led by ready-made garments and handicrafts. The tax department also showed a new chatbot that helps people with tax questions.

Social issue

30/46★ Must-learnEPFO 3.0 and EPFO updates

In plain words

The provident fund body is moving towards an easier system where workers can take out their savings through digital payments. It also changes how much can be withdrawn and when, so people can reach their own money faster.

  • EPFO 3.0 (to be rolled out): withdrawals through UPI; 13 provisions → 3 categories (essential needs, housing needs, special circumstances)
  • Withdraw up to 75% of EPF balance any time (employee + employer share + interest); 25% minimum stays
  • Partial withdrawal after only 12 months of service
  • Unemployment: 75% at once, remaining 25% after 2 months
  • Claims settled in FY2025-26: record 8.31 crore (6.01 crore in FY25)
  • E-PRAAPTI (EPF Aadhaar-Based Access Portal for Tracking Inoperative Accounts): trace, link and activate old accounts
  • UAN (Universal Account Number): 12-digit, one per member, umbrella over multiple Member IDs
Exam angle

How much of the EPF corpus must stay in the account under EPFO 3.0? (25%)

31/46★ Must-learnNITI Aayog: Women and India's credit market (2nd edition)

In plain words

A government think-tank report studied how much more credit reaches women. It found women now borrow far more, especially for starting and running businesses, not only for personal needs.

  • "From Borrowers to Builders", released 7 April 2026; under Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP) with TransUnion CIBIL and MicroSave
  • Women's credit ₹16 lakh cr (2017) → ₹76 lakh cr (2025) = 4.8x; 26% of system credit; penetration 19% → 36%; about 45 crore credit-eligible women
  • Business lending 7.5x; share 16% → 25%; CAGR (2022-25) 31% vs 17% overall; microfinance slowest (2.9x); top graduation: Tamil Nadu 27%, West Bengal 23%

  • 8th Poshan Pakhwada: 9-23 April 2026; theme "Maximizing Brain Development in the First Six Years of Life"; Poshan Abhiyaan launched 2018

34/46★ Must-learnUPI at 10 years and 2025 data

In plain words

Unified Payments Interface lets people pay instantly from one bank account to another using a phone. After ten years it handles huge numbers of daily payments and is the world's biggest real-time payment system.

  • Launched April 2016 (RBI Governor Raghuram Rajan); idea articulated in Payments Vision 2018 for interoperability; 450 mn+ users
  • March 2026: record 22.64 bn payments worth ₹29.52 trn
  • 2025 (Worldline report): 228.5 bn transactions (+33% from 172.2 bn); value ₹299.74 trn; average ticket size falling
  • UPI QR codes 731.38 mn (+15% in 2025)
  • PIB: launched by NPCI on 11 April 2016; volume 2 crore (FY17) → 24,162 crore (FY26); value ₹0.07 lakh cr → about ₹314 lakh cr; banks live 44 → 703 (FY26); first month above 2,000 crore: Aug 2025 (2,001 cr), peak Dec 2025 (2,163 cr)
  • P2M = 63% of volume; P2P = 71% of value; 86% of P2M below ₹500; IMF: about 49% of world real-time payments volume
  • Banks on UPI: 216 (2021) → 691 (Jan 2026); linked abroad with UAE, Singapore, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, France, Mauritius, Qatar; RBI two-factor authentication rule for digital payments from 1 April 2026; JAM trinity = Jan Dhan + Aadhaar + Mobile; RTGS 2004, IMPS 2010

35/46★ Must-learnSBI overtakes ICICI Bank by market capitalisation

In plain words

Bank size is often compared by market value, meaning the total worth of its shares on the stock market. State Bank of India moved ahead of ICICI Bank to become the second most valuable bank.

  • January-March 2026 quarter: SBI becomes India's 2nd largest lender (₹9,04,047 cr); ICICI Bank fell over 10%; HDFC Bank stays first

36/46★ Must-learnGold and silver import: 15 banks authorised

In plain words

Only authorised banks can bring gold and silver into India. The government named fifteen banks that may do this for the next three years.

  • Allowed from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2029, including SBI, HDFC Bank, Bank of India
  • Only Union Bank of India and Sberbank allowed to import gold exclusively

37/46☆ Good to knowBanking and fintech business news

39/46★ Must-learnPM MUDRA Yojana: 11 years

In plain words

Mudra is a scheme that lends small amounts to tiny businesses without asking for anything to be pledged. After eleven years it has reached crores of borrowers, many of them women and first-time business owners.

  • Launched 8 April 2015; loans 57 crore+, ₹40.07 lakh cr (27 Mar 2026); collateral-free up to ₹20 lakh; MUDRA = Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency; guarantee via CGFMU (NCGTC)

Insurance

40/46★ Must-learnIRDAI: Ind AS for insurers from 1 April 2026

In plain words

The insurance regulator is changing how insurers prepare their accounts to a standard used in many countries. This makes their reports easier to compare, and insurers get time to switch over.

  • IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) (Amendment) Regulations 2026, approved at its 135th meeting
  • Applies to all insurers: Life, General, Stand-Alone Health, reinsurers; earlier IGAAP
  • Parallel reporting (Ind AS plus existing framework) for 2 years; one-year forbearance if an insurer cannot comply
  • Joint expert group on Ind AS transition, chaired by IRDAI's Member (Finance and Investment), for two years
  • Ind AS: converged with IFRS; implemented by Ministry of Corporate Affairs

41/46★ Must-learnDomestic Systemically Important Insurers (D-SIIs) FY2025-26

In plain words

Some insurers are so large that their failure would shake the whole financial system, so they are watched more closely. The same three insurers kept this label this year.

  • LIC, GIC Re, New India Assurance retain status (too big to fail by size, importance, interconnectedness)
Remember

GIC Re is the state-owned reinsurer; LIC and New India are the largest life and non-life insurers.

42/46★ Must-learnIRDAI revised cyber-security norms

In plain words

The insurance regulator made its cyber security rules stricter. Company boards must give attention and money to protecting data, and the security chief must work independently.

  • Information Security Risk Management Committee meets quarterly (earlier twice a year)
  • Boards must fund cyber security and close audit gaps within 12 months
  • CISO independent of IT function; no business targets; scenario-based response plans; follow CERT-In directions

43/46☆ Good to knowIRDAI: R1 approval

  • M Pallonji Group (with Divya Sehgal and Federal Bank) gets R1 registration approval for a general insurance venture

44/46★ Must-learnNon-life insurance premium FY26 and obligatory cession

In plain words

General insurers earned more premium, and health insurers grew fastest. A new rule also makes every general insurer hand a small share of each policy to the national reinsurer, which spreads risk.

  • Gross direct premium ₹3,35,918 cr (+9.2%, from ₹3,07,612 cr); standalone private health insurers +19.8% to ₹45,865 cr (IRDAI flash figures)
  • Obligatory cession FY27: 4% of sum insured on each general policy to the Indian reinsurer (GIC Re); terrorism and nuclear pool: NIL
    • Minimum commission on cession: 5% motor third-party and oil and energy; 10% group health; 7.5% crop insurance

45/46☆ Good to knowForeign reinsurer at GIFT City

  • ADNIC (Abu Dhabi National Insurance Company) gets approval for a reinsurance branch in GIFT City

46/46★ Must-learnInsurance sector snapshot and reforms

In plain words

This card shows how big and how deep insurance is in India, and how little of the population is covered compared with the world. It also lists law changes meant to bring in more insurers and more people.

  • India is 10th largest insurance market (1.8% share; Swiss Re); penetration 3.7% (life 2.7%, non-life 1.0%); density $97.0
  • FY25: 41.84 crore policies; premium ₹11.93 lakh cr; claims ₹8.36 lakh cr; AUM ₹74.44 lakh cr; 74 insurers; health is 41% of non-life premium (ahead of motor)
  • Insurance and pension funds are 29.6% of household financial assets (28.6% in FY19)
  • Sabka Bima, Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act 2025: FDI 74% → 100%; IRDAI approval for share transfer 1% → 5%; foreign reinsurer net owned fund ₹5,000 cr → ₹1,000 cr; maximum penalty ₹1 cr → ₹10 cr; one-time registration of intermediaries
  • GST exemption on individual life and health policies (incl. family floater) and reinsurance from 22 Sept 2025 (was 18%)
  • Health rules: moratorium 8 → 5 years (60 months) (2024); 30-day free look; grace period 15 days (monthly) or 30 days (other modes); pro-rata refund on mid-term cancellation
Remember

IRDAI vision: "Insurance for All by 2047".

RBI

In plain words

The Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy committee decides the main interest rate that guides all other rates. This time it left the rate unchanged and shared its forecasts for growth and inflation.

  • Chair: Governor Sanjay Malhotra; members: Dr Nagesh Kumar, Saugata Bhattacharya, Prof. Ram Singh, Dr Poonam Gupta, Indranil Bhattacharyya

2/37★ Must-learnTrade relief and FX derivative rules (rolled back)

In plain words

The central bank eased conditions for exporters by allowing a longer time to repay export loans. It also took back a recent rule on currency derivative deals, which are contracts about future exchange rates.

  • Export credit: enhanced period up to 450 days (pre- and post-shipment) for credit disbursed till 30 June 2026; applies to commercial banks, co-operative banks, NBFC-Factors, All-India Financial Institutions
  • FX derivatives: the 1 April circular (no INR non-deliverable forwards for clients, no rebooking) was withdrawn; NDFs to clients and rebooking allowed again
    • Still barred: INR derivative deals with related parties (Ind AS 24 meaning)
    • Stays: $100 million cap on banks' net open position in the onshore deliverable market (from 27 March)

3/37★ Must-learnFPI debt investment limits FY2026-27

In plain words

Foreign investors may hold only a set share of Indian government and company bonds, and the central bank fixes those shares each year. The limits stay the same for the new financial year.

  • Effective 1 April 2026: G-Secs 6%, State Government Securities 2%, corporate bonds 15%
  • Incremental G-Sec limit split 50:50 between "General" and "Long-term"; all "specified securities" under Fully Accessible Route (FAR)
  • Voluntary Retention Route investments now under General Route limits
PeriodTotal debt limit (₹ cr)
Current14,70,655
Apr-Sep 202615,51,646
Oct 2026-Mar 202716,32,640
  • Issued under FEMA 1999, Sections 10(4) and 11(1)
  • CDS: aggregate notional Credit Default Swaps sold by FPIs capped at 5% of outstanding corporate bonds; extra limit ₹3,30,464 cr for 2026-27

4/37★ Must-learnState market borrowing, April-June 2026

In plain words

State governments raise money by selling bonds, and this card says how much they plan to raise in the quarter. The central bank is also trying a new way of timing these sales for nine states.

  • States/UTs to borrow ₹2,54,509 crore in Q1 FY27
  • RBI pilots Benchmark Issuance Strategy (BIS) for 9 states (AP, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Kerala, MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Telangana, UP): ₹1,53,900 crore

5/37★ Must-learnCross-border inward payments: faster credit (RBI guidelines)

In plain words

Money sent from abroad can take a long time to reach the receiver even after it reaches the bank. New central bank guidelines make banks tell customers quickly and credit the money the same day where possible.

  • Under Section 10(2) r/w Section 18, Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2007; effective six months from the circular
  • Inform customer immediately on receipt of the inward message (after-hours: start of next business day)
  • Reconcile nostro account on near real-time basis, interval normally not above 1 hour
  • Credit within the same business day if received in forex market hours, else next business day; straight-through crediting for resident individuals

6/37★ Must-learnRBI draft: delay on high-value digital transfers (fraud control)

In plain words

Online fraud is causing large losses, so the central bank has proposed a short pause on bigger online transfers. The pause gives the sender time to cancel a payment if it was made by mistake or under pressure.

  • Context: online fraud losses crossed ₹22,000 crore last year; proposed by RBI's Department of Payment and Settlement Systems
  • One-hour hold on account-to-account transfers above ₹10,000 (payer can cancel); exempt: merchant payments, e-mandates, NACH, cheques; payee whitelisting allowed
  • Trusted person for age 70+ and persons with disabilities; mandatory for transfers above ₹50,000
  • Annual credits to individual/small business accounts capped at ₹25 lakh; excess held as "shadow credit", returned if no justification in 30 days
  • Kill switch: switch off all digital channels in one step
Remember

Above ₹10,000 = 45% of fraud cases by volume but ~98.5% by value.

7/37★ Must-learnRBI draft: NBFC Upper Layer identification

In plain words

Large non-bank lenders face tighter rules because their failure could hurt the whole system. The central bank proposes picking them by one simple size test instead of a scoring method.

  • Simple asset-size test of ₹1 lakh crore or more replaces the scoring model (which picked the top ten by assets); reviewed every five years
  • Government-owned NBFCs (NABARD, Exim Bank, SIDBI) to be included in the upper layer
  • All NBFC-UL may use state government guarantees as a credit-risk transfer instrument, without limit

8/37☆ Good to knowRBI Foundation Day (1 April)

  • Established 1935 under the RBI Act 1934; based on the Hilton Young Commission (1926) recommendations
  • HQ Kolkata → Mumbai in 1937; first Governor Sir Osborne Smith; first Indian Governor C.D. Deshmukh

9/37☆ Good to knowRBI: smaller circulars and drafts

  • INR notes can be exchanged at forex counters in departure halls of international airports (earlier: only buy INR from non-residents)
  • Floating Rate Savings Bonds: structure unchanged (7-year tenor, NSC rate + 35 bps, half-yearly reset); online application facility by 30 Sept 2026; PAN mandatory, SFT reporting, DPDP alignment
  • CASA ratio fell to a 2-year low of 37.9% (Dec 2025 quarter) from 40.1% (Dec 2023)
  • Draft Business Correspondent norms: three delivery points (branch, BC-Banking Outlet, BC-Banking Touchpoint); Business Facilitators merged into BC model; uniform commission
  • Proposed e-cheque: digitally signed cheque combining paper-cheque trust with digital speed

10/37★ Must-learnCurrency in circulation, FY26

In plain words

Currency in circulation is the total cash in people's hands and in banks. It grew faster than in recent years, as cash use stayed strong in rural areas and people held extra cash as a precaution.

  • CIC +11.9% to ₹41.68 trillion; highest growth since 2020-21; absolute rise ₹4.44 trillion (highest since 2017-18)
  • Drivers: revival of cash-driven rural economy, precautionary demand; currency with public ₹40.52 tn (15 March 2026)

11/37★ Must-learnForex reserves, week ended 17 April 2026

In plain words

Foreign exchange reserves are the foreign money and gold the country keeps to pay for imports and steady the rupee. They rose in the latest week after a sharp fall in the month before.

  • +$2.3 bn to over $703 bn; foreign currency assets +$1.48 bn to over $557 bn; gold and SDR rose; IMF reserve position +$14 mn to $4.87 bn
  • March 2026: reserves fell $30.5 bn ($728.5 bn → $688.05 bn) despite RBI rupee support

12/37★ Must-learnRBI cancels Paytm Payments Bank licence

In plain words

The central bank cancelled the banking licence of Paytm Payments Bank, so it can no longer work as a bank. The decision follows years of restrictions and rests on a specific section of the banking law.

  • Section 22(4), Banking Regulation Act 1949; effective 24 April 2026; bank barred from "banking" (Section 5(b)) and Section 6 business
  • Grounds under Section 22(3): (b) affairs detrimental to depositors, (c) management prejudicial to public interest, (e) no useful purpose in continuing
  • Bank has enough liquidity to repay all deposits
  • History: onboarding stopped 11 March 2022; business curbs on 31 Jan and 16 Feb 2024
Exam angle

Under which Section can RBI cancel a bank licence? (22(4), Banking Regulation Act 1949)

13/37☆ Good to knowPayments banks at a glance

  • Set up on Nachiket Mor Committee advice; public limited company; minimum paid-up capital ₹100 cr; deposit cap ₹2 lakh per customer
  • First to launch: Airtel Payments Bank (2017); IPPB launched 1 Sept 2018, first fully government-owned
  • Five payments banks: Airtel, IPPB, Fino, Jio, NSDL

14/37★ Must-learnRBI draft Master Direction on Prepaid Payment Instruments 2026

In plain words

Prepaid payment instruments are wallets and cards loaded with money before use. The central bank has drafted new rules on who may issue them and how much they can hold.

  • Banks (debit card issuers) can issue PPIs with prior intimation to DPSS; non-banks need RBI authorisation and ₹15 cr net worth by end of third financial year
  • General-purpose PPI: outstanding balance up to ₹2 lakh; cash loading ₹10,000 per month
  • Gift PPI up to ₹10,000; Transit PPI ₹3,000; wallets for foreign nationals/NRIs (passport + visa) for P2M payments

15/37☆ Good to knowRBI: Ujjivan SFB, refiners, hackathon and AI risk

  • Ujjivan Small Finance Bank's universal-bank application returned (diversify loan book); only AU SFB has transitioned so far
    • SFB to universal bank: scheduled status with 5-year record, listed, net worth ₹1,000 cr, CRAR met, GNPA ≤ 3% and NNPA ≤ 1% in last two years
  • RBI asked state-run oil refiners to curb spot dollar buying and use a special credit line via SBI to ease rupee pressure
  • HaRBInger (4th global hackathon): theme "Secure Banking: Powered by Identity, Integrity and Inclusivity"; problems: tokenised KYC, offline CBDC (e₹), enhancing trust
  • RBI consulting regulators/lenders on cyber risk from Anthropic's Mythos AI model (faster discovery of software vulnerabilities); 2018 data localisation rule keeps payment data on servers in India

16/37☆ Good to knowRBI: NBFC branch rules and FDI company data

  • NBFCs may open branches without prior RBI approval unless restricted
    • Deposit-taking NBFC with NOF up to ₹50 cr or rating below AA: own state only; NOF above ₹50 cr and AA or above: anywhere in India
  • Finances of FDI companies 2024-25: net sales growth 8.7% (9.4% earlier); Singapore, USA, Mauritius account for over half of sampled companies

17/37★ Must-learnRBI: Expected Credit Loss (ECL) norms (final)

In plain words

Banks used to set aside money only after a loan went bad. The new rule makes them estimate likely losses early and keep money aside in advance, with larger amounts for riskier loans.

  • Effective 1 April 2027; forward-looking provisioning on Probability of Default (PD), Loss Given Default (LGD), Exposure at Default (EAD)
StageMeaningProvision
Stage 1Normal loans0.4% minimum (12-month loss)
Stage 2Risky loans (e.g. 60-90 days overdue)5% minimum
Stage 3NPAsFull lifetime loss
  • Extra provision from transition can be spread over 4 years to 31 March 2031, with CET1 add-back during that period
  • All loans at 31 March 2027 under the effective interest rate (EIR) regime by 31 March 2030
Exam angle

What are the minimum Stage 1 and Stage 2 provisions? (0.4% and 5%)

18/37★ Must-learnRBI: Basel III credit-risk (standardised approach) final directions

In plain words

This sets how much capital a bank must hold against different kinds of loans, based on how risky each loan is. The final rules ease some of the earlier proposals and apply from next year.

  • From 1 April 2027; 150% risk weight on unrated corporate/NBFC exposures only above ₹500 cr (₹200 cr was proposed)
  • Unrated bank exposures: long-term 100%, short-term 50%; foreign bank branches may use parent ratings
  • Regulatory retail: all small businesses (turnover up to ₹500 cr); limit ₹7.5 cr → ₹10 cr per borrower
  • Real estate AD&C: minimum borrower contribution 25% of project cost

19/37★ Must-learnRBI: wilful defaulters and calamity relief

In plain words

Banks must now decide quickly whether a borrower deliberately refused to repay. The same card also lets banks give faster relief to borrowers hit by natural disasters.

  • From 1 April 2027: bank must classify a wilful defaulter within 6 months of the account turning NPA
  • Calamity relief (from 1 July 2026): banks may implement resolution on their own on SLBC recommendation, for standard loans not over 30 days overdue; invoke within 45 days, implement within 135 days; one-time 30-day extension via RBI regional director

20/37★ Must-learnRBI: Unregistered Type I NBFCs

In plain words

Some small non-bank lenders deal with no public money and no customers, so strict registration adds little. The central bank excuses them from registering and gives a one-time window to hand back their registration.

  • NBFCs with no public funds, no customer interface and assets below ₹1,000 cr exempt from registration; effective 1 July 2026
  • One-time deregistration window till 31 Dec 2026 via PRAVAAH portal (3 years' audited accounts, auditor certificate, board resolution)
  • NBFCs at ₹1,000 cr or above register as Type I; all others Type II

21/37★ Must-learnRBI: lending norms for urban co-operative banks (final)

In plain words

The central bank set final lending rules for urban co-operative banks. Loans without security may be at most a fifth of all loans, and smaller-tier banks keep a cap on housing loan tenure.

  • Amendment Directions issued 29 April 2026: Credit Facilities, Concentration Risk Management, Financial Statements (disclosures)
  • Unsecured loans and advances: aggregate ceiling 20% of total loans and advances (audited balance sheet of the preceding year)
  • Housing loans: Tier 1 and Tier 2 UCBs → tenure up to 20 years, including any moratorium; Tier 3 and Tier 4 → tenure and moratorium set by Board-approved policy
  • In force from 1 October 2026, or earlier if a UCB adopts the amendments in full
Exam angle

Ceiling on unsecured advances of UCBs? (20% of total loans and advances)

22/37☆ Good to knowRBI: other circulars and launches

  • OTC FX derivatives reporting (from 1 July 2027): AD Cat-I banks report to CCIL trade repository, covering 70%, 80%, 90% of notional in phases
  • Corporate credit cards: overdue reporting and asset classification at corporate level; late fee only on outstanding amount
  • Mission SAKSHAM (Sahakari Bank Kshamta Nirman): capacity-building and certification for urban co-operative banks, launched by Governor Malhotra
  • RBI began surveys on household inflation expectations and consumer confidence (19 cities each)

23/37★ Must-learnRBI note and coin rules: exchange, counterfeit, currency chests

In plain words

The central bank set clear rules for banks on exchanging dirty or damaged notes and on handling fake notes. It also set fines for banks, cash chests and cash machines that fail the public.

  • Counterfeit notes: up to 4 pieces in one transaction → monthly consolidated report to police; 5 or more → immediate FIR; notes of ₹100 and above must be machine-checked for authenticity before re-circulation; every bank keeps a Forged Note Vigilance (FNV) Cell at head office (half-yearly report; monthly data by the 7th; counterfeit notes preserved 3 years)
  • Exchange: soiled notes up to 20 pieces or ₹5,000 a day → free, over the counter; above that → against receipt, payment within 7 days; mutilated notes above 10 pieces or ₹5,000 → receipt, up to 30 days; no branch may refuse coins or small notes; complaint to Ombudsman if bank silent for 30 days
Penalty (Currency Chest directions)Amount
Refusing exchange of coins/small/soiled notes₹10,000; ₹5 lakh if more than 5 instances in a year
Counterfeit note in ATM/over-counter dispensation₹10,000 per instance
ATM cash-out above 10 hours a month₹10,000 per ATM (also White Label ATM operators)
Delayed or wrong chest reportingPenal interest Bank Rate + 2%
  • Currency Chest (CC): stores notes and coins for RBI; minimum deposit/withdrawal ₹50,000, then multiples of ₹10,000; report on CyM-CC portal same day by 7 pm; incentives: NE/hilly/J&K/Ladakh chest capital cost up to ₹50 lakh, revenue cost 50% for 5 years; coin distribution ₹65 per bag (+₹10 rural)
Remember

Remember: 4 pieces → monthly report; 5 or more → FIR.

24/37★ Must-learnFEMA (Guarantees) Regulations, 2026

In plain words

This new rule says who in India may give or take a guarantee involving someone abroad. It also sets how it must be reported and the fee for reporting late.

  • No resident may be principal debtor, surety or creditor in a guarantee with a non-resident unless permitted; exempt: guarantees by AD bank branches abroad or in IFSC; IPC by custodian banks for FPIs to central counterparties
  • Resident can act as surety/debtor if the underlying transaction is not prohibited and both are eligible to lend/borrow; reporting by surety, debtor or creditor as applicable; AD banks file returns within 30 days of quarter-end via CIMS
  • Late Submission Fee: ₹7,500 + 0.025% × amount × years of delay

25/37★ Must-learnRBI capital, card and classification directions

In plain words

Three changes affect banks and cardholders: which reserves count as banks' capital, how late credit card payments are treated, and which older loan rules are being replaced next year. They protect customers from harsh charges and keep banks sound.

  • Tier 2 capital: general provisions on standard assets (Stage 1/2) plus excess provisions from NPA sales count up to 1.25% of credit risk-weighted assets (standardised approach); floating provisions: net off from gross NPAs or count in Tier 2
  • Credit cards: report as past due or levy penal charges only after more than 3 days past due; charges only on the outstanding amount after due date
  • IRAC Directions 2025 (28 Nov 2025) repealed from 1 April 2027; replaced by Asset Classification, Provisioning and Income Recognition Directions, 27 April 2026, same date

26/37☆ Good to knowFloating Rate Savings Bonds 2020: operations

  • Interest = NSC rate +35 bps, reset 1 Jan and 1 July, paid half-yearly; 7-year tenor; cash applications up to ₹20,000; Certificate of Holding in 3 working days; brokerage 0.5%; nominee minimum ₹1,000

SEBI

27/37★ Must-learnSEBI: buyback and IPO norms

In plain words

The market regulator is changing rules on companies buying back their own shares and on listing new shares. It also gives temporary relief for approvals that were about to lapse.

  • Proposal to reintroduce open-market (stock exchange) buybacks beside tender offer under Buy-back Regulations 2018; the route was stopped from 1 April 2025 (unequal participation, tax arbitrage)
    • From April 2026 buyback proceeds taxed as capital gains in shareholders' hands, ending the tax difference
  • ICDR amendment: depositories tag pledged shares "non-transferable" during lock-in
  • One-time relief: IPO observation letters expiring 1 April-30 Sept 2026 stay valid till 30 Sept 2026; Minimum Public Shareholding (25%) deadlines in that window also relaxed; penal action already taken from 1 April 2026 to be withdrawn

28/37★ Must-learnSEBI: new IT platforms

In plain words

The market regulator launched new computer platforms to speed up communication, hearings and checks on cyber security. These help it supervise firms and settle cases faster.

  • Launched by Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey: SUPCOMS (single universal platform for communication), e-adjudication portal (quasi-judicial proceedings), C-SAC (Cyber-Sec Audit Compliance; AI-enabled cyber-audit analysis)

29/37★ Must-learnSEBI: Social Stock Exchange relief and fit-and-proper rules

In plain words

The regulator made it easier for non-profit groups to raise money through a special stock exchange for social causes. It also changed who is considered fit and proper to run a market firm.

  • NPOs can stay registered on the SSE for three years without raising funds (earlier two); minimum subscription for Zero Coupon Zero Principal (ZCZP) instruments 75% → 50%
  • March board decision: minimum investment in social impact funds ₹2 lakh → ₹1,000
  • Fit-and-proper rule: pending complaint, FIR or charge sheet no longer disqualifies automatically; conviction for any economic offence or securities-law violation does; winding-up order (not initiation) disqualifies
    • Intermediaries must report disqualifying events within 15 working days; default five-year ineligibility removed; hearing must be given

30/37☆ Good to knowSEBI: coal exchange, mutual fund sponsors, FPI netting

  • SEBI cleared MCX coal-exchange subsidiary (capital commitment up to ₹100 cr); NSE cleared for "National Coal Exchange of India Ltd" (name approved by MCA; ₹100 cr, 60% stake, 40% for others)
  • Family trusts cannot sponsor mutual funds (sponsor must be a body corporate)
  • FPIs may net same-day cash-market trade funds (instead of gross settlement with custodians); implement by 31 Dec 2026
  • Proposals: broker net-worth based on 10% of average client credit balance (6 months) plus client count (over 10,000 to 50,000 clients ≈ ₹50 lakh); client unpaid securities pledge released the same day if payment before 5 PM

32/37★ Must-learnMinimum public shareholding: six bands (Finance Ministry)

Listed companies must keep some of their shares with the public, which keeps trading fair. The government made the rules fit the size of the company, giving very large firms more time and a smaller initial sale.

  • Bands by post-issue capital: up to ₹1,600 cr; ₹1,600-4,000 cr; ₹4,000-50,000 cr; ₹50,000 cr-₹1 lakh cr; ₹1-5 lakh cr; above ₹5 lakh cr (earlier three, with a special class of ₹1 lakh cr and above)

12/15★ Must-learnIndia's first drawdown for Maldives under SAARC Currency Swap Framework

In plain words

India agreed to let the Maldives draw on a currency swap, which means lending it money in rupees for a time. This helps the Maldives pay its foreign bills and keeps its currency steady.

3/70★ Must-learnConstitutional Amendment Bill: Lok Sabha up to 850 seats

In plain words

A proposed change to the Constitution would raise the number of seats in the Lok Sabha and reserve seats for women. It would use the new population count to redraw constituencies first.

  • Lok Sabha 543 → up to 850: not more than 815 from states, up to 35 from UTs (Article 81); Articles 82 and 170 amended for Delimitation Commission allocation on updated census
  • New Article 334A: women's reservation in Lok Sabha and assemblies, comes into force after delimitation; lasts 15 years unless extended
  • Aim: operationalise women's reservation before 2029 general elections
Exam angle

Which new Article carries women's reservation in the proposed Bill? (334A)

4/70★ Must-learnSHANTI Act (nuclear energy)

In plain words

A new law lets private companies build and run nuclear power plants under licence, which was not allowed before. It also sets how much a company must pay if an accident happens.

  • Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India; Presidential assent 21 Dec 2025
  • Private sector may set up nuclear facilities under licence of the Centre and safety authorisation of the regulatory board
  • Graded operator liability ₹100 cr to ₹3,000 cr by facility type; strict, no-fault liability; Government liability above that up to 300 million SDR

6/70★ Must-learnTenth Schedule (anti-defection)

In plain words

The Tenth Schedule is the part of the Constitution that stops elected members from switching parties for gain. It lets a group switch only when two-thirds of a party's members join another party.

  • Added by the 52nd Amendment Act 1985; the 91st Amendment removed the one-third split provision, now two-thirds merger needed

11/70★ Must-learnCensus 2027: first digital census

In plain words

India has started its first fully digital census, in which people may fill in their details themselves. Counting happens in two stages, houses first and then people, and caste is part of the count.

  • 16th Census, 8th since Independence; outlay ₹11,718.24 cr; caste enumeration included (Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs decision, 30 April 2025); intent notified 16 June 2025
PhaseTiming
Phase I: Houselisting and Housing CensusApril-September 2026; 30 days per state/UT, plus optional 15-day self-enumeration before it
Phase II: Population Enumeration (with castes)February 2027; reference date 00:00, 1 March 2027 (snow-bound areas: Sept 2026, reference 1 Oct 2026)
  • Legal base: Census Act 1948, Rules 1990; Union subject (Seventh Schedule, entry 69); Section 15 keeps data confidential (not under RTI or court evidence)
  • Digital tools: CMMS portal, offline HLO mobile app (16 languages), HLB Creator web map; manuals in 19 languages; about 31 lakh enumerators and supervisors; pre-test Nov 2025 in 5,000 blocks
Remember

First count 1865-72; first synchronous Census 1881; 2021 Census was delayed by COVID-19.

In plain words

Sagarmala is a programme to use India's coastline and ports to boost trade and local industries. This card shows how many projects exist and how many are finished.

  • Sagarmala (2015): port-led development; 5 pillars (port modernisation, connectivity, port-led industrialisation, coastal community development, coastal shipping and inland waterways)
  • 845 projects, ₹6.06 lakh cr; 315 completed (₹1.57 lakh cr); Sagarmala 2.0: ₹85,482 cr budget support, ₹3.6 lakh cr investment; vision documents MIV 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047
  • Sagarmala Finance Corporation Ltd (restructured June 2025 from SDCL, set up Aug 2016): India's first maritime NBFC; ₹4,300 cr sanctioned Dec 2025
  • Major ports 915.17 MT (target 904 MT, +7.06%); turnaround time 96 h (2014) → 49.5 h (2025); inland waterways cargo 18.10 → 145.50 MTPA (2013-14 to 2024-25)
  • Coastline 11,099 km; 12 major ports (Union ministry) and 200+ non-major ports (state boards); about 95% of trade by volume moves by sea

36/70★ Must-learnWind energy, 2025-26

In plain words

India installed more wind power in one year than ever before, moving closer to its clean energy goals. Most of it came from three western and southern states.

  • Best year: 6.05 GW added in FY26 (+46% on FY25; earlier record 5.5 GW in FY17); India 4th in installed wind capacity (56.09 GW); Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra lead, 28 GW under implementation; targets 100 GW by 2030, 156 GW by 2036

37/70★ Must-learnInland waterways: numbers and policies

In plain words

Rivers and canals can carry heavy goods more cheaply than roads, so India has declared many of them national waterways. Only a part of them are in use so far, and the government wants to open more.

  • 111 National Waterways, 20,187 km, 23 states and 4 UTs; 32 operational (5,155 km); Budget 2026-27: 20 more within 5 years (to 52); NW-5 (Talcher-Angul to Paradip/Dhamra, Odisha) to be operationalised
  • Cargo 145.84 MMT (FY25), 198 MMT (till Feb 2026); passengers 1.61 crore → 7.6 crore; target: combined inland and coastal share 6% → 12% by 2047; inland modal share 2% → 5%, 500 MMT by 2047

In plain words

India added more clean power in one year than ever before and now gets over half of its installed power capacity from non-fossil sources. This helps the country meet its climate promises sooner than planned.

  • Record addition 55.3 GW non-fossil in FY26; total non-fossil 283.46 GW (31 Mar 2026): RE 274.68 GW (solar 150.26, wind 56.09, bio 11.75, small hydro 5.17, large hydro 51.41) + nuclear 8.78 GW
  • Generation 1,845.921 BU; non-fossil share 29.2% (538.97 BU); 50% non-fossil capacity reached June 2025 (5 years early)

49/70★ Must-learnNational Panchayati Raj Day (24 April)

In plain words

National Panchayati Raj Day marks the law that gave village governments constitutional status. It is a good moment to remember how local self-government in India was built, step by step.

  • Marks 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act 1992 (in force 1993); Part IX of the Constitution
  • Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) proposed three tiers; Rajasthan was the first state to adopt Panchayati Raj (1959)
  • PAI 2.0 report released on this day (details in the PAI 2.0 card)
  • Over 2.5 lakh Panchayats; 24.04 lakh elected representatives, 49.75% women
  • Gram Sabha = general body of voters, the only permanent unit, not one of the three tiers
  • PESA Act 1996 covers Fifth Schedule areas of 10 states incl. Rajasthan (77,564 villages, 22,040 Panchayats, 664 blocks); Centre of Excellence at IGNTU Amarkantak; Odisha is the only state yet to notify PESA rules
  • Finance Commission grants to rural local bodies: 15th FC about ₹2.36 lakh cr → 16th FC (2026-31) about ₹4.35 lakh cr
  • Tools: SVAMITVA (24 April 2021; drone and CORS mapping, property cards); SabhaSaar (AI minutes, 23 languages, with Bhashini); eGramSwaraj (₹53,342 cr moved via PFMS in 2025-26)

52/70★ Must-learnNSO 80th round: health survey

In plain words

A large government survey asked households how much they use and pay for health care. It shows that free public services and health insurance have lowered costs for many families.

  • Household Social Consumption: Health; 1,39,732 households (76,296 rural, 63,436 urban)
  • Median OOPE per hospitalisation ₹11,285; public facility median ₹1,100; outpatient median in public facilities zero
  • Coverage by health schemes/insurance: rural 12.9% → 45.5%; urban 8.9% → 31.8%
  • Institutional deliveries: rural 90.5% (2017-18) → 95.6%; urban 96.1% → 97.8% (overall 96.2%); ante-natal care 98%; hospitalisation 2.9 per 100 persons
  • Out-of-pocket per hospitalisation: mean ₹34,064, median ₹11,285; public hospitals mean ₹6,631; childbirth ₹2,299 (public) vs ₹14,775 (all); survey period Jan-Dec 2025
  • Reporting ailments: rural 6.8% → 12.2%; urban 9.1% → 14.9%; rural outpatient in public facilities 28% (2014) → 35%
  • Support: 1.84 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs; AMRIT pharmacies 220+ (up to 50% off, 6,500+ drugs)

5/11★ Must-learnWTO 14th Ministerial Conference (MC14)

In plain words

The World Trade Organization held a major meeting of member countries to decide trade rules. India said which proposals it backed and which it refused to accept.

  • Yaounde, Cameroon; concluded 30 March 2026
  • India supported: consensus-based reform; fisheries subsidies draft (cited 61-day fishing ban); e-commerce work; TRIPS non-violation (NVSC) moratorium; technology transfer
  • India opposed: bringing Investment Facilitation for Development (IFD) into the WTO as an Annex 4 plurilateral agreement; premature new agriculture tracks; dilution of special and differential treatment; no consensus on e-commerce moratorium

Science and Technology

1/19★ Must-learnNational Quantum Mission: 1,000 km secure link

In plain words

Quantum technology can protect messages so that spying is nearly impossible. India showed a secure link over a long distance made with homegrown technology.

  • 1,000 km quantum communication network demonstrated using indigenous tech by QNu Labs (target 2,000 km in 8 years); startups supported rise to 17 (nine added)

2/19☆ Good to know3D glass chip packaging unit, Bhubaneswar

  • First in India: Heterogeneous Integration Packaging Solutions (3D Glass Solutions) at Info Valley; one of four semiconductor projects approved in Aug 2025 under India Semiconductor Mission

3/19★ Must-learnArtemis II and Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor

In plain words

A crewed spacecraft flew people around the Moon for the first time in decades. In India a new kind of nuclear power reactor was switched on for the first time.

  • Artemis II launched 1 April 2026 from Kennedy Space Center; first crewed Moon journey since 1972; return 10 April
    • Crew: Reid Wiseman (commander), Victor Glover, Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen (first non-American on a Moon mission)
  • PFBR, Kalpakkam (500 MWe; operator BHAVINI) attained criticality; India becomes second country after Russia with a commercial fast breeder reactor once operational
Exam angle

Which company runs the PFBR? (Bharatiya Nabhikiya Vidyut Nigam Ltd, BHAVINI)

4/19★ Must-learnSkyroot Vikram-1

In plain words

A private Indian company built a rocket meant to carry satellites into orbit. It shows that space work in India is no longer only done by the government.

  • India's first privately built orbital rocket; from Sriharikota; carries up to 350 kg to low Earth orbit; under IN-SPACe authorisation and ISRO oversight

  • SARAL AI (ANRF): research into social-media content in 18 languages; ANRF set up by ANRF Act 2023; MAHA = Mission for Advancement in High-Impact Areas
  • ISRO completed nationwide land-use mapping, integrated in Grammanchitra portal (Panchayati Raj)
  • ESA's Rosalind Franklin rover to launch on SpaceX Falcon Heavy in 2028; NASA's Roman Space Telescope fully assembled (about 1,000 times faster survey than Hubble)
  • IIT Ropar ANNAM.AI: Swan weather stations, Krishi call centres, Annam chat engine
  • WHO approved first infant malaria formulation (artemether-lumefantrine, babies under 5 kg); WHO flags high measles risk in Bangladesh

India is getting its first factory that makes computer chips, in a special economic zone in Gujarat. Rules were also changed so such factories can be built more easily.

9/19★ Must-learnIndia-Russia RELOS pact

In plain words

India and Russia agreed to let each other's armed forces use bases and ports for supplies and repairs. It makes joint operations and long voyages easier.

  • Reciprocal Exchange of Logistics Agreement: mutual access to bases, ports, airfields; up to 3,000 personnel each
  • Similar pact with the US: LEMOA (Logistics Exchange Memorandum of Agreement)

Schemes at a glance

1/11★ Must-learnSMILE: Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise

In plain words

This scheme helps transgender persons and people forced to beg to earn a living. It offers scholarships, skills training, shelter and health cover.

ItemDetail
Launched12 Feb 2022, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Target groupTransgender persons; persons engaged in begging
Outlay₹365 cr for 2021-22 to 2025-26 (₹265 cr transgender, ₹100 cr beggary)
Key featuresScholarships (Class IX to PG), PM-DAKSH skilling (stipend ₹1,000 a month at 80%+ attendance), Garima Greh shelters (21 working in 17 states), Ayushman Bharat TG Plus (₹5 lakh a year cashless cover incl. gender-affirming care)
Reach (March 2026)31,055 beggars identified, 9,935 rehabilitated; beggary sub-scheme in 181 cities
  • How the beggary sub-scheme works: survey and identify → mobilise and counsel → shelter and care → skill training and bank links → old-age homes or de-addiction where needed → follow-up
  • Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019: bars discrimination; offences up to 2 years; Rules 2020: Protection Cells (20 states/UTs), Welfare Boards (25); National Council for Transgender Persons; National Portal issues certificates
Remember

Aim: Bhiksha Vritti Mukt Bharat (begging-free India).

In plain words

Poshan is the government's mission to reduce hunger in mothers and children through better food and care. It joined several older schemes together and uses an app to track every centre.

ItemDetail
POSHAN AbhiyaanLaunched 8 March 2018; Ministry of Women and Child Development; 26+ ministries; focus on first 1,000 days
Poshan 2.0From Budget 2021-22: merges Anganwadi Services, Scheme for Adolescent Girls and POSHAN Abhiyaan (Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0)
Poshan TrackerLive since 1 March 2021; about 14.03 lakh Anganwadi centres, 8.95 crore beneficiaries; PM Award for Excellence in Public Administration 2024
Saksham Anganwadi2 lakh centres sanctioned for upgrade (LED screens, water purifiers, Poshan Vatikas)
FrameworksNavchetana (stimulation, 0-3 years) and Aadharshila (ECCE curriculum, 3-6 years), March 2024; PSE kit ₹3,000 per centre per year
  • Nutrition norms (Schedule II, National Food Security Act 2013) revised Jan 2023; helpline 1515 for POSHAN and PMMVY queries (from Nov 2025)
  • Home Visit Scheduler (April 2026, in Poshan Tracker): 23 home visits for pregnant women and children up to 3 years
  • 8th Poshan Pakhwada: 9-23 April 2026, theme "Maximizing Brain Development in the First Six Years"; Poshan Maah every September (8th launched 17 Sept 2025 at Dhar)

e-NAM is an online market where farmers can sell crops to buyers across states instead of only in their local market. It aims to give farmers a better price and a fairer deal.

ItemDetail
LaunchedApril 2016; app Oct 2016; Platform of Platforms 14 July 2022
Reach (March 2026)1,656 mandis in 23 states and 4 UTs; 1.80 crore farmers, 2.73 lakh traders, 4,724 FPOs
Trade13.25 crore MT worth ₹4.84 lakh crore since 2016 (₹3.19 lakh crore in 2024)

Growth, outlook and data releases

1/64★ Must-learnGDP First Advance Estimates FY2025-26 (Jan 2026)

In plain words

A first rough estimate of how much the economy grew this year, made before the year ends. It says India grew 7.4% in FY26, faster than 6.5% the year before.

  • Released by NSO (National Statistics Office, MoSPI) at constant (2011-12) and current prices
  • Real GDP growth FY26: 7.4% (FY25: 6.5%)
  • Real GDP ₹201.90 lakh crore; nominal GDP growth 8.0% → ₹357.14 lakh crore; real GVA growth 7.3% (₹184.50 lakh crore)
  • Sectors (real): finance, real estate and professional services + public administration 9.9%; trade, hotels, transport 7.5%; manufacturing and construction 7.0%; agriculture 3.1%; utilities 2.1%; GFCF 7.8% (7.1% earlier); PFCE 7.0%
Exam angle

What is the first advance estimate of real GDP growth for FY2025-26?

2/64★ Must-learnCPI inflation Dec 2025 and base-year revision

In plain words

CPI measures how fast consumer prices rise. December's 1.33% was the last reading on the old basket of goods; from January a new, wider basket (base year 2024) is used, with less weight on food.

  • Dec 2025 all-India CPI inflation: 1.33% (provisional), up 62 bps
  • Last release on old base (2012=100); new CPI series on base 2024=100 due 12 Feb 2026
  • Food & beverages weight in new CPI: 45.86% → 36.75%
  • New series: items 299 → 358; housing (incl. water, electricity, gas) weight 10.07% → 17.66%; first used for January 2026 data (released in Feb)
  • Timeline: Dec 2025 (old series) 1.33% → Jan 2026 (first on new series, base 2024) 2.75% → Feb 2026 3.21% (rural 3.37%, urban 3.02%, food 3.47%)
  • New GDP series (base 2022-23) due 27 Feb 2026; new IIP series (base 2022-23) due 28 May 2026
Exam angle

Which base year does the revised CPI series use, and what happens to the food weight?

Remember

Food weight falls 45.86% → 36.75% because consumption patterns have changed since 2011-12.

3/64★ Must-learnGrowth forecasts for India: UN, World Bank, IMF (Jan 2026)

In plain words

Three global bodies (UN, World Bank, IMF) each forecast India's growth for the coming years. Questions usually ask India's figure from one of them.

  • Table compares the three reports; India numbers are the exam targets
  • UN DESA: India grows 6.6% in 2026-27 and 6.8% in 2027-28; global inflation 3.4% (2025) → 3.1% (2026)

8/64★ Must-learnStartup India: 10 years and National Startup Awards 5.0

In plain words

Startup India turned 10, and the government celebrated with awards and state rankings. The number of recognised startups grew from under 500 in 2014 to over 2 lakh.

  • 16 Jan = National Startup Day; Startup India launched 2016. DPIIT-recognised startups above 2.07 lakh (under 500 in 2014); unicorns 4 → nearly 125; India = 3rd largest startup ecosystem
  • Maharashtra leads with 35,991 recognised startups; startups with at least one woman director: 99,640
  • States' Startup Ranking (SRF 5.0): Best Performers: Gujarat (Category A); Arunachal Pradesh and Goa (Category B). Top Performers include Karnataka, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, UP (A) and Himachal Pradesh (B)
  • Support schemes: Fund of Funds for Startups ₹10,000 crore (managed by SIDBI, invests via SEBI-registered AIFs); Seed Fund Scheme ₹945 crore; Atal Innovation Mission (NITI, 2016) ₹2,750 crore till Mar 2028; GENESIS (MeitY, 2022) ₹490 crore, 1,600 deep-tech startups
  • About 50% of startups from Tier II/III cities
Exam angle

Which state is the Best Performer (Category A) in the States' Startup Ranking 5.0?

9/64★ Must-learnDecember 2025 data snapshot: UPI, WPI, trade, PMI

  • UPI: 21.63 billion transactions (+29% y-o-y); value about ₹28 lakh crore (+20%)
  • WPI inflation Dec 2025: 0.83% (provisional)
  • Exports (goods + services) $74.01 bn (−1.01%); imports $80.94 bn (+6.17%); trade deficit $6.92 bn
  • January 2026: gross GST ₹1.93 trillion (+6.2%, import-led); UPI 21.70 bn transactions (+28%), ₹28.33 lakh crore (+21%)
  • HSBC PMI: manufacturing 55.0 (38-month low; Nov 56.6); services 58 (Nov 59.8). Above 50 = expansion
  • India has the world's 2nd-largest 5G subscriber base (400 million+) after China

  • Disinvestment and asset monetisation target ₹80,000 crore for FY27 (FY26 revised estimate ₹33,837 crore); IDBI Bank and LIC as big-ticket sources

11/64★ Must-learnPrice and output data: January 2026

In plain words

January's price and factory-output readings under the new CPI series, plus the new base year for trade statistics.

  • CPI (new series, base 2024) 2.75%; WPI 1.81% (base 2011-12; weights: primary articles 22.62%, fuel and power 13.15%, manufactured 64.23%)
  • Eight Core Industries index +4% (base 2011-12=100); growth in cement, steel, electricity, fertiliser, coal
  • DGCI&S moved base year of merchandise trade indices 2012-13 → 2022-23 (committee under Prof. Nachiketa Chattopadhyay, ISI)

12/64★ Must-learnNational Accounts base year revision (GDP new series)

In plain words

The government changed the base year (the reference year that all GDP is compared with) from 2011-12 to 2022-23. This makes GDP figures more up to date and also changes numbers like the fiscal deficit ratio.

  • MoSPI revising base year of national accounts to 2022-23; new series published 27 Feb 2026: nominal GDP ₹318.07 lakh crore (2024-25), ₹289.84 lakh crore (2023-24)
  • Fiscal deficit/GDP revised on new base: 2024-25 4.9% (was 4.8%), 2023-24 5.7% (5.63%), 2022-23 6.7% (6.4%)
  • Advisory Committee on National Account Statistics (ACNAS) chaired by Prof B N Goldar; 5 sub-committees (new data sources, methodology, constant price, regional accounts, SNA 2025 update)

Trade, FDI and tax

18/64★ Must-learnIndia–EU Free Trade Agreement concluded (26 Jan 2026)

In plain words

India and the European Union finished a free trade deal after nearly 20 years of talks. It lowers barriers on goods and services and opens parts of insurance and banking.

  • Talks launched 2007, relaunched 2022, concluded 26 Jan 2026; EU = India's 22nd FTA partner
  • EU banks allowed 15 branches over 4 years (earlier offer 12)
  • India binds FDI in insurance at 100%; EU eases visas for Indian professionals; AYUSH practitioners allowed
  • Trade: India–EU goods trade USD 136.53 bn (2024-25; exports 75.85, imports 60.68); EU is the largest goods partner; services trade ~USD 83 bn (2024)
  • EU FDI in India 2024: over €132 bn (leading investor)
  • Context: EU leaders Costa and von der Leyen were chief guests at the 77th Republic Day (26 Jan); 16th India–EU Summit on 27 Jan 2026 (15th was virtual, 15 Jul 2020); strategic partners since 2004
  • Mar 2026: India and EU grant each other MFN status for 5 years from FTA entry into force (review in 4th year; auto-terminates unless extended)
  • India–Euratom cooperation on peaceful nuclear energy agreed. Euratom = European Atomic Energy Community, set up by Treaty of Rome 1957
  • India's access: 97% of tariff lines (99.5% of trade value); India offers 92.1% of lines (97.5% of EU exports); social security agreements framework in 5 years; EU 144 services subsectors; India = 4th, EU = 2nd largest economies (25% of world GDP)
  • Financial services: banking FDI 74%, insurance 100%; EU offer excludes meat, dairy, honey, rice, sugar, tobacco; bilateral safeguard transition period 22 years; MFN in services active for 5 years; India banks in EU: SBI, BoB, BoI (5 branches)
Exam angle

Which number of FTA partner is the EU, and how many bank branches did India allow?

Remember

15 branches in 4 years (not 12). FTA partners earlier: Mauritius, UAE, UK, EFTA, Oman, Australia; New Zealand concluded 2025.

23/64★ Must-learnIncome Tax Rules 2026 (effective 1 Apr 2026)

In plain words

New income tax rules, in force from 1 April 2026, put the simplified Income-tax Act 2025 into practice, with changes like HRA in 8 cities and new PAN limits.

  • Biopharma SHAKTI: ₹10,000 crore over 5 years (biologics and biosimilars); 3 new + 7 upgraded NIPERs; 1,000+ accredited clinical-trial sites; target 5% of global biopharma market
  • ECMS (Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme; notified 8 Apr 2025): outlay ₹22,919 crore → ₹40,000 crore; target $500 bn electronics by 2030-31; electronics = 3rd largest export (2024-25)
  • India Semiconductor Mission 2.0: ₹1,000 crore for FY27; focus on equipment, materials, full-stack IP, 3 nm / 2 nm roadmap; ISM 1.0 (Dec 2021, ₹76,000 crore, up to 50% support): 10 projects, ₹1.60 lakh crore, 6 states
  • EPF tax: recognition only for funds exempted under Section 17, EPF Act 1952; 50% G-sec investment cap removed; employer contribution above ₹7.5 lakh taxed as perquisite
Exam angle

What is the ECMS outlay after Budget 2026-27?

53/64★ Must-learnUrban Challenge Fund (Cabinet, Feb 2026)

In plain words

A ₹1 lakh crore fund where the Centre pays 25% of a city project's cost, but at least half the money must come from the market (bonds, loans, private partners).

  • Central assistance ₹1 lakh crore = 25% of project cost; ≥50% must come from market (municipal bonds, loans, PPP); total ≈₹4 lakh crore investment
  • FY2025-26 to FY2030-31 (extendable to FY2033-34); projects by challenge mode; ₹5,000 crore corpus to improve creditworthiness of 4,223 cities
  • Credit Repayment Guarantee Scheme ₹5,000 crore for ULBs below 1 lakh population and NE/hill states: guarantee up to ₹7 crore or 70% (first loan), 50% (next)
Exam angle

What share of project cost does the Urban Challenge Fund cover?

54/64★ Must-learnBudget 2026-27 MSME and startup measures

In plain words

Budget 2026-27 steps for small businesses and startups: new funds, higher loan guarantees and mandatory use of TReDS (a platform for getting paid early on invoices).

  • SME Growth Fund ₹10,000 crore; Self-Reliant India (SRI) Fund +₹2,000 crore; TReDS mandatory for CPSE purchases from MSMEs; TReDS receivables as asset-backed securities; ₹7 lakh crore+ unlocked via TReDS
  • CGTMSE guarantee ceiling ₹5 crore → ₹10 crore; ₹10 lakh cap per consignment on courier exports removed; MSMEs = 31.1% of GDP, ~48.58% of exports
  • Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0: corpus ₹10,000 crore (FFS 1.0 launched 2016); focus deep tech and early-growth founders
  • National Manufacturing Mission: manufacturing 25% of GDP by 2035, 143 million jobs, $1.2 trn exports
Exam angle

What is the size of the SME Growth Fund?

55/64★ Must-learnNational Monetisation Pipeline 2.0 (NMP 2.0)

In plain words

The government plans to raise ₹16.72 lakh crore by leasing out existing public assets (roads, power lines, railways) to private players, called monetisation.

  • Launched by FM; developed by NITI Aayog; period FY26–FY30; target ₹16.72 lakh crore (2.6× NMP 1.0) from 12 sectors; private investment ₹5.8 lakh crore
  • Top sectors: highways, multimodal logistics parks and ropeways ₹4.42 lakh crore (26%); power ₹2.76 lakh crore; railways and ports ≈₹2.62 lakh crore each; tourism lowest
  • NMP 1.0 (2021, FY22–FY25): target ₹6 lakh crore, achieved ≈₹5.3 lakh crore (≈90%); monitored by Core Group of Secretaries on Asset Monetisation (Cabinet Secretary)
Exam angle

What is the target under NMP 2.0?

16.72 lakh crore vs 6 lakh crore of NMP 1.0.

57/64★ Must-learnBudget 2026-27: infrastructure finance and services exports

In plain words

Budget 2026-27 steps to attract money for infrastructure and to push India's services exports, including tax relief for foreign cloud firms.

  • Infrastructure Risk Guarantee Fund (partial guarantees to lenders); City Economic Regions (CERs): ₹5,000 crore per CER over 5 years, challenge mode; dedicated REITs for CPSE real estate; public capex ₹2 lakh crore (FY15) → ₹12.2 lakh crore BE 2026-27
  • Institutions: NIIF (2015; $4.9 bn AUM); NaBFID (2021; DFI); InvITs (SEBI 2014; first public InvIT planned 2026; ₹1.52 lakh crore monetised via ToT and private InvITs); IRFC (1986, railway financing arm)

What is the safe harbour margin for IT services proposed in Budget 2026-27?

58/64★ Must-learnCredit guarantee: CGSMFI-2.0 and MCGS-MSME changes (Mar 2026)

In plain words

Two guarantee schemes: one helps microfinance lenders lend to the poor, the other helps small businesses buy machinery without collateral.

  • CGSMFI-2.0 (Credit Guarantee Scheme for Microfinance Institutions): outlay ₹20,000 crore; 20 Mar – 30 Jun 2026; NCGTC covers default amount: 80% / 75% / 70% for small (AUM < ₹500 crore) / medium (₹500–2,000 crore) / large MFIs; loan cap 20% of AUM (₹100/200/300 crore); ≈36 lakh borrowers; tenure 3 years (1 year moratorium)
  • MCGS-MSME (launched Jan 2025): 60% cover up to ₹100 crore for machinery purchase; now includes services MSMEs; machinery share cut 75% → 60% of project cost; guarantee valid 10 years; exporters: ₹20 crore, 75% cover, 2% upfront (max ₹40 lakh), fee nil in year one then 0.5%
Exam angle

What guarantee cover applies to small MFIs under CGSMFI-2.0?

59/64★ Must-learnBudget 2026-27 ease-of-business and tax reforms

In plain words

Budget 2026-27 tax and customs changes that make doing business easier, such as a lower minimum alternate tax and higher foreign investor limits.

  • MAT treated as final tax, rate 15% → 14%; MAT credit set-off up to one-fourth of tax liability (new regime); buyback taxed as capital gains; non-residents under presumptive tax exempt from MAT
  • Individual PROIs (persons resident outside India) in listed equity via PIS: individual limit 5% → 10%, aggregate 10% → 24%; pre-deposit 20% → 10%; AEO Tier 2/3 duty deferral 15 → 30 days; customs advance ruling validity 3 → 5 years; Customs Integrated System in 2 years
  • Penalty immunity extended to misreporting; foreign-asset non-disclosure below ₹20 lakh immune (from 1 Oct 2024); Four Labour Codes consolidate 29 laws (thresholds 300 workers); SEZ one-time concessional DTA sales; 368 SEZs; SEZ exports ₹11.70 lakh crore (Apr–Dec 2025, +32.02%)
Exam angle

What is the revised MAT rate in Budget 2026-27?

60/64★ Must-learnGovernment borrowing plan, H1 FY2026-27

In plain words

How much the government will borrow in the first half of 2026-27 and how it will raise it (bonds of different tenors and short-term T-bills).

  • Gross market borrowing BE ₹17.20 lakh crore → ₹16.09 lakh crore after G-Sec switches
  • H1: ₹8.20 lakh crore (51.0%) via 26 weekly auctions; incl. ₹15,000 cr Sovereign Green Bonds (SGrBs)
  • Maturities: 3,5,7,10,15,30,40,50 yr; largest share 10-yr 29.0%; greenshoe up to ₹2,000 crore per security
  • Q1 T-Bills ₹24,000 cr/week-set for 12 weeks: 91-day ₹12,000 cr, 182-day ₹6,000 cr, 364-day ₹6,000 cr
  • RBI Ways and Means Advances (WMA) limit H1: ₹2.50 lakh crore

What is the WMA limit for H1 FY2026-27?

With shipping and insurance costs shooting up because of the West Asia war, the government is covering exporters' extra risk through ECGC.
